records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is invoking liberty-as-a-value (freedom from state interference with subjects) and arguing that exceptional legislation must meet a higher justificatory burden before infringing it—a standard claim about constraint on negative liberty.

records.speaker: MR. ACKERS
records.sentence: There was, however, so much in the Bill of a contentious character, and so much that would, in his opinion, make bad worse, that in giving his support to the second reading of the Bill, he must expressly reserve to himself the liberty to oppose some of the clauses.

records.speaker: THE EARL OF CAMPERDOWN
records.sentence: The Bill, as it stood, proposed that the period during which Electric Lighting Companies should enjoy the fruits of their enterprise should be extended from 21 to 42 years, and, in addition, it was provided that at the expiration of that period any Local Authority was to be at liberty to purchase the undertaking upon the terms of paying the then market value of the goodwill of the undertaking.
records.haiku_rationale: Local authorities are empowered (granted capacity) to purchase electric lighting undertakings at market value after the concession period expires—an enabling grant of discretionary power to act.

records.speaker: MR. ILLINGWORTH  (Bradford, W.)
records.sentence: We are asked to alter the Rules of Procedure and further curtail the rights of debate in order that, when a subsequent measure is presented to us, the ancient freedom of debate which has existed in this House may no longer exist.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "ancient freedom of debate" as a value being threatened by proposed procedural changes that would curtail "rights of debate" — this is negative liberty, freedom from interference with Parliamentary debate.

records.speaker: THE PRIME MINISTER AND SECRETARY OF STATE FOR FOREIGN AFFAIRS (The Marquess of SALISBURY)
records.sentence: If the Town Council of Dover had come to their Lordships to claim liberty to fill Dover Harbour up and shut it up until such time as it should be convenient for them to open it themselves, then they would have been in exactly the position of the Local Authorities now, who wished to stifle all electric lighting enterprize until they saw their way to undertake it themselves.
records.haiku_rationale: The claim is that Local Authorities sought liberty (empowerment/capacity) to undertake electric lighting enterprise themselves—they wanted to be free to compete and provide the service, not merely to escape interference.

records.speaker: SIR EDWARD REED  (Cardiff)
records.sentence: Members who make any kind of fight on behalf of the general freedom of the House in this time of trial.
records.haiku_rationale: Members are being freed to fight on behalf of general freedom of the House against constraints/restrictions being imposed during a time of trial; the object is freedom of the House (the assembly's institutional independence and prerogatives).

records.speaker: MR. CRILLY  (Mayo, N.)
records.sentence: but they had not broken the spirit of the Irish people—they had not quenched their desire to have legislative freedom, nor shaken their purpose to have sitting in Ireland a Parliament which, though subservient to the Imperial Parliament in all Imperial matters, should have authority to legislate for the wants and requirements of the Irish people.
records.haiku_rationale: Irish people's desire to have legislative freedom—a Parliament empowered to legislate for Ireland's own domestic wants—is a capacity to self-govern rather than freedom from interference.

records.speaker: MR. CONYBEARE  (Cornwall, Camborne)
records.sentence: When we are told, in those eloquent tones and strains which are familiar to us from Court circles, that we ought to be blessing Providence for the amount of prosperity and liberty and that sort of thing which has resulted to us from 50 years of the present reign, I would venture to ask—and I think it is a question which deserves an answer—who it is we have to thank for all the prosperity which has come to this nation in the course of the last half-century?
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "liberty" as a vague blessing resulting from the present reign (1833-1883), but does not specify what liberty means—neither freedom from what interference nor capacity to do what. The reference is rhetorical and non-specific.

records.speaker: MR. DILLON
records.sentence: For that reason they are determined to destroy us, because they hope and believe that in our ruin would be involved the ruin of the cause of Irish freedom and Irish nationality, and of the suffering people whom we represent in this House.
records.haiku_rationale: Irish freedom and Irish nationality are being freed from domination/destruction by their opponents; this is a rhetorical invocation of freedom as a cause opposed to ruin and oppression, expressing negative liberty (freedom from foreign interference).

records.speaker: MR. LAWSON  (St. Pancras, W.)
records.sentence:
Forster said—
 "If the people who wanted to go to the museums and picture galleries liked to take a railway ticket to Hampton Court they found they were at liberty to look at the pictures there, but they could not look at the pictures close by their own doors—it might be at Bethnal Green.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "at liberty to look at the pictures" is parliamentary procedural language indicating permission or allowance to engage in an action; it does not substantively invoke liberty as a value being claimed or constrained, and the broader point concerns access to museums rather than a philosophical claim about freedom from or capacity for something.

records.speaker: *MR. CHAPLIN
records.sentence: " The modern Radical, I observe, always professes to love liberty;

records.speaker: *THE ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
records.sentence: Seeing, therefore, that after his imprisonment this clergyman would be at liberty to return to his parish, and thus become a centre of contamination, I was obliged to resort to the device which I will state to your Lordships.

records.speaker: THE MARQUESS OF SALISBURY

records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "at liberty to tender their allegiance" is a procedural parliamentary expression meaning "permitted to" or "allowed to," not a substantive claim about liberty as a value being defended or threatened.

records.speaker: *MR. P. O'BRIEN
records.sentence: Let him have liberty, on condition of emigration if you will.

records.speaker: MR. T. M. HEALY
records.sentence: But here in this case the counsel for the prisoner, a Member of this House, desiring to see his client on a matter concerning the justice of his sentence and his liberty, after travelling some 300 or 400 miles, is denied the right conceded readily to the subordinate of the  Times  on a matter of far less importance.

records.sentence: Gentleman will be content with the general expression of the sympathy of the Government with the views he has expressed, and that he will not ask this House, or any House which may succeed it, to limit the reasonable freedom accorded to the Minister in charge of the House, which would inflict great inconvenience without any adequate and commensurate advantage to private Members.

records.speaker: MR. DAVITT
records.sentence: The fight which is being fought against this Bill was waged by the same class, by similar threats, by the same predictions, against every other reform which demanded religious freedom and social security for the people of Ireland.

records.speaker: MR. J. CHAMBERLAIN  (Birmingham, W.)
records.sentence: If this matter is to be treated with dryness because it is a proposal for limiting freedom of discussion in a Parliament which has yet to be created, then I would only say in passing how much more dry must be the treatment of any proposal to limit discussion in a Parliament which already exists.

records.speaker: MR. W. E. GLADSTONE
records.sentence: Friend, who is admittedly within his liberty as a Member of this House without In-each of Order, appears to me to be a proceeding, the adoption of which would result in all effective and practical discussion upon all Bills whatever being rendered impossible.

records.speaker: MR. DILLWYN  (Swansea, Town)
records.sentence: But whether they de, dare themselves in favour of it or not, let a poll be taken, and I have no doubt that the result will be in favour of freedom of religion and the support of that Church which they have so well established for themselves in Wales.

records.speaker: MR. DANE  (Fermanagh, N.)
records.sentence: and what steps the Irish Government have taken to ensure freedom of contract and protection for the law-abiding residents in the Rochfort Bridge District and the district of Medina adjoining?

records.speaker: SIR E. GREY
records.sentence: The Chancellor of the Exchequer already receives a considerable amount in the form of conscience money, and I think that Members of Parliament who feel that the salary is in excess of their merits, or have scruples about receiving any salary at all, will be at liberty to copy the anonymous donors of unpaid income tax.
records.haiku_rationale: Members of Parliament would be free from interference in choosing whether to donate their salary (or not), expressed through the phrase "at liberty to copy" — a negative liberty (freedom from constraint on their choice).

records.speaker: MR. JOSEPH CHAMBERLAIN
records.sentence: I believe that if this Bill were passed they would make a good use of it—that they would rejoice in the new liberty that would be conferred upon them;

records.speaker: MR. WILLIAM REDMOND  (Fermanagh, N.)

records.haiku_rationale: Religious liberty for all denominations is freedom from interference with religious practice and belief—a classic negative liberty.

If I were to stand upon the footing analogous

records.sentence: Seeing the position in which religion is thus placed, they yield to its teachings, and there is instilled into the minds of the people of this country as generation after generation grow up obedience to the teachings of religion obedience to law and to authority which, in my judgment, is a most valuable makeweight in the minds of a free and a freedom-loving people.

records.speaker: MR. ROSS
records.sentence: The Welsh supporters of Disestablishment did not care a straw for Home Rule, but they were appealed to for assistance in sacrificing the liberty of free citizens in Ireland.
records.haiku_rationale: Citizens in Ireland are being freed from (or prevented from sacrificing) interference with their civic independence and self-governance—the speaker opposes a measure that would strip Irish citizens of their existing liberty.

records.speaker: *THE UNDER SECRETARY OF STATE FOR THE HOME DEPARTMENT (Mr. GEORGE RUSSELL, North Beds)
records.sentence: I am persuaded that it would be a proud and happy day for the Church when, in reply to the just boast of the Nonconformist Communions that they were "free born," she is able to say, "With a great sum obtained I this freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The Church has obtained freedom (likely freedom from state establishment or constraint) through a great financial sum, contrasting it with the inherited "free born" status of Nonconformists; this refers to freedom from legal/religious impediment.

records.speaker: *MR. BRYCE
records.sentence: He had not even differed from the views expressed by his distinguished brother the Protestant Archbishop of Dublin as to the positive strength which that Church had in some respects gained by her freedom from State connection.
records.haiku_rationale: The Church gains strength from freedom from State connection — freedom from interference/constraint by the State in ecclesiastical matters.

records.speaker: MR. GOSCHEN
records.sentence: It is said: "We require freedom in order to succeed.
records.haiku_rationale: This sentence is ambiguous: "freedom in order to succeed" could mean either freedom from interference (negative liberty—freedom from obstacles to success) or freedom as empowerment/capacity to act (positive liberty—the ability/opportunity to pursue success); the sentence does not specify from what or to what one is freed.

records.speaker: MR. A. MORLEY
records.sentence: : Clause 7 of the Order in Council, 1890, provides a maximum limit for leave beyond which Heads of Departments are not at liberty to go.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "not at liberty to go" refers to a procedural constraint on departmental authority to grant leave beyond a specified limit; this is parliamentary procedure language indicating administrative restriction rather than a substantive claim about freedom-as-a-value.

records.speaker: THE EARL OF DUNRAVEN
records.sentence:
" 
It was rather curious to reflect that in looking to liberty in this matter they had to turn from the British Parliament to the Romish Church.
records.haiku_rationale: The object of freedom is "liberty in this matter"—the specific content is not detailed in the sentence, but the speaker contrasts where liberty can be found (the Romish Church) versus where it cannot (British Parliament), treating liberty as a capacity or state of non-interference to be secured.

records.speaker: EARL WEMYSS
records.sentence: Liberty that gave the real charm to life.
records.haiku_rationale: Liberty is invoked as an abstract value that enhances life's quality, without specifying what is being freed from or to what—a rhetorical invocation of liberty as a positive ideal and cause.

records.speaker: THE MARQUESS OF SALISBURY
records.sentence: You are treating very lightly the liberty of the subject, and I hope the three first clauses of the Bill will not, at least in their present form, ever appear on the Statute Book.
records.haiku_rationale: The "liberty of the subject" is the freedom from governmental interference with personal status or rights; the speaker opposes clauses that would curtail this negative liberty.

records.speaker: MR. DUNBAR BARTON  (Armagh, Mid.)
records.sentence:
but the Chief Secretary had said—
 "I have never denied that in emergency, as, for instance, in the year 1867, it might become necessary for the Government to suspend the guarantees of liberty and equality.
records.haiku_rationale: The Government's power to suspend "guarantees of liberty and equality" in emergency—the freedom being referenced is freedom from suspension of these guarantees, i.e., protection from arbitrary governmental interference with fundamental rights.

records.speaker: *MR. CHAPLIN
records.sentence: and wherever that was the case they might be quite certain that that freedom was granted already.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom (unspecified what freedom) that has already been granted to someone; without knowing what specific freedom or what it concerns, this remains under-determined between enabling capacity and non-interference.

records.speaker: *MR. CHANNING
records.sentence: The proposal to give freedom of cropping and sale of produce had been sharply criticised, and a great deal had been made of protecting the landlords against the deterioration of the land, but he would point out that the Bill gave protection, because it insisted that there should be provision made against the deterioration of the soil.
records.haiku_rationale: The tenant is being freed from restrictions on cropping and sale of produce—enabling capacity to make economic decisions about their land without landlord interference; this is capacity to act (positive liberty).

records.speaker: THE DUKE OF DEVONSHIRE
records.sentence: We know the difficulties in which the Government are placed, partly in consequence of the conduct of some of their allies, and partly in consequence of the conduct of some of their own Members when they were in a position of greater freedom and less responsibility.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom refers to a position of less responsibility and greater scope for action, contrasted with the constraints of current governmental accountability—a capacity to act with fewer obligations.

records.speaker: COLONEL SAUNDERSON
records.sentence: and he, as an Irishman, declared that it was in the interests of the freedom and peace of his country that this Act should remain in force, and that it should be in the power of any Government to put its provisions, when the necessity arose into operation.
records.haiku_rationale: The freedom being invoked is national/governmental freedom to exercise executive power in an emergency ("in the power of any Government to put its provisions... into operation"), which is an empowerment or capacity granted to the state.

records.speaker: MR. GOSCHEN
records.sentence: No layman or clergyman has asked for greater freedom;
records.haiku_rationale: No layman or clergyman has asked for greater freedom from interference or constraint; the sentence invokes liberty as a value opposed to restriction.

records.speaker: MR. R. WALLACE  (Edinburgh, E.)
records.sentence: The Members of the legislative body would know that their constituents would have the power of rectifying any legislative error that they might make and, therefore, there would be greater freedom in their legislation.
records.haiku_rationale: Legislators would have greater freedom to legislate without fear of unaccountable error, because constituents retain power to rectify mistakes—freedom from the constraint of excessive accountability or hesitation.

records.speaker: THE DUKE OF ARGYLL
records.sentence: It is a Bill which undoubtedly affects the liberty of a great many persons, containing more than 50 clauses, and we are passing it on the faith of others, except so far as we have been able to read the Bill during the few hours it has been in our possession.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence refers to a Bill that "affects the liberty" of persons without specifying whether the effect constrains their freedom from interference or enables their capacity to act; the context suggests constraint/impact on liberty but the specific direction (freedom from what, or freedom to do what) is not specified in this sentence alone.

records.speaker: *MR. ARNOLD MORLEY
records.sentence: , and Mears, who was a warehouseman, stated that he regarded the use of his name as an unwarrantable liberty, and objected to its being brought into the controversy.
records.haiku_rationale: Mears objected to having his name used in a controversy; "took the liberty" is parliamentary procedure meaning someone acted without authorization or propriety.

records.speaker: *THE UNDER SECRETARY OF STATE FOR THE HOME DEPARTMENT (Mr. GEORGE RUSSELL, North Beds)
records.sentence: " Yes, Sir, in that one word "freedom" lies the whole of our contention in this matter as it presents itself to members of the Established Church.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "freedom" as a central value in a Church establishment dispute, opposing the Established Church's interest against some constraint or competing position; the object of freedom is under-specified beyond the single word "freedom" itself.

records.speaker: THE MARQUESS OF SALISBURY
records.sentence: We have no such liberty of delay.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker asserts that they lack freedom (capacity) to delay action, meaning they are constrained and unable to exercise the power to postpone — this invokes a lack of enabling capacity rather than interference with a named freedom.

records.speaker: THE FIRST LORD OF THE TREASURY
records.sentence: Of this I can assure him, that the Powers who have taken in hand the task of providing for the freedom of Crete will not be bound by the views of anybody but themselves.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of Crete — capacity for Crete to govern itself, freed from foreign/Ottoman rule; the Powers are being granted liberty to determine their own course of action regarding enabling Crete's independence.

records.speaker: MR. E. ROBERTSON
records.sentence: He was not at liberty to discuss the general policy of the Government, but following the observations which had been made by the hon.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker was not at liberty to discuss government policy—this is a procedural/parliamentary constraint on what topics he could address, not a substantive claim about liberty as a value.

records.speaker: MR. THOMAS BAYLEY  (Derbyshire, Chesterfield)
records.sentence: Hardinge referred to the grounds upon which slaves were now freed by the Sultan and by himself, plainly showing that he had the power of giving or withholding freedom, and that in fact he administered a law which acknowledged the legal status of slavery.
records.haiku_rationale: Slaves are being freed (given freedom) by the Sultan and Hardinge; the freedom here is from enslavement/bondage—a removal of subjection—which is a classic negative liberty.

records.speaker: MR. H. H. ASQUITH  (Fife, E.)
records.haiku_rationale: The House of Commons is being freed from constraint—the Act would deprive it of its "absolute freedom" to decide unilaterally how tax revenue is spent, meaning the Act removes the House's freedom FROM interference or restriction by other bodies in exercising this constitutional power.

records.speaker: SIR JOHN BRUNNER  (Cheshire, Northwich)
records.sentence: It was a very common argument on the other side that they ought to have freedom of choice in order that children might be brought up in the religion to which they and their parents were attached.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence discusses freedom to choose a child's religious upbringing—an empowered capacity to act (select one's preferred religion) rather than freedom from interference, making this a positive liberty claim.

records.speaker: LORD BALFOUR
records.sentence: The Question was a hypothetical one, and he did not feel himself at liberty to give a definite answer with regard to what might be done in the event of certain things occurring which had not actually taken place.
records.haiku_rationale: Lord Balfour uses "at liberty to give a definite answer" as a parliamentary procedural phrase meaning he is not permitted or willing to respond to a hypothetical question; this is not a substantive claim about freedom-as-a-value but rather a conventional expression about his position in debate.

records.speaker: MR. E. H. PICKERSGILL  (Bethnal Green, S. W.)
records.sentence: Now, as to the power of the tribunal and its freedom from restrictions.
records.haiku_rationale: A tribunal's capacity or empowerment to act without constraints; freedom to exercise authority and make decisions without procedural or legal restrictions imposed upon it.

records.speaker: LORD NORTON
records.sentence: The mixture of the two damaged both, and neither got the freedom it needed.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence refers to freedom as a capacity or condition that each entity "needed"—the freedom required to function properly without damage from the admixture. This points to freedom as an empowered state or self-sufficiency rather than mere non-interference.

records.speaker: COLONEL HUGH McCALMONT  (Antrim, N.)
records.sentence: that is the home of freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: This is a bare invocation of "freedom" as a rhetorical ideal associated with a place ("home"), without specifying what is being freed or from-or-to what.

records.speaker: CAPTAIN NORTON
records.sentence: He knew of several cases where men who were highly desirable as cavalry officers had left of their own free will simply because they objected to interference with their personal liberty and personal habits.
records.haiku_rationale: Men objected to interference with their personal liberty and habits — freedom FROM interference with how they conduct their personal lives.

records.speaker: THE PRIME MINISTER (The MARQUESS of SALISBURY)
records.sentence: but I wish to reserve full liberty to the Government at a somewhat later period to enter on an investigation of that kind if in its judgment the public interest can be served by it.
records.haiku_rationale: The Prime Minister is reserving the Government's capacity to conduct an investigation in the future if deemed in the public interest—an empowerment or authorization to act, not freedom from interference.

records.speaker: MR. HANBURY
records.sentence: : In those cases, where allowances are granted for aid head postmasters are at liberty to employ their own assistants, but they are required to furnish annually a statement, which they have to certify as correct, showing as regards such assistants their names, length of service, number of hours of daily attendance, the amount paid to them in cash, and the estimated value of their board and lodging in cases where the assistants live on the post office premises.
records.haiku_rationale: Head postmasters are permitted to employ their own assistants without interference, a procedural freedom regarding employment decisions.

records.speaker: THE PRIME MINISTER (The MARQUESS of SALISBURY)
records.sentence: I have only to answer that, as at present advised, the Government do not see their way to the appointment of such a body, but they reserve to themselves the liberty of agreeing to such an appointment at a later period if they think it desirable.
records.haiku_rationale: The Government reserves to itself the liberty (capacity/power) to agree to an appointment at a later period — this is empowerment to act, a discretionary authority to decide whether to appoint a body in future.

records.speaker: LORD WARKWORTH  (Kensington, S.)
records.sentence: For if it was the liberty of the individual to work or not work as he pleased that was at stake, there was no longer any justification for the interference by the State with Sunday traffic of any kind provided that it was voluntarily engaged in.
records.haiku_rationale: What is being freed: the individual's choice whether to work or not work. From what: state interference with Sunday traffic. This is freedom from state constraint on voluntary action—a core negative liberty concern.

records.speaker: SIR WILFRID LAWSON
records.sentence: : As regards the freedom of the district from crime, is it not the fact that there are no public-houses in the district?
records.haiku_rationale: The district being freed from crime (a harm/social evil), achieved through absence of public-houses—a condition of security and safety.

records.speaker: *MR. CARVELL WILLIAMS (Notts,  Mansfield )
records.haiku_rationale: The Church is being empowered to manage its own affairs without external interference—an enabling capacity to govern itself.

records.speaker: MR. T. M. HEALY  (Louth, N.)
records.sentence: They had a splendid record during the present year, and perhaps it was just as well that the Chief Secretary was left out and was in a position of greater freedom and less responsibility in his conduct and management of Irish affairs.
records.haiku_rationale: The Chief Secretary is freed from governmental responsibility and oversight in managing Irish affairs, enabling greater discretionary capacity to act.

records.speaker: *SIR W. HARCOURT
records.sentence: ] Her safety is the precious hope of all that are desolate and oppressed, and we may devoutly pray that she will long endure to hand on, like the torch-bearers of her classic age, the lamp of freedom which her valour has kindled, and which her wisdom may long keep alive.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "the lamp of freedom" as a cause or heritage handed down by a political leader (implied to be Britain or its monarch), opposed to oppression and desolation. This is a rhetorical invocation of liberty as freedom from oppression and tyranny, characteristic of negative liberty discourse.

records.speaker: MR. ROBERT YERBURGH (  Chester )
records.sentence:
He had read a very interesting speech by the Duke of Devonshire on the position of the Volunteers, in which he laid great stress on their value for home defence, and he said no opportunity should be lost of so defending a vital point as to give the Fleet liberty of action and that freedom which was

essential for its proper use.

records.sentence: At the same time they wanted to have a little more freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The actors want increased capacity or opportunity to act without unspecified constraint; they desire greater room for discretion or choice (positive liberty).

records.speaker: LORD BRAYE
records.sentence: It would be hard to number the motives which must suggest themselves both to the national and to the Imperial mind for the keeping of the jubilee with honour worthy—they surely must be without number, yet the chief of all must be the sense of gratitude for a co-existence of religious and political liberty unknown outside our Empire.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "religious and political liberty" as a distinctive achievement worthy of celebration and gratitude—what is being freed is the capacity for religious belief and political participation, understood as goods existing uniquely under British imperial governance rather than elsewhere. This is negative liberty: freedom from interference with religious practice and political activity.

records.speaker: THE EARL OF DUNRAVEN
records.sentence: Communities of Englishmen in the broader sense, great communities enjoying perfect legislative freedom in these respects.
records.haiku_rationale: Great communities are freed to exercise legislative autonomy (freedom TO make laws themselves), an empowerment to govern themselves rather than freedom from interference with a pre-existing activity.

records.speaker: THE ATTORNEY GENERAL
records.sentence: It was but fair that the tribunal should be at liberty to say to the workmen, "You can be heard on this point or on that point because you are interested in it, but we cannot allow you to be heard on points in which you have no interest.
records.haiku_rationale: The tribunal is being empowered to exercise discretionary authority—to decide which points workmen may present—making this about institutional capacity to govern a proceeding.

records.speaker: MR. BRODRICK
records.sentence: "] By this means alone can, the field army be given absolute freedom of movement, and have the security that a light column striking at London from some other point of the coast will meet with determined resistance.
records.haiku_rationale: The field army is being freed (given the capacity) to move about without constraint, enabling tactical mobility and strategic action in defense.

records.speaker: MR. T. M. HEALY
records.sentence: Why did not that attorney, when he knew that the action was threatened, say to the Court, "It was my mistake," and apply to the Court for liberty notwithstanding to make proof of the improvements?
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker asks why the attorney did not apply to the Court for liberty (permission/leave) to make proof despite a procedural default—"at liberty to speak" / "took the liberty of" is parliamentary/legal procedure language where "liberty" means formal permission or technical leave, not a claim about freedom-as-a-value.

records.speaker: SIR ROBERT REID  (Dumfries Burghs)
records.sentence: These kinsmen of theirs had for the last 70 years been striving for freedom in various ways.
records.haiku_rationale: Kinsmen striving for freedom over 70 years in various ways—a general invocation of freedom as a cause/value against constraint or subjugation, without specifying the particular object of freedom (from what oppression, to what end).

records.speaker: MR. JOHN REDMOND  (Waterford)
records.sentence: He, at any rate, as a Nationalist, would have this consolation—that by their action they would have torn to shreds the last rag of argument in favour of the maintenance of the Union, and they would have hastened the day when Ireland would find in a national Government of her own, not only political freedom, but her best safeguard against further spoliation.
records.haiku_rationale: Ireland gains freedom through (or via) her own national Government—the object is Irish political autonomy/self-governance empowered rather than merely freed from interference.

records.speaker: *MR. SAMUEL SMITH  (Flintshire)
records.sentence: it arose before the growth of human liberty, before the individual man was conceived of as having rights of his own, and when he was merged in the society or state to which he belonged.
records.haiku_rationale: The individual man is being freed from merged/subsumed status in the collective (society/state) so as to possess and exercise his own rights—this is positive liberty, the empowerment to act as an autonomous agent with recognized personal rights.

records.speaker: MR. HUBERT DUNCOMBE  (Cumberland, Egremont)
records.sentence: He would take the liberty of reminding hon.
records.haiku_rationale: This is a parliamentary procedure phrase where "took the liberty of" means "permitted myself to" or "ventured to"; it is not making a substantive claim about liberty as a value or freedom from interference.

records.speaker: *THE SECRETARY OF STATE FOR THE HOME DEPARTMENT (Sir M. W. RIDLEY,  Lancashire, N., Blackpool )
records.sentence: I do not think this House would be disposed to do otherwise than safeguard in a more rigid manner the liberty of the subject.
records.haiku_rationale: The liberty of the subject is to be safeguarded in a rigid manner—freedom from interference or encroachment on the subject's rights and personal status.

records.speaker: MR. ASQUITH
records.sentence: "] But, while I entirely agree with the Government in regard to that paragraph, I ask the apostles of contracting out on the Benches opposite, those who in 1894 defeated our Bill because we would not permit contracting out—[ cheers ]—those who at the last General Election went to their constituents and declared that they were the champions of freedom of contract—[ laughter ]—against the predatory and socialistic legislation of a Radical Government—I ask how we stand to-night?
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "freedom of contract" as a political slogan that the Opposition used to oppose legislation restricting contracting-out rights; this is freedom FROM government interference with the ability to make contracts.

records.speaker: *SIR A. K. ROLLIT  (Islington, S.)
records.sentence:
Gentleman the Member for West Monmouth, who, speaking as the head of the Government, said—
 "These servants have perfect freedom to combine, and to have all the advantages and privileges of trades unions.
records.haiku_rationale: Servants are freed to combine and participate in trades unions—the freedom being discussed is freedom from legal prohibition to associate collectively, a classic negative liberty.

records.speaker: *MR. JOHN ELLIS  (Notts, Rushcliffe)
records.sentence: and, therefore, speaking merely as a Member of the House, he felt at liberty to say that in the circumstances, he was inclined to think that the House would he wasting its time by proceeding further with the Measure.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "at liberty to say" is a parliamentary idiom meaning the speaker is permitted or enabled to speak; this is a procedural formality, not a substantive claim about liberty as a political value.

records.speaker: MR. BAYLEY
records.sentence: : Do we understand that there is a Court at Pemba, which can give a man his freedom?

records.speaker: *MR. CURZON
records.sentence: It means that every slave is at liberty to go before a court established for that purpose, and to claim his freedom.

records.speaker: MR. M'CARTAN
records.sentence: and whether it is under Statute or by a rule of the Home Office the governor of the prison is authorised to give the prisoner liberty to attend the inquest?
records.haiku_rationale: The governor is authorised to give the prisoner liberty (freedom/permission) to attend the inquest—empowering or enabling the prisoner to do an action.

records.speaker: *MR. J. A. PEASE  (Northumberland, Tyneside)
records.sentence: One was the giving slaves the right to purchase their freedom, and the other telling the Arab masters that they must not ill-treat their slaves.
records.haiku_rationale: Slaves are freed to the capacity of purchasing their own freedom (positive liberty—empowerment to act), and slaves are freed from ill-treatment by masters (negative liberty—freedom from interference).

records.speaker: *THE EARL OF WEMYSS
records.sentence: At any rate, his noble Friend ought to be pleased with a sermon the text of which was the noble Marquess's own dictum, that "Liberty is the noblest idol before which any man could bow.

records.sentence:
It abolishes the schedule of rules under which all prisoners are treated alike, and gives us a set of rules under which, for the first time, a Secretary of State will have considerable lati

tude and considerable freedom.

records.speaker: MR. THOMAS ELLIS
records.sentence: But he ventured to say that a great deal of the freedom, independence, and usefulness of hundreds of parochial clergymen in this country—especially of those who had conspicuously added to the piety, scholarship, and dignity of the clerical profession, was due to the fact that they had not to rely on the favour of the Bishop, but that they relied on the views of enlightened layman, and upon the patronage of colleges and other public institutions of the country.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from dependence on episcopal favour; clergymen are freed from interference/control by the Bishop and instead rely on independent sources (enlightened laymen, colleges, public institutions).

 125 
goods.

records.sentence: If the tiller of the soil has no resource in his own country excepting agriculture, well, of course, he must necessarily be at the mercy of the landlord: you have unlimited competition and no freedom of contract.

records.speaker: MR. HALDANE  (Haddington)
records.sentence:
It is because that desire is in their minds to-day that I

distinguish the Home Rule feeling of the Irish people from this Motion to-day, and I express my conviction that, however long we may have to wait, you will only solve that problem in the same manner as you solved the question of Canada and the question of Quebec, by giving them full freedom, and recognising their right in their existence as a people to be free.

records.speaker: MR. DILLON
records.sentence: I think the elector ought to have absolute freedom as to their selection and of placing upon the council that man who, in their opinion, is most fit to represent them, and who, in their judgment, will do their business best;

records.speaker: *MR. CURZON

records.sentence: ] If the true principle of the British Constitution was to develop individual liberty and to give everyone as much liberty as possible, British rule in India had accomplished that result to a most remarkable extent.

records.sentence: whether, on the petitioner's appeal for protection, liberty, redress, and restoration of her property, the Governor of Lagos has declined to interfere;

records.sentence: and whether by such a paragraph the freedom of the Legislature of the Colony to accept or reject such legislation is compromised?

records.sentence: Surely it is incumbent upon you to do all you can to give them such liberty as is consistent with the present condition of things, the liberty to make the best of their conditions.

records.haiku_rationale: The speaker offers a "boon of freedom" (presumably from some constraint or obligation) and threatens to "pin you down" (constrain you further) if rejected—the object of freedom is not clearly specified, but the rhetorical structure invokes liberty as relief from a binding position.

records.speaker: MR. HALDANE
records.sentence: I would therefore suggest to the right honourable Gentleman and the House that the situation could be met, not by striking out those words, but by introducing words such as I have suggested into the clause as it stands, which would leave the right honourable Gentleman freedom, but which would indicate to his successors in office the policy which he himself intends to adopt, and which I believe it is the sense of the House he should adopt, in connection with the administration of our prisons.
records.haiku_rationale: A government official (the right honourable Gentleman) is being granted discretionary freedom from legislative constraint in administering prisons—a capacity to choose policy within his office, free from restrictive statutory language.

records.speaker: *SIR LEWIS McIVER
records.sentence: At all events, I am at liberty to say that Wano is in the heart of the southern portion of Waziristan with which I am dealing.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "at liberty to say" is a parliamentary procedural expression meaning the speaker is permitted to make a statement; it does not advance a substantive claim about liberty-as-a-value.

records.speaker: *MR. CURZON
records.sentence: He concluded with a general charge against the Arab officials, to the effect that they had never come to understand the first principles of justice, and had not the slightest desire to see justice done or freedom given;
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom given to Arab officials — positive liberty, an enabling capacity or empowerment, contrasted with "justice done" as goods to be granted to them.

records.speaker: *THE BISHOP OF SALISBURY
records.sentence: Therefore, it is advisable that there should be no mistake in the beginning of such a connection, and there ought to be full liberty given to everyone who knows of any just cause or impediment against an institution to report it to the bishop, and to insist that the bishop should consider it.
records.haiku_rationale: Full liberty given to individuals to report impediments and insist the bishop consider them—capacity to act/participate in institutional oversight

records.speaker: MR. MACNEILL
records.sentence: but what he thinks is good enough to convince the House of Commons that these men ought not to have their liberty, would not secure a conviction before the commonest of common juries in this country, or even in Ireland, where justice is dependent on the Government, and where the administrators of it do their work with their eyes on the Treasury Bench.
records.haiku_rationale: Men are being deprived of liberty (their freedom from detention/constraint) based on evidence that would not meet normal legal standards in a jury trial.

records.speaker: THE PRIME MINISTER AND SECRETARY OP STATE FOR FOREIGN AFFAIRS (The Marquess of SALISBURY)
records.sentence: If you come to examine it in detail, I do not see how the liberty to make a railway and to run a railway can give to any foreign country a political power over China.
records.haiku_rationale: The liberty in question is the freedom to construct and operate a railway—a capacity to undertake commercial activity. The claim is that this capability does not transfer political power, so the freedom being discussed is freedom TO act (to make and run a railway), not freedom FROM interference.

records.speaker: *MR. BRODRICK
records.sentence: Banker that he was at liberty to pursue his business, but that, in the event of the two Governments subsequently deciding that the area of exemption from likin was to be confined to the foreign concessions, he would be liable to the payment of likin.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "at liberty to pursue his business" is parliamentary procedure language meaning "permitted/allowed" in the technical sense—not a substantive claim about freedom-as-a-value. The sentence addresses legal liability and trade regulation, not fundamental liberty.

records.speaker: *SIR E. SASSOON  (Hythe)
records.sentence:
Until the question of the Yang-tsze Valley is settled I would humbly urge the Government to stiffen their backs and to show the same leaven of grit and virility which they displayed with such conspicuous success in the North and on the West Coast of Africa, and even in China itself, when they made Count Muroavieff withdraw his protest against the Newchwang loan, so that the
 828 
British flag may continue to be regarded as the symbol of liberty, security, and unrestricted freedom of trade.
records.haiku_rationale: British merchants and traders are freed from interference with their commerce—"unrestricted freedom of trade" names the absence of constraints on commercial activity in the Yang-tsze Valley and allied territories.

records.speaker: *MR. ALLAN
records.sentence: : I myself wanted to go to war to help the Cretans and Armenians to gain their independence and liberty;
records.haiku_rationale: Cretans and Armenians are being freed to gain their independence and liberty — i.e., empowered to govern themselves, which is positive liberty.

records.speaker: *SIR H. H. FOWLER
records.sentence: The British nation is as reponsible for the fiscal policy, for the commercial freedom, for the material progress of India as it is for its civil and military administration.
records.haiku_rationale: The "commercial freedom" referenced here is freedom from interference with trade and commerce in India — a core negative liberty concept. The speaker asserts Britain's responsibility for maintaining this non-interference, framed alongside fiscal policy and civil/military administration.

records.speaker: MR. THORBURN  (Selkirk and Peebles)
records.sentence: The proud title which it has assumed proclaims the principle on which it is founded to be that of liberty.
records.haiku_rationale: This sentence proclaims a foundational principle of liberty as a general value or cause opposed to despotism, without specifying what is being freed or from-to what; it is a rhetorical invocation of liberty as an abstract ideal.

records.speaker: MR. SCHWANN (Manchester, N.)
records.sentence: Judgment was given in his favour, and Don Simon was set at liberty.
records.haiku_rationale: Don Simon was freed from imprisonment/detention; this is freedom from constraint on his physical liberty.

records.speaker: THE EARL OF WEMYSS
records.sentence: I have had a motion upon the Paper of your Lordships' House for some months, and as this motion will explain all that I ask for at the present time and the views which I hold on this question, I will take the liberty of reading it to your Lordships.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "take the liberty of reading" is a parliamentary procedural idiom meaning "permit myself to" or "proceed to", not a claim about freedom as a political value.

records.speaker: MR. BRYCE
records.sentence: but it will depend upon the view which the Committee takes, and the freedom which it is allowed.
records.haiku_rationale: The Committee is given freedom (discretion or latitude) to act according to its view, which is a form of empowerment or capacity to operate without constraint.

records.speaker: SIR M. WHITE RIDLEY
records.sentence: from eight to ten having to sit in the mess room, or wherever the official likes—though, of course, he is liable to be called upon—and then from ten to six he is at liberty to go to bed.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "at liberty to go to bed" refers to freedom from constraint—the official is not required to remain on duty during those hours and may do as he wishes, including sleep. This is freedom from interference/obligation, not an empowerment to do something he couldn't otherwise do.

records.speaker: MR. JOHN BURNS
records.sentence: Given every latitude that ought to be given to freedom, to disciplined gaiety, to art, to literature, and to the rational enjoyment of a free people in their own way in a rich and large city, I think there is yet much to be done to prevent sheer animalism and brutality and bestiality protruding themselves as they have protruded themselves recently in very subtle forms in the West End of London.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes freedom of enjoyment and self-expression (freedom of the arts, literature, and recreation in one's own way) as a value to be respected, contrasting it with restrictions on animalism and brutality—a classic negative liberty position that certain forms of conduct should not be restricted.

records.speaker: *MR. BUTCHER  (York)
records.sentence: The objection that this was an interference with freedom of contract was unsound, because there could be no freedom of contract where there was weakness on the one side, and advantage taken of that weakness on the other.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from contractual interference is being discussed, but the speaker argues true freedom of contract requires substantive equality of bargaining power—thus implying freedom to contract meaningfully requires state intervention against exploitation of weakness.

records.speaker: MR. G. W. BALFOUR
records.sentence:
O'Brien said—
 "I have no hesitation in saying that men like John O'Donnell, who is fighting our own tyrants here at home to their teeth in the kopjes of the rent office and the coercion courts and Her Majesty's gaols, are doing better and more practical service for the cause of Irish freedom than if they were serving in any foreign army, no matter how gallant.
records.haiku_rationale: Irish freedom here means liberation from British colonial rule and coercive state institutions (rent offices, coercion courts, gaols) — freedom from interference with Irish self-governance and from oppression.

records.speaker: THE PRIME MINISTER AND SECRETARY OF STATE FOR FOREIGN AFFAIRS (The Marquess of SALISBURY)
records.sentence: But in dealing with this question I urge that you shall show to all the world that you do not deal with it as something on which you are at liberty to legislate on slender grounds or in the absence of thorough investigation.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "at liberty to legislate" is a parliamentary procedural expression meaning Parliament is not constrained from legislating; it does not invoke liberty-as-a-value regarding freedom from interference with something substantive.

records.speaker: MR. CREAN
records.sentence: I protest against this treatment, and it would be well that the public should know that there is no freedom of speech or of constitutional action in these towns, and that policemen baton peaceable crowds in the hope of making those crowds disorderly.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of speech and constitutional action are being removed through police interference; the speaker protests against the absence of non-interference with speech and assembly.

records.speaker: SIR JOHN BRUNNER  (Cheshire, Northwich)
records.sentence: They are now compelled by law to pay in a portion of their salaries to provide superannuation for themselves, and it is therefore peculiarly wrong that either the school board or denominational managers should be at liberty to send them about their business without any reason being assigned, seeing that by such dismissal they lose the payments they have made.
records.haiku_rationale: School managers are currently free from restraint in dismissing teachers without cause, but the speaker argues this freedom from interference should be curtailed because dismissal (permitted by current law) deprives teachers of their superannuation contributions; the sentence invokes "liberty" to criticize an existing non-interference regime.

records.speaker: SIR SAMUEL HOARE
records.sentence: I believe there are many cities, where it is impossible to acquire land within the borough area except at a very great cost, which will take advantage of this Bill to acquire land three, four, or five miles away, where the people can live and enjoy the fresh air and a liberty which it is impossible for them to enjoy in their present circumstances.
records.haiku_rationale: The "liberty" being discussed is freedom from urban confinement and overcrowding — the capacity to live away from cities and enjoy fresh air and space, i.e., an empowered opportunity to change one's living conditions.

records.speaker: MR. WILLIAM REDMOND  (Clare, E.)
records.sentence: Because they enjoy those things which Parliament has given them—those measures of freedom which you deny to the Irish people at home.
records.haiku_rationale: The Irish people are being denied measures of freedom (liberty from constraints/interference) that Parliament has granted to others; the sentence invokes freedom as a value opposed to denial and constraint.

records.speaker: MR. MARKS
records.sentence: Having once complied with the law in connection with that purely formal first issue, he was at liberty to ignore all the safeguards contained in that clause.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker describes a state of non-interference allowing a party to ignore safeguards—he was permitted/free from restriction to disregard legal requirements. This invokes liberty as absence of constraint.

records.speaker: MR. A. J. BALFOUR
records.sentence: Gentleman for more than a few minutes, but I must say a word or two of comment upon the strange doctrine of constitutional freedom which the right hon.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence alludes to "constitutional freedom" as a doctrine without specifying what is being freed or from-or-to what; the phrase is incompletely expressed and the substantive claim about freedom is not developed in this excerpt alone.

records.speaker: MR. A. J. BALFOUR
records.sentence: That liberty, I think, is of great importance.
records.haiku_rationale: Bare invocation of "liberty" as a value without specifying what is being freed, from what, or to what capacity.

records.speaker: THE EARL OF CAMPERDOWN
records.sentence:
My intention in proposing to insert these words is to give the local committee the liberty of saying,
 702 
after it sees the scheme, that it is too expensive and one with which it does not see its way to fall in.
records.haiku_rationale: The local committee is being empowered (given capacity) to decide whether to reject an expensive scheme—this grants them the ability to exercise discretion, making it positive liberty (freedom to make a choice).

records.speaker: SIR CHARLES DILKE
records.sentence: This is a case, as the Committee will remember, of the return into slavery by the action of a British court of a person who had been ten years in freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: A person who had been living in freedom is being returned to slavery by court action—this describes removal of freedom from external interference with personal status and bodily autonomy, a paradigmatic case of negative liberty being stripped away.

records.speaker: THE FIRST LORD OF THE TREASURY (Mr. A. J. BALFOUR,  Manchester, E. )
records.sentence: Our freedom of action will be wholly unimpaired, but some machinery will be provided by which the arguments and the evidence on either side will be put before us in some intelligible and assimilable form.
records.haiku_rationale: What is being freed: the First Lord's freedom of action (political/governmental decision-making); from what: from being hampered or constrained by unorganized information. The claim is that despite implementing new machinery for presenting evidence, their capacity to act will remain unimpaired.

records.speaker: MR. A. J. BALFOUR
records.sentence: If you conceive a body of men like the burghers of the Transvaal, fervently animated by the idea of liberty, but conceiving liberty as liberty for themselves and no liberty for anyone else, conceiving liberty as many of the aristocracies of the old world conceived it, as a body of free superiors having under their heel a large subject population, I do not wholly condemn the sentiments that condition of things generates.
records.haiku_rationale: Liberty is invoked as freedom from external constraint (for "free superiors"), but the sentence presents a hierarchical conception where one group's freedom is purchased through domination of another group with no liberty, making the underlying claim about freedom ambiguous between negative liberty (freedom from interference) and a twisted positive liberty (empowerment to rule others).

records.speaker: THE ARCHBISHOP OF CANTERBURY
records.sentence: In that case the Privy Council went to the utmost length of giving liberty to the teaching of doctrine which they themselves acknowledge was not the teaching that was naturally to be drawn from the formularies of the Church, but which they said they could not condemn because the Church had nowhere forbidden the holding or teaching of it.
records.haiku_rationale: The Privy Council granted empowerment to teach a particular doctrine—capacity to hold and teach something not naturally drawn from Church formularies—rather than removing interference with teaching. This is liberty as granted capacity or permission to do something.

records.speaker: MR. JOHN BURNS  (Battersea)
records.sentence: Except for deferring to that body of company promoters  in excelsis , the Liberty and Property Defence League, and except for pandering to the ignorant prejudices of the Lord Wemysses and the gang of company promoters who met at the Society of Arts three months ago, I can see no reason for this Committee.
records.haiku_rationale: The Liberty and Property Defence League is a proper noun / organization name being criticized rhetorically; the word "Liberty" appears as part of a named entity, not as a substantive claim about freedom-as-a-value or freedom from/to something specific.

records.speaker: SIR. H. CAMPBEEL-BANNEERMAN  (Stirling Burghs)
records.sentence: and they showed no desire in this case to take advantage of the freedom offered.
records.haiku_rationale: The freedom being discussed is one that has been offered or made available to them — a capacity or opportunity that has been provided, which they declined to take advantage of.

records.speaker: SIR ROBERT REID
records.sentence: But if we were to violate that essential condition of our Empire in South Africa, must not everyone feel that, quite apart from the question of South Africa, the most gloomy forebodings might be raised among other colonies as to the tenure of their freedom resting upon a precarious basis?
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes the colonies' "tenure of their freedom" as a value at stake if Britain violates imperial commitments; the freedom here is the capacity/right of colonies to govern themselves or maintain their autonomous status within the Empire.

records.speaker: *MR. PATRICK O'BRIEN  (Kilkenny)
records.sentence: I say that this is as gross an interference with the freedom of the press as over occurred in Ireland, and that is saying a great deal.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes freedom of the press as something being interfered with—freedom from governmental or other external interference with press operations.

records.speaker: THE ATTORNEY GENERAL FOR IRELAND (Mr. ATKINSON,  Londonderry, N. )
records.sentence: Member has indulged in a freedom which it would be obviously most improper for me to follow, because he has criticised and entered into the validity of a charge that is now pending against these two men.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker uses "indulged in a freedom" to refer to the member's procedural latitude to criticize a pending charge; this is parliamentary idiom ("took the liberty of"), not a substantive claim about liberty-as-a-value.

records.speaker: COLONEL SAUNDERSON
records.sentence: Gentlemen opposite may say, and however they may sneer and misrepresent the motives that have caused the Government to take this action, the British people will record their approval of a policy which will give freedom and justice and prosperity to the whole of South Africa.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "freedom...to the whole of South Africa" as a positive outcome of government policy—freedom as a state of prosperous self-determination or self-governance for a people/territory, not freedom from interference with a specific capacity or right.

records.speaker: LORD HUGH CECIL  (Greenwich)
records.sentence: The essence of freedom was to have a free choice.
records.haiku_rationale: Being freed to have the capacity to make free choice; freedom is defined as empowerment to exercise volition.

records.speaker: MR. JOHN BURNS
records.sentence: Having said that, it is possible so to organise the public decency of streets as to give liberty, almost licence, and yet keep the young from being corrupted.
records.haiku_rationale: The freedom being discussed is liberty (licence) in matters of public decency and street conduct—freedom from restriction on adult behavior—while simultaneously constraining conduct to protect young people from corruption; this combines removal of interference with a paternalistic constraint, making the liberty reference mixed.

records.speaker: LORD HENEAGE
records.sentence: said that after this expression of opinion from the Leaders on both sides of the House, he felt himself at liberty to consent to the adjournment.
records.haiku_rationale: Parliamentary procedural use: the speaker felt empowered to consent to adjournment; "at liberty" is a formulaic phrase meaning permitted/able to act, not a substantive claim about freedom-as-a-value.

records.speaker: MR. ATKINSON
records.sentence: He based his application for liberty to sublet on the necessity of giving his whole time to the performance of his official duties.
records.haiku_rationale: Parliamentary procedure: seeking permission ("liberty") to sublet property; this is a procedural request for authorization within parliamentary/administrative rules, not a normative claim about freedom as a value.

records.speaker: MR. DILLON  (Mayo, E.)
records.sentence: : Am I to understand I shall be at liberty to move in Committee, by way of new clauses or Amendments, provisions securing the interests of debenture-holders and depositors?
records.haiku_rationale: A parliamentary member asks whether he will be permitted (procedurally) to move amendments in Committee—a procedural question about what parliamentary actions are allowed, not a substantive claim about liberty as a value.

records.speaker: ME. WINSTON CHURCHILL  (Oldham)
records.sentence: As soon as it is known that there is in the Transvaal a government under which property and liberty are secure, so soon as it is known that in these countries one can live freely and safely, there would be a rush of immigrants from all parts of the world to develop the country and to profit by the great revival of trade which usually follows war of all kinds.
records.haiku_rationale: Security of property and liberty, and ability to "live freely and safely," are conditions enabling economic activity and immigration — capacity to act without fear of arbitrary interference with persons and property.

records.speaker: *THE LORD BISHOP OF HEREFORD
records.sentence:
I cannot but believe, while holding firmly, as I do, to the great value of individual liberty and the importance of never neglecting the principle of  laissez faire  in polities, that temperance reform is one of the most pressing matters of the time, and it is our duty, a duty
 
 667 
involving no interference with devotion to the principle of individual liberty, to take measures to regulate a dangerous trade.
records.haiku_rationale: Individual liberty is invoked as a principle opposing interference with trade and conduct (non-interference); simultaneously, the speaker advocates regulatory measures, which constitute interference. This presents both negative liberty (freedom from interference) as a stated value and positive/state action (regulation) as a competing duty.

records.speaker: THE MARQUESS OF SALISBURY
records.sentence: The innocent consumption by temperate consumers of that which is not an illegal indulgence is not a liberty which it is right for Parliament to restrict, unless they are driven by some very supreme consideration to do so.
records.haiku_rationale: Salisbury invokes freedom from Parliamentary restriction of innocent consumption (a non-interference right), framed as a liberty that Parliament should not curtail unless under overwhelming necessity.

records.speaker: THE CHANCELLOR OF THE EXCHEQUER (Sir M. HICKS BEACH,  Bristol, W. )
records.sentence: : The President of the Local Government Beard has asked me to answer this question, as the resolution aims, not only at the exclusion of deleterious ingredients from beer, but at limiting the freedom of brewers to use materials which, though wholesome, are not malt and hops.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence discusses limiting brewers' freedom to use non-malt and non-hops materials in beer production—i.e., freedom FROM regulatory interference with their choice of ingredients.

records.speaker: MR. WILLIAM O'BRIEN
records.sentence: The judges would certainly not be the least zealous to avail themselves of any materials for starting one of those great crusades against public liberty of which you have set art example.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "public liberty" as something being defended against "crusades" (attacks/interference), making it a negative liberty concern—freedom from interference with the public's liberty and rights.

records.speaker: MR. J. CHAMBEELAIN
records.sentence: In the first instance, that must be more restricted in these two colonies than it is in the colonies of the Cape and Natal, but a liberty and constitution, leading ultimately to self-government, which Ave all desire to see established as soon as possible.
records.haiku_rationale: A constitution and self-government of two colonies are being granted, giving them empowerment to govern themselves—a positive liberty capacity.

records.speaker: MR. TULLY (continuing)
records.sentence: The unfortunate and defenceless people who surrendered their arms very speedily found out what were the English ideas of liberty and freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is criticizing English conduct toward disarmed people as inconsistent with professed ideals of liberty and freedom—invoking liberty as freedom from oppressive treatment and arbitrary state action, contrasted with what actually befell the defenseless.

records.speaker: MR. JAMES LOWTHER
records.sentence: That Conference passed a resolution, he thought with absolute unanimity, urging that liberty should be accorded to the colonies to make fiscal arrangements without reference to any foreign Power.
records.haiku_rationale: The colonies are being empowered (or enabled) to make fiscal arrangements without external constraints—they are being granted the capacity and authority to govern their own trade policy.

records.speaker: Unknown
records.sentence: I return you My thanks for the expression of your loyal attachment to My person and your confidence in My desire to promote the happiness and liberty of My subjects, and I fervently join in your prayer that Almighty God will guide and strengthen my councils to that end.
records.haiku_rationale: The monarch invokes "liberty of My subjects" as an object of desire that she will work to promote—this is freedom (in a broad sense) as a state of well-being or flourishing that the government aims to bring about, a capacity or condition enabling subjects to live well, which aligns with positive liberty (empowerment toward a good state) rather than negative liberty (freedom from specific interferences).

records.speaker: THE SECRETARY OF STATE FOR THE COLONIES (Mr. J. CHAMBERLAIN, Birmingham, W.)
records.sentence: On the contrary, we are securing to them the liberty to make their own choice, and it is only because that choice seems to have been against the feelings of the elected members, who are chiefly lawyers, that this agitation has arisen.
records.haiku_rationale: The object of freedom is "to make their own choice" — an empowered capacity being secured to a group, not merely non-interference with choice-making. This is freedom TO exercise agency.

records.speaker: The SECRETARY of STATE for the COLONIES (Mr. J. Chamberlain,  Birmingham, W. )
records.sentence: and in order to do that we are to announce "measures for securing the liberty and property of those now in arms who surrender, for the settlement of those territories, and for promoting the reconcilement and well-being of their inhabitants.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence promises to secure liberty and property of Boer combatants who surrender, and to promote the well-being of inhabitants through settlement measures — framing liberty as a valued outcome (restored right/status) in the context of post-conflict reconciliation, alongside property rights and material welfare.

records.speaker: MR. THOMAS O'DONNELL
records.sentence: Are these the prospects that will induce men who love liberty dearer than life, posterity dearer than self,** to come in and end this horrible and inhuman war?
records.haiku_rationale: Men who love liberty (freedom from external interference and constraint, opposed to tyranny and war) are being appealed to as agents who value their own and their posterity's independence and self-determination.

records.speaker: MR. MURPHY  (Kerry, E.)
records.sentence: Although they are doing it in a different way, they are, like ourselves, fighting for their liberty.
records.haiku_rationale: People fighting for their liberty from oppression or external constraint—a rhetorical invocation of liberty as freedom from domination or interference.

records.speaker: MR. LOUGH
records.sentence: Gladstone and Sir George Cornewall Lewis had not had to act after a period of twenty-five years freedom from the duty;
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence refers to a period of absence from an obligation or duty (the duty in question), not freedom as a political or rights-based value—it is about exemption from administrative responsibility.

records.speaker: MR. SPEAKER
records.sentence: and now, my Lords, it is my duty, in the name and on behalf of the Commons of the United Kingdom, to lay claim, by humble petition to Her Majesty, to all their ancient and undoubted rights and privileges, especially to freedom of speech in debate, freedom from arrest, and free access to Her Majesty whenever occasion may require, and that the most favourable construction may be put upon all their proceedings.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence claims freedom of speech in debate, freedom from arrest, and free access—these are protections from interference with parliamentary rights and person, classic negative liberties.

records.speaker: *VISCOUNT FRANKFORT DE MONT-MORENCY
records.sentence: Therefore it seems to me unlikely in the highest degree that any increase of pay would attract men of this class to join the Army and give up the comparative freedom of civil life for the restrictions of military life in barracks.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker contrasts "freedom of civil life" (freedom from military restrictions) with "the restrictions of military life in barracks"—freedom from externally imposed constraints on movement, conduct, and autonomy.

records.speaker: MR. BROADHURST
records.sentence: I would like, if the Leader of the House will permit me, to take the liberty to remind him that there are still other parties in the House than that which owns allegiance to his sway and great power.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is using "take the liberty to remind him" as a parliamentary formula requesting permission to speak; this is procedural usage where "liberty" means permission to proceed with an utterance, not a substantive claim about freedom as a value.

records.speaker: MR. ARTHUR LEE  (Hampshire, Fareham)
records.sentence: But I think he himself will admit that the speech which he delivered last night was originally designed to introduce that Amendment, and therefore I am at liberty to refer to certain points in it.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker claims to be permitted (by the parliamentary rules or situation) to refer to certain points; "at liberty" here is a parliamentary procedural expression meaning "permitted" or "allowed"—not a substantive claim about freedom as a value.

records.speaker: THE LORD BISHOP OF HEREFORD
records.sentence: John Stuart Mill, that great advocate of individual liberty, would, I venture to think, have been with us in our attempts to deal with this evil.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes Mill as an "advocate of individual liberty" in the context of addressing a social evil, appealing to the principle of liberty as opposition to external constraints and harm—a classic negative liberty rhetorical move.

records.speaker: MR. WILLIAM ABRAHAM  (Glamorganshire, Rhondda)
records.sentence: I allow them to have the freedom of their opinion.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of opinion is freedom from interference with one's beliefs and thoughts; the speaker permits them to hold opinions without his intervention or constraint.

records.speaker: MR. SYDNEY BUXTON
records.sentence: said that Lord Wolseley's promises were as he recollected them, promises of personal liberty and justice, and they had been entirely fulfilled.
records.haiku_rationale: Lord Wolseley promised personal liberty and justice (freedom from arbitrary interference and oppression), and these promises were fulfilled—this invokes liberty as a cause opposed to tyranny.

records.speaker: SIR FRANCIS POWELL
records.sentence: The liberty now exercised by the sister of the deceased wife living in the desolated home and acting as mother to the unhappy children will be taken away.
records.haiku_rationale: The sister's liberty (freedom/right) to remain in the home and act as mother to the children will be removed, a loss of capacity to continue her current role.

records.speaker: MR. BRYCE
records.sentence: He, therefore, earnestly hoped that the Government would give a certain amount of freedom to the Committee on this matter.
records.haiku_rationale: The Committee is being freed to act with autonomy (discretion) on the matter, rather than being constrained by Government direction—this is empowerment to govern itself.

records.speaker: Sir ROBERT REID  (Dumfries Burghs)
records.sentence: Gentleman conceived himself at liberty to put forward the very next year the same proposal which he had defended on that very limited ground.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "at liberty to put forward" refers to a gentleman's freedom to make a proposal, using "at liberty" in the parliamentary procedure sense meaning "permitted" or "entitled to"—not a substantive claim about freedom-as-a-value. This is procedural language about what someone is entitled to do within debate, not about liberty in the normative political sense.

records.speaker: SIR FRANCIS POWELL
records.sentence:
Why should there be taken away the freedom
 440

opinion that the certificate is all right they are at perfect liberty later on to bring forward evidence to show that that is so, but in my opinion the issuing of certificates by the Home Office is not done with that care which should be given to those cases.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker uses "at perfect liberty" in parliamentary procedure — referring to the procedural right to bring forward evidence at a later stage, not advancing a claim about liberty as a political value.

records.speaker: Mr. KIDD
records.sentence: in the way I indicate, if he will enable any miner who wants it to have a suitable home, a home in the real British sense, a home which is really the Englishman's castle, a home reflecting the taste of the occupants of the home, as every home should do, the miner for the first time in his life will realise freedom of contract.
records.haiku_rationale: A miner "realises freedom of contract" (capacity to make binding agreements) when enabled to own a suitable home reflecting his tastes—this is freedom to exercise contractual agency through homeownership.

records.speaker: Lieutenant-Colonel WEIGALL
records.sentence: Asquith when he received the freedom of his native town—
records.haiku_rationale: Asquith receiving the "freedom of his native town" is a ceremonial honour (formal civic status granted to a distinguished person), not a claim about liberty-as-a-value in the philosophical sense.

records.speaker: Dr. ADDISON
records.sentence:
At the conclusion of our proceedings, with the concurrence of the Committee, I said:
 It must be open for the Government to review the situation, and if we really find it vitally necessary for administrative purposes and the working of the services of the Education Department to bring up words on Report which will meet the administrative difficulties, which I am sure the carrying out of the Amendment proposed would certainly make for us, I must be at liberty to do so.
records.haiku_rationale: Being "at liberty to" do something (bring up words on Report) describes the speaker's empowerment to take procedural action necessary for administrative purposes.

records.speaker: Unknown
records.sentence: All that they ask is—seeing that the Bolsheviks secured the arsenals of Russia—that they should be supplied with the necessary arms to enable them to fight for their own protection and freedom in the land where the Bolshevists are anti-pathetic to the feeling of the population.
records.haiku_rationale: The freed agent (anti-Bolshevik Russian forces) is seeking capacity to act—specifically, to fight and secure their own protection and freedom in Russia—empowered by receiving necessary arms from external suppliers.

records.speaker: Mr. W. R. SMITH
records.sentence: I hope a new phase of things is arising where the same freedom and liberty of action will be accorded to the agricultural labourer as are enjoyed by other sections of the industrial world.
records.haiku_rationale: Agricultural labourers are being freed FROM occupational restrictions that other industrial workers do not face—freedom of action in employment conditions is relief from discriminatory constraint.

records.speaker: Mr. DEVLIN
records.sentence: " That is the answer you get when you talk about freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence makes a rhetorical dismissal of an abstract appeal to "freedom" without specifying what freedom means or what is being freed from or enabled to do.

records.speaker: Sir T. WHITTAKER
records.sentence: With regard to land values I may speak with considerable freedom, because when the land values proposals were first made in the form in which they appeared I ventured to criticise them strongly, and made use of one expression which our Unionist Friends embodied in a poster, and used in support of their candidates at the General Election.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is describing his capacity to speak freely ("speak with considerable freedom") on land values, referring to his past ability to have criticised proposals—he is describing a capacity/permission to act or speak without constraint, not a removal of interference from speech itself. The phrase is parliamentary procedural: the speaker is explaining he can speak on this topic because of his prior involvement and credibility.

records.speaker: Mr. CLYNES
records.sentence: We should give them the fullest measure of liberty.
records.haiku_rationale: Liberty being granted/given to "them" (a nation or people) in a postwar context, representing empowerment of self-governance or independence.

records.speaker: Sir E. CARSON
records.sentence:
Clause 4 runs as follows:
 Whereas it has been the custom in the public elementary schools in the county borough of Belfast to give instruction in religion to children whose parents did not object to the instruction so given, but with liberty to parents, without forfeiting any of the other advantages of the schools, to elect that their children should not receive such instruction.
