records.haiku_rationale: Unlicensed printing is freed from state licensing requirements; this defends freedom of the press from prior restraint and government control over printing.

records.speaker: Mr. Arthur Henderson
records.sentence: Once it is established that the Fascist Powers of the world are determined to expand and commit acts of aggression against not only China but any other democratic Power which seeks to stand in their way, the United States of America would, I believe, not only be compelled by the pressure of world opinion, but would be anxious to rally to the defence of democracy and freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "defence of democracy and freedom" as a cause opposed to Fascist aggression and expansion—a rhetorical appeal to negative liberty (freedom from tyrannical interference by aggressive powers).

records.speaker: Mr. Dingle Foot
records.sentence: ' The draftsman is always at liberty to put points of that sort to those who instruct him, but the decision is not ultimately his;
records.haiku_rationale: The draftsman's ability to raise points with instructors is a procedural faculty within a professional context, not a claim about freedom-as-a-value from interference or empowerment to act in the substantive political sense.

records.speaker: Mr. Gallacher
records.sentence: I ask not only for justice for these people but for all kinds of liberty, because, sooner or later, we on this side are going to see to it that they get the liberty of going down the pit or of going into some other industry to work for their living.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is claiming the freedom (or capacity) of workers to go down the pit or enter other industries to work for their living — the object of liberty is the enabled opportunity to choose and pursue employment without deprivation or exclusion.

records.speaker: Miss Rathbone
records.sentence: We have a great opportunity, if we would only seize it, of making our true and beautiful song of liberty as frequently and as well heard as the hideous din of the Nazis and the Fascists.
records.haiku_rationale: Liberty is invoked as an ideological cause (the "song of liberty") to be championed and heard against totalitarian oppression (Nazis and Fascists), contrasting freedom from tyranny with authoritarian regimes—a rhetorical appeal to negative liberty as opposition to coercive state control.

records.speaker: Sir Arnold Gridley
records.sentence: The oil industries are glad to feel that until last year there was comparative freedom from strikes.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from strikes: the oil industries are freed from labour disruption/industrial action, a negative liberty regarding absence of constraint.

records.speaker: Mr. Silverman
records.sentence:
" 
The whole policy of this Government has been not to allow freedom of contract on any aspect of social affairs which involves questions of wide public importance.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of contract (the ability to enter into agreements without state interference) is being restricted by the Government in matters of public importance; this names freedom from interference with contractual liberty.

records.speaker: Mr. Spens
records.sentence: In these circumstances I am convinced that it is in the interests of the community to get back to ordinary freedom of contract in respect of houses of all classes as soon as we can.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of contract—capacity of parties to negotiate and conclude agreements without state interference—is freedom from restriction on voluntary economic exchange.

records.speaker: Admiral of the Fleet Sir Roger Keyes
records.sentence:
While food storage and greatly increased production of home-grown food cannot be an alternative to a strong Navy and an efficient and sufficient Mercantile Marine, the more food that can be stored and produced, the more freedom there will be for the Navy to exercise its proper function at the outset of war, namely, to destroy the enemy's sea communications and to seek and destroy his sea forces or


contain them.
records.haiku_rationale: The Navy is being freed from logistical constraints (the need to protect food supplies) to pursue its military function of destroying enemy sea communications and forces — freedom to act unfettered from a domestic vulnerability.

records.speaker: Mr. Attlee
records.sentence: They have had many chances lately of taking a stand on the side of freedom, a stand for collective security and a stand on the side of international law, and of preventing things from going down the abyss.
records.haiku_rationale: This sentence invokes "freedom" as a cause opposed to tyranny and abyss; it refers to nations taking a stand "on the side of freedom" in the context of collective security and international law, indicating resistance to oppressive interference with international order.

records.speaker: The Prime Minister
records.sentence: This is especially true in the case of two countries like Great Britain and France, with long associations of friendship, with interests closely interwoven, devoted to the same ideals of democratic liberty, and determined to uphold them.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "democratic liberty" is a rhetorical invocation of liberty as a political ideal opposed to tyranny, naming freedom from autocratic rule rather than any specific capacity the speaker is empowered to exercise.

records.speaker: Sir A. Sinclair
records.sentence:
Therefore, I say that one indispensable way—it is not, of course, the complete policy of constructive peace which I want the Government to pursue—one indispensable way of averting war is to make it clear beforehand to Germany that if, in our opinion, Czechoslovakia is the victim of unprovoked aggression—and we, of course,

must retain our freedom of decision as to whether aggression is unprovoked—[HON.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker asserts the need to retain freedom of decision regarding whether aggression is unprovoked—a capacity to make autonomous judgments on matters of state without external constraint, a form of empowerment or self-determination.

records.speaker: Mr. Mebane
records.sentence: He referred to freedom of contract.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of contract is freedom from interference with one's right to enter into voluntary agreements; it names non-interference with contractual choice.

records.speaker: Mr. Paling
records.sentence: Gentleman will deal with the matter and see that wages are increased, that social services are put into operation, that the labour department is set up, that trade unions are allowed to exist, with the same full rights as they have in this country, and that full liberty will be given to these people to voice their grievances publicly without going against the law of the land.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence grants capacity (liberty) for people to voice grievances publicly—a positive empowerment to act, contrasted with the enabling conditions being set up (wages, services, unions).

records.speaker: Mr. Parkinson
records.sentence: If it is contrary to the policy of his Department to limit their freedom to engage labour in any way, why does the Department use the Fair Wages Clause, and why do they lay down conditions for local authorities who engage unemployed workers?
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "freedom to engage labour" — the capacity to hire workers without constraint — which is being curtailed by Fair Wages Clause requirements and conditions on local authorities. This concerns freedom from interference with labour practices and contracting.

records.speaker: The Financial Secretary to the Treasury
records.sentence: It was not given a definite, cut-and-dried afforestation programme, and Parliament has given the Commission very considerable freedom in its detailed administration;
records.haiku_rationale: Parliament grants the Commission freedom from detailed parliamentary constraints in administering afforestation — empowering the Commission to exercise discretion over administrative decisions.

records.speaker: Mr. McKie
records.sentence: He mentioned the River Tweed, and that is why I have taken the liberty this evening of raising the question of the Talla scheme and the taking of the compensation water under that scheme, which was bound to be poured down the River Tweed.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "taken the liberty of raising the question" is a parliamentary procedural expression meaning "exercised my parliamentary privilege/right to bring up", not a claim about freedom-as-a-value.

records.speaker: The Prime Minister
records.sentence: He is characterised by fearlessness, freedom from prejudice, integrity and impartiality, and I am quite certain that everyone here will wish him all success.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from prejudice is freedom from a mental disposition or bias that might interfere with judgment; it names freedom from an internal constraint on impartial thinking and decision-making.

records.speaker: Major Dower
records.sentence: In addition to that, they were set at liberty immediately the crisis was past in order to ensure that they did not lose their civilian jobs, and in many cases when they returned to them they received pay for the time when they had been on leave.
records.haiku_rationale: They were set at liberty (released from detention/military service) immediately after the crisis ended — freedom from continued confinement or obligation.

records.speaker: Mr. Petherick
records.sentence: Gentleman said something about the question of Gibraltar, and claimed that the Government, in any arrangement that was made, should insist on the freedom of the Straits.
records.haiku_rationale: The freedom being invoked is freedom of the Straits from obstruction or control—freedom of passage/navigation through a territorial waterway, a classic form of negative liberty (freedom from interference with movement/commerce).

records.speaker: Unknown
records.sentence: Gentleman opposite ended with some eloquent words about liberty.
records.haiku_rationale: This is a rhetorical reference to liberty as a cause or value that the opposing speaker invoked eloquently, without specifying what liberty is being discussed or its specific object.

records.speaker: Mr. Batey
records.sentence: I was going to argue for more Amendments in the Bill, or more freedom in the Bill, so that money might be spent more freely and so that we might know where it was going to be spent in the future, both in the Special Areas and also in the outside areas.
records.haiku_rationale: More freedom for money to be spent more freely, and transparency about future spending—this concerns empowerment of administrative/budgetary discretion to act, not freedom from interference with a specific liberty right.

records.speaker: Mr. Gallacher
records.sentence: they have a sense of independence and freedom that they never could have under the old conditions.
records.haiku_rationale: They have the capacity/sense of independence and freedom to act (versus previously being unable to act this way under old conditions); this is empowerment or enablement to be independent.

records.speaker: Mr. Gallacher
records.sentence: Members to think what it means to have a whole batch of young lads in the decisive years of their lives in a Borstal institution, even with the amount of freedom which exists.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "freedom" to describe the conditions within a Borstal institution, emphasizing that even the limited freedom available does not adequately mitigate the harm of incarceration during formative years—freedom from institutional constraint is the object being discussed.

records.speaker: Lieut.-Commander Fletcher
records.sentence:
And I was particularly struck by words used by Lord Willoughby de Eresby—again we have a namesake in the House to-day—who said:
 If greater freedom for the public was required, personally he would not be opposed to it.
records.haiku_rationale: This is a bare invocation of "freedom for the public" without specification of freedom from what interference or to do what. The context does not disambiguate whether it means removing constraints on the public or empowering them to act.

records.speaker: Major Rayner
records.sentence: Members have pointed out, that he has been registered from the day of his birth, and he cannot for the life of him see why the principle of compulsory registration should not be extended to an organisation which is intended to save his life and his liberty.
records.haiku_rationale: Liberty here refers to freedom from state interference or coercion—specifically, the speaker is defending compulsory registration (for an organization intended to protect life and liberty) by noting that registration is already applied to births. The "liberty" invoked is protection from arbitrary state action, a core negative liberty concern.

records.speaker: Mr. Montague
records.sentence: When we talk about the freedom of the Press, we ought to consider not only rights but duties.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of the Press is a negative liberty: the press is freed from interference and censorship, though here the speaker invokes the notion alongside a discussion of duties.

records.speaker: Mr. H. G. Williams
records.sentence: I believe in freedom of contract.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker asserts belief in freedom of contract — freedom from interference with the right to enter into voluntary agreements without state obstruction.

records.speaker: Mr. McCorquodale
records.sentence: I want freedom for the individual to practice such communion with his Maker as he finds most satisfying to his own conscience, and I want him everywhere to have such peace of mind that he can so develop his own mental and spiritual faculties as to enrich his own life and that of all others with whom he comes in contact.
records.haiku_rationale: This sentence seeks both negative liberty (freedom of conscience/religious practice from interference) and positive liberty (capacity to develop one's mental and spiritual faculties and enrich one's life). The speaker invokes both non-interference with religious conscience and the empowerment to develop oneself fully.

records.speaker: Mr. Williams
records.sentence: I stand for the principle of liberty.
records.haiku_rationale: Bare invocation of "liberty" as a general principle opposed implicitly to tyranny or oppression, without specifying what is being freed or from/to what—a rhetorical appeal to liberty-as-a-value.

records.speaker: Mr. Buchanan
records.sentence: Working people in these days ought to have some kind of liberty in these matters.
records.haiku_rationale: Working people ought to have some kind of freedom/capacity to act or make choices in "these matters" (unspecified in context), suggesting empowerment to do something rather than mere absence of interference.

records.speaker: Mr. White
records.sentence: I have been wondering what would happen if I were to mention the words "liberty" and "democracy" in the course of this Debate.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is rhetorical and speculative about mentioning the words "liberty" and "democracy"; no substantive claim about freedom from interference or capacity/empowerment is made.

records.speaker: Mr. Lawson
records.sentence: but Britons have definitely made up their minds that they will brook no interference with their political liberties, through which they can alone win economic freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: Britons are freed from interference with their political liberties (negative liberty), and those liberties enable them to achieve economic freedom (positive liberty outcome); the sentence treats political liberty as freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Mr. Ellis Smith
records.sentence: Are they freedom, peace, and social justice?
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "freedom" rhetorically as a political ideal/value, listing it alongside peace and social justice as goals, but does not specify what is being freed or from/to what.

records.speaker: Mr. Trevor Cox
records.sentence: It may be that the German Chancellor is anxious to usher in some new, happy, golden age of innocence and freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: A rhetorical invocation of "freedom" as a political ideal and cause opposed to Nazi tyranny and oppression; the specific object of freedom (freedom from what constraint or interference) is unspecified and remains a general ideological appeal.

records.speaker: Mr. Sexton
records.sentence: These people are limited not only in their liberty;
records.haiku_rationale: These people are limited in their general liberty—restricted from acting freely, constrained by external limitation.

records.speaker: Mr. Sexton
records.sentence: " Well, the freedom of the poor is a very limited thing.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is describing the capacity/empowerment of poor people—what they are able to do—as limited, invoking freedom as the scope of actionable choice available to the poor (positive liberty).

records.speaker: Colonel Wedgwood
records.sentence: "we need not defend liberty because the Government are going to introduce conscription and everybody will come in in his proper turn.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker ironically claims we need not defend liberty against conscription, sarcastically implying conscription threatens individual freedom from compulsory military service—a freedom from state interference in personal bodily autonomy and choice of occupation.

records.speaker: The Solicitor-General for Scotland
records.sentence: I think everyone in the House is favourable to the general principles of the Bill and desires for small collections as great a freedom as is compatible with reasonable restrictions to prevent fraud.
records.haiku_rationale: Small collections are being freed from restrictions (negative liberty), but the sentence also emphasizes that this freedom is limited by "reasonable restrictions to prevent fraud," making the underlying claim about enabling capacity within constraints (positive liberty of action). The dual framing—freedom from interference balanced against permitted restrictions—makes this ambiguous.

records.speaker: Mr. Pethick-Lawrence
records.sentence: " But if the fire goes on it it not a question of thinking who is to blame, it is a question of all hands to assist, and because we love our country and believe in its future, because we believe in democracy and liberty, not only here but throughout the world, we say to the Government that if you are really going forward to put out the fire now we are bound to give you our help.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "democracy and liberty" as a cause and value that motivates support for the Government's efforts, using liberty as a rhetorical appeal to a shared ideal opposed to (implicit) tyranny or disorder—a classic negative liberty appeal.

records.speaker: Mr. Stephen
records.sentence: If you give them liberty and justice you will not have these outrages.
records.haiku_rationale: Being freed from oppression/injustice (the outrages) by being given liberty and justice—a capacity for dignified, lawful treatment.

records.speaker: Mr. Benn
records.sentence: If the Amendments are made in another place by the Government and they come back to us here as Amendments, we should have freedom to discuss them as such almost with the same latitude as if they had been moved in this House.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from procedural constraints on discussing amendments—what is being freed is the capacity to debate amendments with latitude, freed from restrictive parliamentary procedure.

records.speaker: Mr. Adams
records.sentence: I thought we were at liberty at raise a question any time after you had run through the Clauses.
records.haiku_rationale: This is parliamentary procedure language: "at liberty to" means "permitted" or "entitled to," referring to standing procedural rules for when questions may be raised, not a claim about freedom-as-a-value.

records.speaker: The First Lord of the Admiralty
records.sentence:
It was to bridge the gap between what we had ready at the beginning and what we have ready now that the Admiralty decided to use the aircraft carriers with some freedom in order to bring in the unarmed, unorganised and unconvoyed traffic which was then approaching our

shores in large numbers.
records.haiku_rationale: Naval vessels (aircraft carriers) are given operational freedom from constraints in order to accomplish a military objective (protecting merchant shipping)—an enabling capacity rather than a protection from interference.

records.speaker: Sir Charles Cayzer
records.sentence: I do not think that there is a Member in this House who would consider a peace which would militate against complete freedom in Europe or which would subject the downtrodden peoples in Europe to a perpetuation of German domination, but the right hon.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from German domination and oppressive control over European peoples; the object of freedom is the downtrodden peoples of Europe, freed from subjection to German rule.

records.speaker: Mr. McGovern
records.sentence: They did not win freedom for the people.
records.haiku_rationale: The people are being freed (or not freed, in this case) – but freed from what or to do what is not specified in the sentence. The object of freedom is unspecified.

records.speaker: The Secretary of State for Dominion Affairs
records.sentence: That combination is exactly an example of how order and freedom can be reconciled.
records.haiku_rationale: Order and freedom are presented as reconcilable principles in governance, but the sentence does not specify what is being freed, from what constraint, or what capacity is being enabled—it merely asserts that these two values can coexist.

records.speaker: Mr. Simmonds
records.sentence: Friend will he bear in mind that the country sincerely hopes that this will be no isolated instance and that there will be given to the Royal Air Force wide liberty of action to distinguish itself in similar enterprises?
records.haiku_rationale: The Royal Air Force is being granted liberty of action—empowerment and operational discretion to conduct military enterprises without constraint. This concerns the capacity or freedom to act, not freedom from interference with a named activity.

records.speaker: Mr. Sorensen
records.sentence:
Rightly or wrongly, she has come to the conclusion that she was not

consulted at the beginning of the war and yet was involved in it, and that whatever may be the lip service we pay to freedom in India, we do not intend to treat India as a sovereign nation able by her own volition to decide, as other Dominions do, her own course of action in the future.
records.haiku_rationale: India's freedom is her capacity to decide her own course of action and govern herself as a sovereign nation, not dependent on others' dictates.

records.speaker: Miss Rathbone
records.sentence: But, if we are suspect, if you have no use for us, do not send us abroad as prisoners, but find us room in some Colony or Dominion, or in the United States, and enable us to start a new life away from Europe and all its entanglements and oppression in an era of freedom again.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker seeks enablement to start a new life away from oppression—empowerment to escape and rebuild elsewhere, not merely freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Mr. Lipson
records.sentence: The good is so vital to the nation, particularly in these days when we have to face propaganda from the Continent against free thought and the freedom of the human spirit that we should be reluctant to take such a step as is proposed by this tax.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of the human spirit is being defended against propaganda designed to suppress independent thought—a claim about freedom from interference with autonomous thinking and belief.

records.speaker: Mr. Mander
records.sentence: It is composed—like almost every country in the world—of those few who believe in dictatorship and force, and those many who believe in democracy and freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "freedom" as a value opposed to "dictatorship and force," making a rhetorical claim about freedom as the absence of domination and coercive control.

records.speaker: The Minister of Economic Warfare
records.sentence: The House will also recall that on 20th August the Prime Minister stated that His Majesty's Government will do their best to encourage the building-up of reserves of food all over the world for the relief of the countries of Europe once these have been wholly cleared of German forces and have genuinely regained their freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: Countries are freed from German occupation/forces — liberation from foreign military control and domination, a classical case of freedom from external interference and oppression.

records.speaker: Mr. Gordon Macdonald
records.sentence: Since that will involve legislation I wonder to what extent we are at liberty to discuss the statement.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "at liberty to discuss" is a parliamentary procedural expression asking whether the speaker is permitted to comment on a statement, not a substantive claim about liberty-as-a-value.

records.speaker: The Under-Secretary of State for Scotland
records.sentence: Occupiers and others are at liberty to preserve and sell mole skins.
records.haiku_rationale: Occupiers and others have permission to preserve and sell mole skins; "at liberty to" is a parliamentary idiom meaning "permitted to engage in" an economic activity without restriction or prohibition.

records.speaker: Colonel Llewellin
records.sentence: My Noble Friend has asked the association to let us keep him, but eventually, of course, he may go back and he is at liberty to do so.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "at liberty to do so" (return) is parliamentary procedural language meaning he is permitted or not prevented from returning, referring to freedom from constraint, not empowerment to return.

records.speaker: Mr. Burgin
records.sentence: One of our difficulties in this freedom-loving land, where anybody could start a business as he wished and carry it on with individual enterprise in his own way, is that there is no index to industrial knowledge, industrial production and industrial distribution.
records.haiku_rationale: Businesses are freed from regulatory constraint to start and operate "as he wished" with "individual enterprise in his own way" — negative liberty from interference in economic activity.

records.speaker: Mr. James Griffiths
records.sentence: I would take the liberty of speaking on behalf of my colleagues in the trade union movement, and the pioneers who have spent generations in trying to stop Sunday work.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "take the liberty of speaking" is parliamentary procedural language (permission/license to act) and does not invoke liberty as a value substantively. The sentence uses "liberty" as an idiom for "permission to proceed," not as a philosophical claim about freedom.

records.speaker: Mr. Radford
records.sentence: Is it right, with losses to civilian life of men, women and children continually taking place, that we should keep at liberty a woman who has deliberately signalled to German airmen when raiding Southampton?
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker uses "at liberty" in the parliamentary idiom meaning "at large" or "free from detention"; the question concerns whether to detain (or not keep at liberty) a woman accused of signalling to enemy aircraft. This is a claim about freedom from interference with detention/confinement, specifically negative liberty.

records.speaker: Unknown
records.sentence: the maintenance after the war of sufficient armed strength to make effective the will of the nations resolved to preserve peace and freedom;
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence uses "freedom" as an abstract value to be preserved through military strength. It is not specifying freedom from or to a particular constraint or capacity—"freedom" appears as an end-goal alongside "peace" that armed strength will help preserve. This is too general and under-specified to determine whether it refers to negative liberty (freedom from oppression/interference) or positive liberty (empowerment to govern or act).

records.speaker: Mr. Loftus
records.sentence: That is why it is so essential that this House should keep control over the liberty of its Members.
records.haiku_rationale: The House must retain control over its Members' liberty (freedom from external interference in their parliamentary debate and conduct).

records.speaker: Sir G. Jeffreys
records.sentence: I believe that India's heart would warm to us in the measure that we gave freedom to India.
records.haiku_rationale: India is freed to govern itself; the speaker advocates empowering India (positive liberty—granting autonomy/self-determination), not merely removing interference.

records.speaker: Mr. Noel-Baker
records.sentence: Political freedom takes another form in the West African and other Colonies, namely, the progressive organisation of indirect rule and of local government through tribal chiefs.
records.haiku_rationale: Political freedom is being realized through the progressive organisation of local government and indirect rule through tribal chiefs—an empowerment and capacity structure enabling self-governance, not merely removal of interference.

records.speaker: Mr. Wedgwood
records.sentence: I do not think it should be the exclusive privilege of a Britisher to die in the defence of liberty.
records.haiku_rationale: A Britisher is freed to die in defence of liberty (empowered capacity to participate equally in defending a value/cause), not from external interference; the speaker argues against exclusive privilege, seeking to extend participatory opportunity.

records.speaker: Mr. Bevan
records.sentence: Therefore, there is no argument here for liberty in the abstract.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker rejects an abstract appeal to liberty as a valid argument in the context at hand; the specific object of freedom is unspecified, and the sentence merely negates a general appeal to an undefined concept of liberty.

records.speaker: Petty-Officer Herbert
records.sentence:
The first and

most important in principle of freedom is freedom of the person.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence asserts that "freedom of the person" is the most important principle of freedom—a foundational invocation of personal liberty as freedom from interference or restraint on one's person and bodily integrity.

records.speaker: Petty-Officer Herbert
records.sentence: Fourthly, there is freedom of contract: Is there anybody in this House who would say that the institution of freedom of contract has to be preserved in a permanent and inviolable condition for the rest of the war?
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of contract is being freed (preserved) from wartime restriction; this invokes negative liberty—freedom from interference with the ability to make binding agreements.

records.speaker: Mr. Greenwood
records.sentence: I am certain that the spirit or the people will be strengthened and their hearts encouraged by the knowledge that the United Nations mean what they say—some doubts have been expressed about it, but I accept that the United Nations mean all they say —and that the purpose of the war is to plant freedom and justice firmly in the world.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom being "planted" in the world as a goal of war is an invocation of liberty as a cause opposed to oppression and tyranny—a claim about freedom from foreign domination and authoritarianism, characteristic of negative liberty rhetoric.

records.speaker: Sir S. Cripps
records.sentence: Member so regards it, he is at liberty to put down an Amendment.
records.haiku_rationale: A member is permitted to put down an amendment—this is parliamentary procedure giving permission to act within the formal rules of debate; "at liberty" here means procedurally allowed to do something, not a claim about freedom-as-a-value against interference or oppression.

records.speaker: Unknown
records.sentence:
And in his "Ode to Liberty," he wrote:
 The palsied arm of tottering, powerless age.
records.haiku_rationale: This is a poetic quotation with no substantive claim about liberty-as-a-value; it merely quotes a literary work titled "Ode to Liberty" without making an argument about freedom from or to anything.

records.speaker: Mr. Creech Jones
records.sentence: I want to stress that the corollary of this considerable contribution from the Colonial peoples to our present struggle for freedom and civilisation is our responsibility for bringing them more rapidly to political maturity and social and economic prosperity.
records.haiku_rationale: The "struggle for freedom and civilisation" is being waged against external threat (Axis powers) and is opposed to oppression; bringing colonial peoples to "political maturity" and "prosperity" is an empowering project of social and economic development that enables capacity and self-governance.

records.speaker: Mr. Sorensen
records.sentence: Do I understand that it is out of Order now to speak of Indian freedom?
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "Indian freedom" invokes freedom from colonial rule and foreign interference—a freedom that is being claimed as a value and as potentially subject to parliamentary order.

records.speaker: Sir W. Allen
records.sentence: Surely I am at liberty to reply to the hon.
records.haiku_rationale: Parliamentary procedure: speaker asserting procedural right to respond in debate; "at liberty" is a formulaic procedural expression, not a substantive claim about freedom as a political value.

records.speaker: Mr. Shinwell
records.sentence: Is it not important also to know whether, if the United States are going to build faster ships, which are so important to our war purposes, we are to get a proper supply and not get ships that were built under the Liberty programme and which are of lower speed?
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is concerned about obtaining adequate material supplies (ships) of sufficient quality for the war effort. "Liberty programme" refers to the US Liberty ship construction program (a proper noun and historical program name), not freedom-as-a-value. The sentence is about procurement and supply logistics, not about liberty or freedom as a political principle.

records.speaker: Mr. Collindridge
records.sentence: I would appeal to those who will be merged from the borough forces to use this legislation, but I do hope that to them, and to all police, there will be granted at some date hot far distant that liberty which hitherto the county borough police have had, of watch committee or standing joint committee consideration accompanied by right of appeal to the Home Secretary.
records.haiku_rationale: Police are being freed from some form of oversight by gaining the right to watch committee or standing joint committee consideration with appeal to Home Secretary – this describes empowerment to have their grievances heard and considered by specific bodies, an enabling institutional capacity.

records.speaker: Mr. Butler
records.sentence: In my answer of 14th February I drew attention to the fact that the local education authority was at liberty to seek a site for this purpose if so desired and there would be no difficulty in principle, and I hope that due publicity has been given to that.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "was at liberty to seek a site" is a parliamentary procedural expression meaning the local education authority had the option/permission to seek a site; it does not substantively invoke liberty as a value concerning freedom from interference or empowerment in a policy sense.

records.speaker: Sir Robert Rankin
records.sentence: And let us give, so far as is possible in war-time, liberty and freedom of action to those merchants who in most difficult days are carrying on the commerce of the West Indies.
records.haiku_rationale: Merchants are being freed from wartime restrictions to act in commerce—they are granted capacity/empowerment to conduct trade despite wartime constraints.

records.speaker: Viscount Hinchingbrooke
records.sentence: The Commission is perfectly at liberty to make any series of inquiries that it thinks fit.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "at liberty to make inquiries" describes a permitted or empowered capacity to act without restriction, but this is procedural language in a legislative context referring to what an institutional body is permitted to do, not a substantive claim about liberty as a political value.

records.speaker: Sir George Schuster
records.sentence: And remember these men are just as fervent patriots and just as anxious for the advance to freedom of their country as those who incited the mobs to attack them.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence refers to "freedom of their country" — national or collective independence/self-governance, what the country is being freed to become (advance toward), not freedom from state interference with individual rights.

records.speaker: Mr. Brown
records.sentence: I know—and I am going to be a little pointed—that since I raised this case in the House of Commons the Board of Trade have issued a new Order, which is perhaps the best justification for my raising the question, taking away the freedom of local people to make this kind of appointment.
records.haiku_rationale: The Board of Trade's new Order is taking away (removing) the freedom of local people to make a specific kind of appointment—a capacity/power previously held by them. This is the loss of an empowerment to act, making it positive liberty being constrained.

records.speaker: Mr. John Dugdale
records.sentence:
] 
I am all for freedom of speech, and I do not say that I hold Mr.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes freedom of speech, which is freedom from interference with expression and debate—a classic negative liberty.

records.speaker: Mr. David Adams
records.sentence: If we are to have greater freedom of trade and greater planning in industry, it is time that we anticipated the urgent needs that will present themselves as far as the export and import trade of this country is concerned.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "greater freedom of trade" as a value to be advanced, meaning freedom from government restrictions on commerce—a classic negative liberty claim about non-interference with trading activity.

records.speaker: Mr. Dugdale
records.sentence: I would ask that those liberties which we prize, that particular liberty which we prize so highly in this country, should be given to the West Indies and given without delay.
records.haiku_rationale: Liberties (understood as self-governance/democratic rights) that the UK prizes are being "given" to the West Indies—an empowerment to govern themselves, parallel to granting a nation capacity for self-determination.

records.speaker: Mr. Messer
records.sentence:
When dealing with old age pensioners we are dealing with people who have had a period of employment in their lives and


freedom and independence.
records.haiku_rationale: People (old age pensioners) are being freed to achieve or maintain independence and self-sufficiency—this names a capacity they should have rather than freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Mr. Creech Jones
records.sentence:
The efficiency of the Service has undoubtedly suffered in consequence 
not only in that direction but in others, and the freedom of the Secretary of State to secure the maximum efficiency has been impeded.
records.haiku_rationale: The freedom being constrained is the Secretary of State's capacity to achieve maximum efficiency; the impediment is removal of his ability to take action toward a goal, not freedom from external interference with a fundamental right.

records.speaker: Dr. Thomas
records.sentence: As one who is a lover of liberty, as my right hon.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence is a rhetorical self-description ("lover of liberty") without specifying any substantive claim about what is being freed, from what, or to what. It is a bare invocation of liberty as a value and cause, characteristic of pre-substantive parliamentary framing.

records.speaker: Mr. Foot
records.sentence: Nothing whatever is said on the freedom of movement from one part of the country to another.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of movement (from one part of the country to another) is a classic freedom-FROM-interference; the sentence criticizes the absence of any protection for this liberty.

records.speaker: Mr. Arthur Greenwood
records.sentence: I realise that great nations engaged in a common war for freedom must have their differences, even under the pressure of that common war, and I appreciate that when the struggle is over there are possibilities of differences arising between.
records.haiku_rationale: Nations are engaged in a common war *for* freedom — freedom from tyranny/fascism/oppression — the object being freedom from enemy control and domination.

records.speaker: Sir L. Lyle
records.sentence: Gentleman consider suggesting to the Home Secretary that he should join the National League for Freedom?
records.haiku_rationale: A speaker is suggesting that the Home Secretary join the National League for Freedom—an organizational commitment to a political cause, not a specification of what is being freed or from/to what.

records.speaker: Mr. Peake
records.sentence: We have had to steer between the abuses which would result, on the one hand, from giving the Service voter complete freedom of choice in the matter of choosing a constituency in which to vote, and, on the other hand, the large number of serving men who would be disfranchised if we tied the matter up too tightly.
records.haiku_rationale: Service voters' freedom of choice in selecting a constituency is being constrained by regulation to avoid both abuse (from too much freedom) and disfranchisement (from too little)—a balancing of negative liberty with practical constraints.

records.speaker: Mr. Cove
records.sentence: Every resolution of Congress was on the side of the freedom of nations.
records.haiku_rationale: Nations are being freed from external interference in self-governance and determination of their own affairs.

records.speaker: The Prime Minister
records.sentence: Until the Greek people can express their will in conditions of freedom and tranquillity, it is the settled policy of His Majesty's Government to support the King of the Hellenes, who is at once our loyal Ally and the constitutional head of the Greek State.
records.haiku_rationale: The Greek people are freed (enabled) to express their will—to exercise political agency and self-determination—under conditions free from external interference and disturbance.

records.speaker: Mr. Magnay
records.sentence: We started fighting for freedom first.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes freedom as a value/cause that motivates fighting and resistance, without specifying a particular domain or capability—a rhetorical invocation of liberty as opposed to tyranny/oppression.

records.speaker: Major Lloyd
records.sentence: But what does liberty mean?
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence poses a bare, definitional question about the meaning of "liberty" without specifying what is being freed or from/to what.

records.speaker: Professor Gruffydd
records.sentence: They are now to be handed over lock, stock and barrel to the tender mercies of the local authority and any vestiges of individual freedom which they had in the past will be taken from them.
records.haiku_rationale: Individual freedom (specifically freedom from interference by local authorities in managing schools) is being removed or taken away from individuals, making this a loss of negative liberty.

records.speaker: Lieut.-Colonel Sir Assheton Pownall
records.sentence: There has for some time been an interesting report in the Library, from part of which we are not at liberty to quote.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "not at liberty to quote" is a parliamentary idiom meaning "not permitted" or "not able to proceed with"; it refers to procedural constraint on quoting, not a normative claim about freedom as a value.

records.speaker: The Deputy-Chairman
records.sentence: To say merely that they came back strengthened in their ideas of liberty, would be in Order.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "ideas of liberty" refers to convictions or concepts about freedom from interference and restraint, characteristic of negative liberty discourse in rhetorical contexts.

records.speaker: Mr. Loftus
records.sentence: First, I would suggest that wherever we find in Europe a Government, whether an  emigré  Government or not, which before the war was generally accepted by the people, a respected Government giving political liberty and individual freedom, we should, when its country is liberated from the Germans, support it for the time being.
records.haiku_rationale: A government that gives "political liberty and individual freedom" to its people is being praised as a worthy recipient of support; the speaker is commending governments that enable or respect personal and political freedoms.

records.speaker: Mr. Jewson
records.sentence: Therefore, within the framework of this system which we are trying to create, we must see that the individual has his freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The individual is being freed to have freedom itself—empowered to exercise agency and autonomy within a created system, rather than protected from specific interference.

records.speaker: Mr. Silkin
records.sentence: I think they ought to have freedom in the general policy and management of the hospitals, but I think they must be subject to a certain amount of public control, and I feel that the voluntary hospitals will have to face that fact.
records.haiku_rationale: Voluntary hospitals are to be freed (empowered) to make decisions about general policy and management, but within constraints of public oversight—a mixed claim presenting both enabling autonomy and limiting supervision.

records.speaker: The Prime Minister
records.sentence: I may say, however, that at the end of the war, when medals are struck, every one who has worn the King's uniform and served in uniformed, disciplined Services, will, I presume—I say "presume" because the matter may not rest with His Majesty's present advisers—receive a Victory Medal to commemorate this great struggle for human freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence frames the war as a "struggle for human freedom" (freedom from Nazi tyranny/oppression), using rhetorical invocation of liberty as a cause opposed to totalitarianism—a paradigmatic negative liberty appeal.

records.speaker: Professor Savory
records.sentence: We are entitled to freedom as well as unity—and there is no more important matter in which that freedom can be exercised, than in the choice of peace or war.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom to choose (whether to pursue peace or war) is an empowering capacity granted to a political body—this is positive liberty, the freedom to do something consequential.

records.speaker: Sir J. Grigg
records.sentence:
] 
What he had in mind was their freedom to be adopted as candidates, and also that the Government would have to make provision for the soldier to be allowed to exercise his franchise in some way or other.
records.haiku_rationale: The freedom being discussed is soldiers' capacity to exercise their franchise (vote) and to be adopted as candidates—empowerment to do certain things rather than freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Mr. Salt
records.sentence:
In asking for that, and showing my appreciation of the work done, I hope that the same freedom

will be given to private enterprise, so that they can also work on their own.
records.haiku_rationale: Private enterprise is being freed TO work on their own (empowered to operate independently), which is a capacity to act without external constraint.

records.speaker: Mr. Wedderburn
records.sentence: I do not think there is any example of any other country, certainly not any European country, which has deliberately conferred sovereignty aid freedom on any of its dependent possessions as we have done in South Africa, in Ireland, in Egypt and in Mesopotamia.
records.haiku_rationale: Sovereignty and freedom are conferred (empowered) upon dependent territories—this is about granting self-governance capacity to formerly subordinate possessions.

records.speaker: Mr. Ede
records.sentence: I believe that the Minister's efforts to understand everybody else's point of view, and to give, as far as possible, a spirit of co-operation to this Bill, has been welcomed by the country, which desires to see how this greater measure of liberty can, in fact, be worked in this country.
records.haiku_rationale: The country desires to see how "greater measure of liberty" can be "worked" or realized in practice — this refers to the capacity/opportunity to exercise or implement freedom, not freedom from a specific constraint. The sentence treats liberty as an empowered state or condition to be achieved and made practical.

records.speaker: The Prime Minister
records.sentence: It will long be honoured in history, and I am sure that children will read the romance of this struggle and will have imprinted on their minds that love of freedom, that readiness to give away life and comfort, and all there is around one, in order to gain the right to live unmolested on your native heath.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom here is the right to live unmolested on one's native heath—freedom from interference with one's life, home, and existence. This is negative liberty: freedom from external constraint and molestation.

records.speaker: Commander Sir Archibald Southby
records.sentence: Whatever our individual views may be regarding Regulation 18B, there can be no doubt whatever that, as matters now stand, there is no judicial safeguard for the liberty of the subject against the arbitrary acts of the Executive.
records.haiku_rationale: The object of freedom is "the liberty of the subject" (protection from arbitrary executive interference); what is lacking is a judicial safeguard—a mechanism to prevent interference. This is negative liberty: freedom from arbitrary executive action.

records.speaker: Mr. Hely-Hutchinson
records.sentence:
If we examine the nature and causes of unemployment it can be shown in theory that the only effective technique in the prevention of unemploy-

ment which a Government can employ is interference with individual freedom of choice—that is to say interference with private enterprise—and not only can we show it in theory but also we have seen it in practice in the last 10 or 20 years.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence claims that preventing unemployment requires government interference with individual freedom of choice and private enterprise—freedom FROM interference with business decisions and economic activity.

records.speaker: Mr. Pethick-Lawrence
records.sentence: In fact, these paragraphs owe their origin entirely to the Treasury, but I think that in some respects they are difficult because they deal with a highly technical subject-matter and because the authors of these paragraphs move in those particular regions with a freedom and an agility which I confess I sometimes view rather with alarm, because I move in them somewhat laboriously and with faltering steps.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker uses "freedom and agility" to describe the movement of the Treasury authors through technical subject-matter—a metaphorical freedom of movement/operation, not a claim about a fundamental liberty-as-a-value.

records.speaker: Mr. Hogg
records.sentence: There is no such thing as absolute freedom or absolute tyranny.
records.haiku_rationale: This is a philosophical claim about the non-existence of absolute states, not a substantive claim about what people are freed from or empowered to do; it names no specific object of freedom nor specifies any constraint or enabling capacity.

records.speaker: Commander Sir Archibald Southby
records.sentence: Running through all of them has been an increasing insistence upon the importance of the individual freedom of the citizen.
records.haiku_rationale: The citizen's freedom from interference or constraint; the sentence asserts the importance of non-interference with individual agency, resonating with classic negative liberty concerns about protecting citizens from external control.

records.speaker: Mr. Silkin
records.sentence: It recognises that local authorities will need greater freedom and financial assistance, but it does not provide them, substantially, with that freedom, and certainly does not provide them with the financial assistance.
records.haiku_rationale: Local authorities are being freed (or denied freedom) to act independently in governance and resource allocation—a positive liberty about empowerment and capacity to self-govern.

records.speaker: Captain Gammans
records.sentence:
In the spirit of restoring liberty to their fellow British subjects, or


having it dinned into their ears that these people stabbed their comrades in the back at a vital stage of the war?
records.haiku_rationale: Restoring liberty to fellow British subjects means empowering them to govern themselves and exercise self-determination, freed from occupation or external domination — a positive liberty claim about enabling a people's capacity for self-rule.

records.speaker: Mr. Godfrey Nicholson
records.sentence: I think we have to consider how far the Cripps offer and the methods tried so far can constitute the only means by which we hope to bring India her freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: India is being freed from colonial rule—this is about empowering India to govern itself (self-determination), not about removing interference with an existing capacity.

records.speaker: Mr. Quintin Hogg
records.sentence: We should not be able to assist them even if it were consistent with our own independence and freedom to do so.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence concerns freedom (capacity) of a nation to act—specifically the freedom to assist another party—constrained by consistency with national independence.

records.speaker: Mr. Law
records.sentence: There is nothing against a man's liberty in the fact that two men in the same office have the same job at different rates of pay—I think the most one would say is that it is an indication of a not very well run office.
records.haiku_rationale: The statement defends a man's liberty (freedom from interference in employment conditions) against the objection that differential pay for the same job violates it—claiming pay disparity is a management issue, not a liberty issue.

records.speaker: Mr. Shinwell
records.sentence: It has been said that they expect at the close of the war to have a merchant fleet—Liberty ships, emergency ships and Victory ships—of, say, between 30,000,000 and 40,000,000 tons.
records.haiku_rationale: "Liberty ships" is a proper noun referring to a class of merchant vessel produced during WWII; "liberty" here appears incidentally as part of a ship name, not as a substantive claim about freedom-as-a-value.

records.speaker: Mr. Alexander
records.sentence: Such an adjustment in naval building for this purpose, however, might prove difficult, because the very principle implies a long-term naval programme, with complete freedom to the Admiralty, subject, of course, to the Cabinet's consent, to accelerate or retard it as required, but, as Parliament, rightly I think, always wishes to, and does, control naval building in peace-time, such a long-term programme may be difficult to achieve.
records.haiku_rationale: The Admiralty is being granted freedom to accelerate or retard a naval building programme—freedom to make operational decisions; this is an empowerment to act on discretionary judgment.

records.speaker: Sir W. Smithers
records.sentence: That paragraph is one of the gleams of light in the whole proposal, for here the Government, composed of members of all parties, admit that capitalism, private enterprise, individual freedom, has been the reason of our success in the past;
records.haiku_rationale: Individual freedom (understood as absence of state interference in economic and private affairs) is identified as the historical cause of national success; this invokes freedom from constraint, particularly from collectivist or state control.

records.speaker: Mr. James Griffiths
records.sentence: The second principle is the principle which the Government have laid down in the Atlantic Charter, that they were determined, with the other nations and Governments associated with them, to establish freedom from want.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence identifies "freedom from want" as the object of freedom, explicitly naming what is being freed from (want/deprivation). This is a classic negative liberty formulation: freedom from an undesired condition or constraint.

records.speaker: Mr. James Griffiths
records.sentence: If we are to achieve freedom from want and full social security, we shall have to lay down a new economic foundation in this country, and that can only be done in a planned economy in which the resources of the nation, material and human, are used for national and not private needs.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence articulates "freedom from want" — being freed from deprivation — which is a classic negative liberty formulation, even though achieving it requires building new economic structures (which are presented as the instrumental means, not the object of freedom itself).

records.speaker: The Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs
records.sentence:
It has now been reported from Cairo that the two prisoners have made the following confession:
 We are members of the Fighters for the Freedom of Israel organisation and what we have done was done on the instructions of this organisation.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "Freedom of Israel" is a proper noun—the name of an organization (Fighters for the Freedom of Israel)—not a substantive claim about liberty as a value or principle.

records.speaker: Mr. Price
records.sentence: The Poles themselves fought heroically in the great rebellion of 1863 for a freedom which they could not give themselves.
records.haiku_rationale: The Poles are being freed from Russian imperial rule/oppression (negative liberty from external domination), but the sentence emphasizes that they lacked the capacity to achieve this liberation themselves—they could not empower themselves to govern independently (positive liberty capacity).

records.speaker: Mr. Stokes
records.sentence: There we have two small nations who are looking to us to fulfil the guarantee which so many nations have now given—there were some 14 or 15 mentioned by the Foreign Secretary yesterday—as to their future liberty and independence, and they are very anxious lest we shall let them down.
records.haiku_rationale: The small nations are being freed to self-governance and independence (positive liberty) rather than freed from specific interference. The guarantee concerns their capacity to govern themselves and determine their own future, not protection from particular constraints.

records.speaker: Sir A. Evans
records.sentence: "] I say that advisedly, because at bases in this country, when these young girls get their leave they can enjoy it in circumstances of complete freedom and go where they like.
records.haiku_rationale: Young girls are freed (from constraints on their movement and choice of where to go) to enjoy their leave and "go where they like."

records.speaker: Mr. Gallacher
records.sentence:
If there is to be freedom for local authorities to do their


job, there will have to be control over loans, and the rate of interest that they have to pay.
records.haiku_rationale: Local authorities are being empowered (given capacity) to do their job through financial control mechanisms (loans and interest rates), indicating positive liberty—freedom to act, not merely freedom from interference.

records.speaker: The Solicitor-General
records.sentence:
Surely the best way of marrying those two ideas is to say, We are at liberty to provide part


of your remuneration by giving lodging but the revaluation of that must be with the independent wages council.
records.haiku_rationale: This is parliamentary procedure language: "at liberty to" is an idiomatic phrase meaning "permitted to" or "allowed to" in the context of what a wages council may do, not a substantive claim about freedom-as-a-value.

records.speaker: Colonel Stanley
records.sentence: It means that more and more paper work is put upon the Governor, thereby keeping from him freedom to tour and see for himself, for other people to see him and have the chance of expressing their views to him.
records.haiku_rationale: The Governor is kept from freedom to tour and personally see constituents and hear their views—freedom from bureaucratic constraint that enables executive capacity to govern effectively and maintain direct contact with the people.

records.speaker: The Prime Minister
records.sentence: For more than a year past, and since the tide of war has turned so strongly against Germany, the Polish problem has been divided into two main issues—the frontiers of Poland and the freedom of Poland.
records.haiku_rationale: Poland is freed from German domination/occupation—empowerment of a nation-state to govern itself independently, which is positive liberty, but the abstract invocation of "freedom of Poland" as a national cause opposed to foreign control is also a core negative liberty concept (freedom from external rule).

records.speaker: Mr. Harold Nicolson
records.sentence:
" 
The Prime Minister has simplified the matter and clarified our minds very much by dividing the problem into its two main compartments of frontiers and liberty.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence mentions "liberty" as one of two key policy compartments (alongside "frontiers") that the Prime Minister has divided; liberty is referenced as a substantive issue to be addressed, but no specific claim is made about what freedom from or capacity to do something it means.

records.speaker: Mr. Gallacher
records.sentence: These Members have never at any time before been apostles of democracy or freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence makes a rhetorical claim about certain Members never having been advocates ("apostles") of democracy or freedom as a political value opposed to authoritarianism or constraint, but does not specify what is being freed or from-or-to what.

records.speaker: Commander Sir Archibald Southby
records.sentence: They find democracy in alliance with Communism in order to accomplish the overthrow of Nazism, and they fear and suspect—not without cause—the sacrifice of those democratic principles upon which alone man's freedom can be rooted and secured.
records.haiku_rationale: Man's freedom is rooted in and secured by democratic principles; the concern is sacrifice of those enabling democratic structures, not interference with specific freedoms themselves.

records.speaker: Dr. Summerskill
records.sentence: He has lost that freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The specific object of freedom is unclear from this bare pronoun reference; without prior context establishing what freedom is being discussed, it is impossible to determine whether this refers to a negative liberty (freedom from interference) or a positive liberty (empowerment/capacity), making this ambiguous.

records.speaker: Mr. Amery
records.sentence: The first is that no limit is set to India's freedom to decide for herself her own destiny, whether as a free member and partner in the British Commonwealth or even without it.
records.haiku_rationale: India is freed to decide/determine her own destiny (self-governance) — empowerment to choose her political status and form of government.

records.speaker: Mr. Clement Davies
records.sentence: If anybody is entitled to a decent home it is the boy who has fought for the liberty of his country.
records.haiku_rationale: The subject is fighting soldiers freed from tyranny/oppression in defense of national independence, a rhetorical invocation of negative liberty as a cause opposed to authoritarian rule.

records.speaker: Mr. Morrison
records.sentence: Freedom is not an abstract thing.
records.haiku_rationale: This is a bare philosophical claim about the nature of liberty itself, not specifying what is being freed from or toward what.

records.speaker: Mr. Popplewell
records.sentence: The freedom to exploit our people in industry is decidedly on the wane, while the freedom is growing for our people to enjoy a reasonable measure of protection and to know that they are assured at long last, should they lose a limb or an arm or suffer some injury which requires a surgical appliance, that there will not be tremendous delay and playing about with National Health Insurance and approved societies and suchlike.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence contrasts two freedoms: declining freedom for industrialists to exploit workers (negative liberty from state/regulatory interference) versus growing freedom for workers to enjoy protection and swift access to healthcare (positive liberty — an empowered capacity to receive benefits and avoid harm).

records.speaker: Mr. Bevin
records.sentence: Another thing that has handicapped us is that, owing to the destruction of all freedom in Germany, it did not matter what we told them;
records.haiku_rationale: The German people have been freed from something (all freedom in Germany has been destroyed), and the speaker is lamenting the absence of that state—the loss of the capacity to exercise choice or self-determination in communicating with them.

records.speaker: The Prime Minister
records.sentence: Hitler, like the Kaiser before him, learned that there are bonds of the spirit much stronger and more enduring than any material ties, and that freedom units more thoroughly than domination.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom (as a spiritual and moral force) unites people more thoroughly than domination does—freedom is presented as an enabling, cohesive capacity that binds communities together in contrast to coercive control.

records.speaker: Major Conant
records.sentence: I regard it of tremendous importance to everyone who has the liberty of the individual at heart.
records.haiku_rationale: The liberty of the individual is being protected from interference or constraint; "liberty of the individual" is a core negative liberty concept referring to freedom from external compulsion or control.

records.speaker: The Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs
records.sentence: And do remember this—I make this plain because sometimes we are lectured about it—in the British Empire, we gave freedom where it did not exist before, by the development of the Commonwealth.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker claims that Britain gave freedom (positive liberty—empowerment to self-govern) to territories in the Empire through Commonwealth development, granting subject peoples the capacity to govern themselves.

records.speaker: Dr. Corlett
records.sentence: we have complete freedom to express ourselves as we wish.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of expression (to express ourselves as we wish) is freedom from interference with one's speech and self-expression.

records.speaker: Dr. Corlett
records.sentence:
Recently the Headmistresses Association sent out a question-aire to ask the headmistresses whether


they felt there was any lack of freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: Headmistresses are asked whether they perceived a lack of freedom, but the sentence does not specify what freedom is at issue—freedom from administrative interference, freedom to set curriculum, freedom to hire staff, etc. The referent and direction (from/to what) remain unspecified.

records.speaker: Mr. Hopkin Morris
records.sentence: Member, on whatever side of the House he sits, who believes in the liberty of the subject and in the keeping of contracts between employers and employed, that the breaking of an ordinary contract of this kind should be subject to the penalties of the criminal law.
records.haiku_rationale: Liberty of the subject (the object of freedom) is being protected from interference with contractual rights and criminal penalties—a classic invocation of negative liberty against state coercion.

records.speaker: Mr. Foot
records.sentence: We have had many speeches and Debates in this House about freedom to print.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "freedom to print" refers to freedom from interference with printing—a traditional civil liberty protecting the press from censorship and restraint.

records.speaker: Sir W. Darling
records.sentence: This Bill is not for liberty.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker denies that the Bill advances liberty in general; the sentence negates a claim about freedom as a cause, opposing something to liberty without specifying what is being freed or from what.

records.speaker: The Under-Secretary of State for the Home Department
records.sentence: Many of the Regulations which appear in the First Schedule are in the nature not so much of restrictions of liberty as of enlargements of it.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker characterizes regulations as "enlargements of liberty" rather than restrictions—claiming they expand the capacity of individuals to act (positive liberty through empowerment), not merely remove interference.

records.speaker: Mr. Maude
records.sentence: Gentleman was introducing the Bill, he told us about the increase of liberty to be gained by the Regulations.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker describes "increase of liberty to be gained by the Regulations" — the Regulations are portrayed as conferring or enabling a capacity, suggesting empowerment to act rather than mere removal of interference.

records.speaker: Mr. Tiffany
records.sentence: We had the fullest freedom to enter any part of Yugoslavia, and no let or hindrance was placed in our way.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker describes having freedom from obstruction or constraint to enter any part of Yugoslavia without impediment—a negative liberty (freedom from interference or restriction on movement).

records.speaker: Unknown
records.sentence: I see very little likelihood at present of professional men being able to move about from one employer to another with the freedom which we used to know under Tory Government before the war.
records.haiku_rationale: Professional men are being freed to move between employers; this concerns their capacity and opportunity to change employment, enabling them to act without constraint.

records.speaker: Mr. Piratin
records.sentence: Member had had that kind of experience in the pre-1939 days he would not call it freedom so glibly as he has done in speaking on this Motion of Censure.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom is invoked as a rhetorical ideal opposed to the oppression and hardship of pre-1939 days, making a claim about freedom from interference and want.

records.speaker: Sir S. Cripps
records.sentence: It is, there fore, a good argument—I am not going into it—to say that preferences were intended to be dealt with under this elimination, but it appears not to matter either one way or the other because we are at liberty to say, "We 'will reduce preferences," or, "We will not," or "We will eliminate preferences" or "We will not eliminate preferences" according to what we get offered in exchange by other Powers.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is describing parliamentary discretion regarding preferences in trade negotiations—freedom from procedural constraint to take various policy positions.

records.speaker: Mr. Strachey
records.sentence: Broadly speaking, the rule as set out in the two relevant paragraphs of King's Regulations, 1072 and 1073, is that an airman or officer is at liberty to write letters to the Press so long as his letters do not concern the Service in any way.
records.haiku_rationale: An airman or officer is at liberty to write letters to the Press (freedom of expression/press) so long as his letters do not concern the Service.

records.speaker: Sir S. Cripps
records.sentence: He has complete and absolute liberty as to the settlement to which he comes and, moreover, it is clear that he is bargaining a preference from which another person gets the benefit.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is referring to someone's freedom/capacity to reach a settlement of his own choosing—what settlement he comes to is his decision. This is an empowered capacity to act (make a choice), not freedom from interference.

records.speaker: The President of the Board of Trade
records.sentence: To that end, they shall include provision for agreed action by the United States of America and the United Kingdom, open to participation by all other countries of like mind, directed to the expansion, by appropriate international and domestic measures, of production, employment, and the exchange and consumption of goods, which are the material foundations of the liberty and welfare of all peoples;
records.haiku_rationale: Liberty here is presented as a material foundation enabled by expanded production, employment, and economic exchange—a positive capacity or condition of wellbeing that requires enabling measures, not merely freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Mr. Foot
records.sentence: I believe it would be perfectly proper on the part of the Government, in the interests of liberty, when they are disposing of this newsprint, to say that the newsprint increase of supplies shall go to provincial and weekly newspapers and that special consideration shall be given to those newspapers which can show that they are not tied up with any combine and to cases where a provincial newspaper is a genuine provincial newspaper, run by the people in that city.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom for provincial and weekly newspapers from being tied to combines and from centralized control, enabling them to operate independently.

records.speaker: Mr. Lennox-Boyd
records.sentence: Gentleman whether we have or have not agreed to sign the Fifth Freedom, as we would like a definite answer on that subject;
records.haiku_rationale: The reference is to the "Fifth Freedom" (a Cold War-era term denoting freedom of the seas or trade rights), framed as a matter of international agreement/commitment that Parliament may or may not sign; this invokes liberty as a value in diplomatic/geopolitical context, describing freedom from interference with commerce or movement, but the sentence itself does not specify the substance clearly enough to distinguish positive from negative liberty—it merely asks for a position on whether Britain will commit to a named international freedom.

records.speaker: Captain Gunter
records.sentence: I submit, in consideration of this operation of the Act, that the minority have always had freedom of expression, and in my experience have not failed to use it.
records.haiku_rationale: The freedom being asserted is freedom of expression—a classic negative liberty protecting non-interference with the act of expressing oneself. The speaker claims the minority have possessed this freedom (from interference) and exercised it.

records.speaker: Mr. House
records.sentence: I am asking, on behalf of the injured workman, that he shall have freedom of choice, but the freedom of choice which I am seeking for him is that the injured person shall be able to attend either a registered medical practitioner, on the one hand, who is generally described as an orthodox practitioner, or, on the other hand, an unorthodox practitioner.
records.haiku_rationale: The injured workman is being empowered to choose between registered and unorthodox medical practitioners—this is freedom-to (capacity/opportunity to select among options), not freedom-from interference.

records.speaker: Sir Peter Bennett
records.sentence: I want to see economic freedom given to the young men to go out and adventure and rebuild the industries which in time are bound to die I do not want to see them frozen by control or Government action.
records.haiku_rationale: Economic freedom is being given to young men as an empowered capacity to venture out and rebuild industries—freedom to act and compete—as opposed to being frozen by control or government action.

records.speaker: Mrs. Nichol
records.sentence: The task which will exercise the Ministers who are to go to India shortly is that of obtaining the full cooperation of the Indians, which will in the end give her freedom and keep her friendship for this country in perpetuity.
records.haiku_rationale: India is freed to self-governance and independence, which empowers her to act as a nation capable of maintaining friendly relations—this is positive liberty granting India the capacity to govern itself.

records.speaker: The Prime Minister
records.sentence: Is it any wonder that today she claims—as a nation of 400,000,000 people that has twice sent her sons to die for freedom—that she should herself have freedom to decide her own destiny?
records.haiku_rationale: A nation (India) is being freed to self-govern and decide its own destiny—an empowerment to autonomous self-determination, not a removal of external constraints on an existing capacity.

records.speaker: Mr. Willink
records.sentence: The system under which they will have to work will be a definite limitation on the freedom of the choice of doctor.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence describes a system that limits freedom of choice regarding doctor selection—a constraint on the capacity to choose one's own healthcare provider.

records.speaker: Commander Galbraith
records.sentence: Gentleman, when he talked of freedom of management, whether, in fact, he had had time to read this Bill.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker questions whether a gentleman had time to read a bill before discussing "freedom of management"—the specific object of freedom here is the capacity of management to operate or make decisions, which is about empowerment to act, not freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Major Fraser
records.sentence: In that respect there are freedom and order in the air and on the landing ground, and that is the framework within which American civil aviation is prospering.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "freedom" in relation to aviation operations (in the air and on landing grounds) as a general contextual good that enables American civil aviation to prosper, without specifying freedom from what interference or freedom to do what specifically; the claim is too underspecified to distinguish between negative liberty (freedom from regulation) and positive liberty (operational capacity/opportunity).

records.speaker: Mrs. Gould
records.sentence: I do not think it is possible to help these people to regain their economic freedom, to regain the state in which we all want to see them, until something is done to get rid of the zonal boundaries.
records.haiku_rationale: People are freed (to regain economic freedom and a desired economic state) by removing zonal boundaries that currently constrain their economic capacity and agency.

records.speaker: Colonel Wheatley
records.sentence: I was talking about " liberty,"The word used by the fellaheen;
