records.haiku_rationale: People are being freed from interference with their choice of how to travel; the Opposition would deny this freedom of choice/movement by restricting transport options.

records.speaker: Mr. Mawby
records.sentence: The Prime Minister said that he would bring in a Bill to make certain that they had that freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence is vague about what freedom is being granted or protected. It does not specify the object of freedom (freedom of/from what?), making it impossible to determine whether this is about freedom from interference or capacity to act.

records.speaker: The Minister of Labour
records.sentence: The matter ought to be clarified in such a way that the individual worker and the trade union official have freedom of action to perform the legitimate functions which it has been believed they have had for the last sixty years.
records.haiku_rationale: Workers and trade union officials are freed to perform legitimate functions—an empowerment to act and exercise capacity, not merely freedom from interference with pre-existing action.

records.speaker: Commander Courtney
records.sentence: asked the Minister of Aviation whether he will take steps to introduce an intermediate qualification for private pilots not in possession of a full instrument rating to allow greater freedom of movement for private and business aircraft equipped with up-to-date navigational and radio facilities.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence concerns enabling private pilots to operate aircraft with intermediate qualifications, seeking increased capacity/opportunity (freedom TO move aircraft) rather than removal of interference.

records.speaker: Mr. Merlyn Rees
records.sentence: This is something about which I feel very strongly, that local freedom matters a great deal.
records.haiku_rationale: Local freedom refers to freedom from interference with local autonomy and self-governance in local affairs.

records.speaker: Mr. Popplewell
records.sentence: Friend comes forward with a request for a further extension of this kind he should take the first step towards giving complete commercial freedom to all the undertakings for which he has responsibility.
records.haiku_rationale: Complete commercial freedom is being granted to undertakings, empowering them with the capacity to act commercially without constraint.

records.speaker: Mr. Hogg
records.sentence: Members opposite—it involves a very real curtailment of the liberty of Ministers to exercise their freedom of speech and their freedom of voting in the House.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence identifies a curtailment of Ministers' freedom of speech and freedom of voting in the House—i.e., removal of non-interference with their speech and voting capacity as parliamentarians.

records.speaker: Mr. Higgins
records.sentence: and if he will now declare, pursuant to Article 46 of the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms, that he recognises as compulsory,  ipso facto  and without special agreement, the jurisdiction of the European Court of Human Rights on all matters concerning the interpretation and application of the Convention.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence concerns recognition of compulsory jurisdiction of a court for protection of human rights, which frames liberty as removal of interference — establishing a legal system to defend individuals from state violation of fundamental rights.

records.speaker: Mr. Higgins
records.sentence: asked the Prime Minister what decision has been reached by Her Majesty's Government regarding the recognition of the competence of the European Commission on Human Rights to receive petitions within the terms of Article 25 of the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms;
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence discusses government recognition of the European Commission's competence to receive petitions under a human rights convention—a procedural and jurisdictional matter, not a substantive claim about what freedom persons have or should have.

records.speaker: Mr. Godber
records.sentence: In fact, the Bill does involve the freedom of the individual, and I have suggested to the Minister a way in which he can get out of that difficulty.
records.haiku_rationale: The individual's freedom from interference (with some unspecified right or action affected by the Bill), with the speaker suggesting a procedural escape from a constraint.

records.speaker: Mr. Robinson
records.sentence: The waters are deeply troubled, and it is not surprising that destructive elements like the Fellowship for Freedom in Medicine and the Communist Party are fishing in them, exploiting and trying to maximise the dissatisfaction.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker references "Fellowship for Freedom in Medicine" as a destructive element exploiting dissatisfaction, but does not articulate any substantive claim about what liberty means or what is being freed from or to—the phrase "Freedom in Medicine" appears as part of a proper noun (an organization name) rather than as a substantive invocation of liberty-as-a-value to be defended or opposed.

records.speaker: Mr. W. F. Deedes
records.sentence: But if a reasonable degree of freedom is to continue for the owners of shotguns—and I accept this—then I say that the Home Secretary will have to crack down harder than the Bill proposes on a minority which makes these weapons a menace.
records.haiku_rationale: Owners of shotguns are freed from state interference with their weapon possession, provided stricter regulation is applied to misusers; this concerns freedom from restriction on lawful ownership and use.

records.speaker: Mr. Michael Foot
records.sentence: There are many instances in Parliamentary history when privilege has been used not to defend but to injure freedom, and throughout most of the eighteenth century privilege was invoked by the House of Commons in a manner which interfered with the right of free debate and free discussion throughout the country at large.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker identifies two specific objects of freedom: free debate and free discussion. These are being freed from interference—specifically, from the invocation of parliamentary privilege that prevented these communicative activities. This is a claim about freedom FROM obstruction of debate and discussion.

records.speaker: Mr. Fraser
records.sentence: Gentleman's point about the workshops' freedom, I would just like to tell him that we are concerned to see that the nation's resources are properly and fully employed, and are seen to be properly and fully employed.
records.haiku_rationale: The "freedom" of workshops is invoked as an apparent constraint on resource employment, but the sentence does not articulate what the workshops would be freed from, nor does it clearly specify whether it is empowering workshops (positive) or protecting them from interference (negative). The speaker's concern with proper resource employment suggests a regulatory or oversight framing without clear liberty semantics.

records.speaker: Mr. Greenwood
records.sentence: This is money going to the Seychelles, not only from the Freedom from Hunger Campaign but under Colonial Development and Welfare funds, for which we have, of course, some continuing responsibility.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "Freedom from Hunger Campaign" is a proper noun naming a specific charitable/development campaign; the sentence uses it as an institutional reference (funding source), not to make a claim about liberty-as-a-value.

records.speaker: Mr. Bell
records.sentence: I was asking him to make a persuasive intervention, in the interests of personal freedom, with his hon.
records.haiku_rationale: Personal freedom is invoked as a cause that requires intervention—a value opposed to constraint or coercion, framing freedom negatively as the absence of unwanted interference.

records.speaker: Mr. Joseph Hiley
records.sentence: Liberty to try to express to the House the strong feeling which exists in the country against the Bill.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is invoking a parliamentary procedural grace to express political opinion in the House. The object of "liberty" is the act of expressing views ("to express to the House"). This is the conventional parliamentary phrase "took the liberty of" or "seek liberty to" — granting permission to perform an act of speech within parliamentary procedure.

records.speaker: Mr. Gardner
records.sentence: Or will he have the new fear that, because the person who has come into his house no longer has any fear of the ultimate penalty—the death penalty—that person might take the chance of bringing in with him a pistol and using that pistol if the householder stands between him and his liberty?
records.haiku_rationale: The householder's "liberty" refers to freedom from interference by an intruder—specifically, freedom of action and movement in one's own home without being harmed or controlled by the burglar.

records.speaker: Mr. Burden
records.sentence:
It is headed "Clean Air Act, 1956", and states: 
 The Parliamentary Secretary made it cleat to the Clean Air Council that the producers' present forecasts of fuel availability were based on the assumption that for purposes of the Clean Air Act grant the present freedom of choice between fuels and appliances would continue to operate when future smoke control areas were established.
records.haiku_rationale: The "freedom of choice between fuels and appliances" is an enabling capacity that allows producers to select among options when implementing smoke control requirements—a positive liberty to choose among alternatives.

records.speaker: Mr. Bell
records.sentence: There is, of course, no right to freedom of speech which does not include the right to say things which outrage one's contemporaries.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence affirms the scope of freedom of speech as a negative liberty — freedom from interference with expression, specifically including protection for speech that offends others.

records.speaker: Mr. Murray
records.sentence: asked the President of the Board of Trade, in view of the difficulties experienced by shareholders in obtaining repayment of money invested with the Freedom Group and of the fact that this company is acting in a manner oppressive of its shareholders, if he will cause an investigation to be held under Section 165 of the Companies Act, 1948.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence discusses "Freedom Group" as a proper noun (company name), not as a claim about liberty-as-a-value. The substantive issue concerns shareholder protection and investigations into oppressive corporate conduct, not freedom from interference or empowerment to act.

records.speaker: Mr. Rhodes
records.sentence: asked the President of the Board of Trade if he will appoint an inspector to conduct inquiries under Section 165 of the Companies Act, 1948, into the financial affairs of the Freedom Group, which is acting in a manner oppressive of its shareholders, in view of the fact that shareholders are experiencing difficulties in obtaining repayment of loans.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence refers to "Freedom Group" as a proper noun (company name), not a substantive claim about liberty-as-a-value.

records.speaker: Mr. Jay
records.sentence:
The Freedom Group, the National Fellowship, the People's League

for the Defence of Freedom, the Free Press Society and the Anti-Socialist Front are not companies and Section 165 of the Companies Act does not, therefore, apply to them.
records.haiku_rationale: This sentence uses "Freedom" and "Defence of Freedom" as proper nouns naming organizations, and discusses parliamentary procedure (Section 165 of the Companies Act applicability). No claim about liberty-as-a-value is made.

records.speaker: Mr. Reginald Eyre
records.sentence: Over-emphasis on uniformity in the provision of housing limits what could be an expanding area of freedom in the exercise of personal choice and taste.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker identifies an expanding capacity for personal choice and taste in housing as a form of freedom that is being limited by excessive uniformity in provision—freedom to choose housing according to one's preferences is an empowered capacity.

records.speaker: Mr. Crossman
records.sentence:
local authorities had been given a sense of freedom in their capital investment programmes which they


do not have today.
records.haiku_rationale: Local authorities are freed to decide their capital investment programmes — empowered capacity to act autonomously rather than constrained by current restrictions.

records.speaker: Dr. Mabon
records.sentence: I appreciate the point, but the problem hinges on the submission of the quinquennial review by the corporation, which is at liberty to commission any transportation study it wishes, but at the moment my Department is concerned about the procedure under the review.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "at liberty to" means the corporation has the procedural capacity/permission to commission transportation studies; this is parliamentary procedural language indicating permission to act, not a substantive claim about freedom-as-a-value.

records.speaker: Mr. Julian Snow
records.sentence: I will take the liberty of quoting two paragraphs of that resolution.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "take the liberty of" is a parliamentary procedural formula meaning "permit myself to" or "proceed to," not a substantive claim about freedom-as-a-value.

records.speaker: Mr. MacColl
records.sentence:
We are very anxious in this

Money Resolution to have as much freedom for debate as is consistent with precedent and something we felt reasonable to offer to the House.
records.haiku_rationale: Members seeking freedom for debate — freedom from procedural restriction on parliamentary discourse — a negative liberty (absence of interference with debate).

records.speaker: Mr. Crosland
records.sentence: So we must have some degree of coordination, consistent with the academic freedom which we rightly treasure.
records.haiku_rationale: Academic freedom — freedom from interference with scholarly inquiry and intellectual independence — is a negative liberty, valued as protection against external constraint.

records.speaker: Unknown
records.sentence: and calls upon all national advertisers, including Her Majesty's Government, so to diversify a proportion of their advertising as to make a significant contribution to ensuring the independence of existing newspapers and periodicals and an increasing freedom of choice for the public .
records.haiku_rationale: The public is being freed (to have capability/capacity to choose among diverse newspapers and periodicals), achieved by enabling advertisers to diversify their spending to support newspaper independence.

records.speaker: Mrs. Hart
records.sentence: This Amendment gives effect to the substance of the Amendments moved in Committee, recognising the importance of the point that was in our minds at the time but leaving it to the universities to determine the detailed arrangements for election to suit local circumstances and giving them the kind of freedom that they should have in this kind of rather precise and detailed matter.
records.haiku_rationale: Universities are being empowered (given capacity) to determine election arrangements suited to local circumstances—freedom to self-govern detailed institutional processes.

records.speaker: Mr. Leslie Hale
records.sentence: I am making no personal attack on him, but we must avoid saying these things in this House, where men died for freedom of conscience, where men were prepared to go to the block to protect what some people now call academic principles.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of conscience is the specific object; men died resisting interference with their ability to act according to conscience—a freedom from compelled belief or conformity.

records.speaker: Mr. Freeson
records.sentence: Friend aware that that is a deplorably negative reply to an important Question concerning a matter of civil liberty and personal rights?
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence references "civil liberty and personal rights" as substantive matters being discussed, without specifying what is being freed or from what. It is a procedural complaint about the character of a ministerial reply, not a substantive claim about the object or direction of freedom.

records.speaker: Mr. Bell
records.sentence: and that he should enjoy freedom of expression and freedom to persuade other people.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is asserting freedom of expression (negative liberty: freedom from interference with expressing oneself) and freedom to persuade others (positive liberty: capacity/empowerment to act persuasively on others).

records.speaker: Mr. Healey
records.sentence: This remains our policy, but the training of Vietnamese service men started as far back as 1961 under the previous Government and we see no reason why we should not assist in the training of a free country to defend its freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The specific object is a free country's capacity to defend its own freedom; the sentence empowers it to do so through military training assistance.

records.speaker: Mr. Stewart
records.sentence: Here again, it may be asked, what degree of freedom will there be in these elections?
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is asking what degree of freedom (freedom from interference or control) will exist in elections—whether elections will be genuinely free or constrained by manipulation or coercion.

records.speaker: Mr. R. H. Turton
records.sentence: Of course a parent's freedom of choice is of value to the country.
records.haiku_rationale: Parents are freed from interference in choosing their children's schooling or upbringing, negatively construed as non-interference with parental choice-making.

records.speaker: Mr. Sandys
records.sentence: While restoring freedom of decision to individual firms, it retained a strong element of public control.
records.haiku_rationale: Individual firms are being freed to make their own decisions (capacity to choose), rather than being freed from interference with decision-making.

records.speaker: Mr. Gwynfor Evans
records.sentence: If we had that freedom we could subordinate the economy to social ends and, in particular, to create the conditions of full nationhood in our country.
records.haiku_rationale: The freedom being claimed is empowerment (of Wales) to govern itself and subordinate its economy to social ends, enabling the creation of conditions for full nationhood—a positive liberty of self-determination and capacity to act on values.

records.speaker: Mr. John Smith
records.sentence: I sometimes detect the idea at Question Time that "charity" is an over-used word, like "peace" and "freedom", and is now meaningless, as it has been worn smooth by too many lips and tongues.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is commenting on the rhetoric of "freedom" as a word that has been overused and rendered meaningless through repeated invocation, without making a substantive claim about freedom as a value or what it means to be free from or empowered to do anything.

records.speaker: Unknown
records.sentence: Bill to give greater freedom to the Press and to broadcasting authorities by clarifying and amending the law relating to contempt of court, official secrets and defamation, presented accordingly and read the First time;
records.haiku_rationale: The bill seeks to free the Press and broadcasting authorities from legal restraints (contempt of court, official secrets, and defamation law), thereby reducing interference with their operations and expression.

records.speaker: Mr. William Baxter
records.sentence: I am sure that it is the wish of the House that, in being given this greater freedom, they will not forget their great responsibility not only to their own generation, but to the future generations of the islands.
records.haiku_rationale: Greater freedom is granted to the islands' government to exercise authority and self-governance, empowering them to act—a capacity to govern themselves rather than freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Mr. Dobson
records.sentence: the ship is at liberty to use the commercial channel to get the necessary assistance.
records.haiku_rationale: A ship is permitted (granted freedom from prohibition) to use a commercial channel; the object is navigational freedom (freedom of movement/access through a channel).

records.speaker: Mr. Channon
records.sentence: He talks of a threat to individual freedom, but goes on to threaten it himself because he is taking away people's rights.
records.haiku_rationale: Individual freedom and rights are being taken away (removed through interference), which is a threat to freedom from state/governmental deprivation.

records.speaker: Sir John Vaughan-Morgan
records.sentence: Nevertheless we must realise that they represent a large infringement upon the liberty of doctors to prescribe.
records.haiku_rationale: Doctors' freedom from interference in their professional practice of prescribing medicines—the sentence identifies an infringement upon (reduction of) their non-interference liberty.

records.speaker: Mr. Crowder
records.sentence: But I hope this evening that although we are discussing something that affects the liberty of the subject we will do it on a strictly non-political basis.
records.haiku_rationale: The subject's liberty is being protected from political interference—the speaker hopes discussion will remain non-partisan despite affecting constraints on freedom, positioning liberty as freedom from unwanted interference or abuse of power.

records.speaker: Mr. Reynolds
records.sentence: I know, as he said, that the new borough recently gave its Freedom to the College.
records.haiku_rationale: A local authority "gave its Freedom to the College" — this is a ceremonial/honorary honour (the formal "freedom of the city"), not a substantive claim about liberty-as-a-value or an exercise of empowerment or constraint.

records.speaker: Mr. Cant
records.sentence: I am sure that my constituents appreciate that in this party I have complete freedom to say what I like from these benches, or, indeed, anywhere else.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom to say what one likes from the parliamentary benches and elsewhere — absence of constraints on speech expression.

records.speaker: Mr. Pannell
records.sentence: I read an article last week in a Sunday newspaper in which it was said that there are no D Notices or Official Secrets Act in that heavenly country, in the land of freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "land of freedom" is a rhetorical invocation contrasting a place without D Notices or Official Secrets Act restrictions (freedom from censorship/state control) with the speaker's own country.

records.speaker: Mr. Shinwell
records.sentence: It is not a matter of the freedom of the Press.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker explicitly invokes "freedom of the Press," which names freedom from interference with press activities—a core negative liberty.

records.speaker: Mr. St. John-Stevas
records.sentence: Friends—which they are at complete liberty to take or not—I think that in view of the course of the debate it would be reasonable, in view of the views which have been expressed, not to vote against the deletion of "well-being" but that one should vote against the inclusion of the words about the existing children of the family which have been so widely objected to.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "at complete liberty to take or not" refers to parliamentary procedure—the speaker is noting that friends are procedurally permitted to accept or reject his advice on how to vote. This is incidental procedural language, not a substantive claim about freedom as a value.

records.speaker: Mr. Laurence Pavitt
records.sentence: Surely it is possible to try out not just the co-ordinating and liaison services which already exist in many areas, but to have prototypes of a service for the elderly to which all three sectors would contribute, but with more freedom and autonomy, away from the controlling influence of each, to see whether a service for the elderly would be possible drawing comprehensively on all three, which at the moment are administered and financed separately.
records.haiku_rationale: The "freedom and autonomy" being advocated is freedom of service sectors (NHS, local authorities, voluntary) from mutual controlling influence—freedom from bureaucratic constraint—to function more independently in coordinating elderly care services.

records.speaker: Mr. McMaster
records.sentence: Our aircraft industry as a whole must have freedom to design and develop new aircraft.
records.haiku_rationale: The aircraft industry is being freed to innovate and develop new aircraft—a positive enabling capacity, not merely freedom from interference with an existing activity.

records.speaker: Mr. Carr
records.sentence: The policy on which the Government have embarked will destroy this freedom if it is allowed to go on.
records.haiku_rationale: The specific freedom being referenced is not explicitly named in the sentence; "this freedom" is a bare anaphoric reference to an unspecified object of liberty threatened by government policy.

records.speaker: Mr. Lyon
records.sentence: This liberty must, of course, be limited by the right of national newspapers, and indeed the B.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "liberty" as a value in need of limiting by competing rights (national newspapers and the BBC), without specifying what freedom is being discussed or whether it concerns freedom from interference or capacity to act.

records.speaker: Sir T. Beamish
records.sentence: It promises fair shares for all, freedom from anxiety, universal affluence, greater reward for less effort, the all-embracing care of a benevolent State and peace on the cheap.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from anxiety (and implicitly from want/deprivation) through state provision of security and care — freedom from a negative condition enabled by welfare capacity.

records.speaker: Mr. Gordon Campbell
records.sentence: I believe that we have individuals in our society who, because of their disability, find themselves without a great many rights and freedoms.
records.haiku_rationale: Individuals with disabilities lack rights and freedoms (opportunities/capacities) that others possess—freedom from discrimination and removal of barriers that prevent them from exercising the same capabilities and participation as non-disabled citizens.

records.speaker: Sir T. Beamish
records.sentence: Liberty is never the soft option.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes liberty as a general principle opposed to comfort or ease, but does not specify what is being freed or from-or-to what. It is a rhetorical claim about liberty as a value without substantive content on the freedom-from-interference or empowerment distinction.

records.speaker: Mr. Marten
records.sentence: Gentleman now quite simply give the House of Commons a firm assurance that Her Majesty's Government will continue to support the United States Administration in their fight for freedom in Vietnam?
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "freedom" as a value that the US Administration is fighting to defend in Vietnam, rhetorically opposing it to what is implicitly portrayed as tyranny or oppression — a classic negative liberty appeal (freedom from enemy control/domination).

records.speaker: Mr. Robert Maclennan
records.sentence: Their implementation would serve not only to remove anomalies, uncertainties and obscurities in the law—for example, by the repeal of the almost universally disliked and certainly universally misunderstood Infants Relief Act, 1874—but would rectify certain intolerable restrictions on the freedom of young people.
records.haiku_rationale: Young people would be freed from legal restrictions (the Infants Relief Act and other constraints), removing obstacles to their autonomous action — this is negative liberty, freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Sir G. Sinclair
records.sentence: All this is at a time when Australia and New Zealand are engaged in Vietnam in what they believe to be fighting for the safety of the area and for the survival in freedom of their own countries.
records.haiku_rationale: The "survival in freedom" of their own countries means the capacity of Australia and New Zealand to exist as self-governing independent nations, free from external domination or control—a positive liberty claim about national self-determination and empowerment.

records.speaker: Unknown
records.sentence: to restore freedom to pursue actions against aircraft owners and operators for nuisance by noise and vibration;
records.haiku_rationale: Restore the capacity (legal empowerment) to pursue actions against aircraft owners for nuisance by noise.

records.speaker: Mr. Norman St. John-Stevas
records.sentence: First of all, there is the maintenance and the tradition of respect for liberty, and secondly, even more importantly, the maintenance of our institutions.
records.haiku_rationale: Liberty is invoked as a tradition and value to be maintained, without specifying freedom from what interference or freedom to do what. The sentence names respect for liberty as a cause alongside institutional maintenance, but does not articulate the specific object or direction of freedom.

records.speaker: Mr. Pardoe
records.sentence: This seems to be an erosion of liberty, but it may nevertheless be necessary.
records.haiku_rationale: An unnamed liberty is being eroded (reduced/removed), presenting liberty as a value under threat from necessity, but the specific object of freedom is not identified.

records.speaker: Mr. T. L. Iremonger
records.sentence: what is liberty to him who is poor, sick, in need, unemployed, without housing and so on?
records.haiku_rationale: What is liberty worth to someone lacking material welfare—being poor, sick, unemployed, without housing—raises whether freedom from interference matters if one lacks capacity to act on it.

records.speaker: Mr. John Fraser
records.sentence: I have always felt it to be an intrusion on the liberty of the subject that his representative Member of Parliament is not able to examine many spheres of Government spending and policy except in a debate on the Floor of the House, when he is not able to go into matters in detail.
records.haiku_rationale: The object of freedom is the MP's (and by extension the subject's) capacity to examine and scrutinize government spending and policy in detail through multiple channels—being restricted to debate on the Floor of the House limits this empowered capacity to act effectively as a representative.

records.speaker: Mr. Grieve
records.sentence: Gentleman, makes one convinced that the logical conclusion of Socialism is an ant hill in which the individual has no freedom of choice.
records.haiku_rationale: The individual is freed from the capacity/opportunity to make choices—this invokes positive liberty (the empowered ability to choose), which Socialism allegedly denies.

records.speaker: The Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food
records.sentence: Member knows, I have even taken the liberty and privilege of making a Ministerial broadcast on radio and television.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "taken the liberty" is a parliamentary idiom referring to the procedural right to take an action; it does not invoke freedom as a value against interference or express empowerment to act in a substantive sense.

records.speaker: Mr. Walker
records.sentence: When will the railways be given much greater freedom to develop these enormous property assets?
records.haiku_rationale: Railways are being freed to develop property assets—this is empowerment to act, capacity to do something, not freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Sir Alec Douglas-Home
records.sentence: Does he recognise that the same danger exists in respect of other countries whose freedom is vital to the interests of the free world?
records.haiku_rationale: Countries are freed to govern themselves (from external domination/interference), vital to the interests of the free world — positive liberty as collective empowerment of nations to determine their own destiny.

records.speaker: Sir E. Boyle
records.sentence: I should be very sorry, and I am sure the whole Committee would regard it as not right, if the Secretary of State were in a stronger position regarding academic freedom for the polytechnics simply because he has the function of designating them.
records.haiku_rationale: Academic freedom is freedom from interference with scholarly and educational activity; the concern here is whether designation authority should strengthen the Secretary of State's power to constrain that freedom, making this about protection from external control.

records.speaker: Mr. Macmillan
records.sentence: Those which I have been able to obtain indicate that, in those countries where the trade margin is fixed either by law or by a professional body and where the sale of medicine is almost wholly restricted to pharmacies—curiously enough, the two categories are the same in Europe—in almost every case the profit margins are higher than in those countries where there is greater freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from legal or professional restriction on medicine sales and trade margins; comparative freedom to sell medicines outside restricted channels (pharmacies) without regulatory fixing.

records.speaker: Unknown
records.sentence: We consider it necessary as part of our overall strategy for the economy to seek legislation covering at least 18 months, with freedom to renew it.
records.haiku_rationale: The legislation grants freedom to renew (capacity to extend the law), empowering the government to act—a positive liberty enabling future action.

records.speaker: Mr. Judd
records.sentence: I cannot understand how it is possible for us to look at the freedom fighters of Southern Africa in any different way and with any less respect from the way we looked at the resistance movement in France during the war, or at the Hungarian freedom fighters in 1956.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "freedom fighters" and "resistance movement" as rhetorical references to liberation struggles against oppressive regimes (colonial/authoritarian rule), appealing to the value of freedom from tyranny and foreign domination.

records.speaker: Mr. Jenkins
records.sentence: The Bill seeks to restore freedom to pursue actions against aircraft owners and operators for nuisance by noise and vibration.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom to pursue legal actions (capacity/empowerment to do something previously restricted), not freedom from interference with an activity itself.

records.speaker: Mr. Snow
records.sentence: Any superannuation scheme can attempt to provide reasonable benefits only to those who remain members throughout their lives, and such an optician would find either that his freedom of movement within the profession was severely handicapped or that, on joining a limited company or commercial firm, which is very common these days, the normal course of his career would be forfeited and virtually all his accrued superannuation benefits would be lost.
records.haiku_rationale: An optician's freedom of movement within the profession (career mobility and choice of employment) is being constrained/handicapped by superannuation scheme rules that penalize leaving or changing employment status.

records.speaker: Mr. Cant
records.sentence: Friend see as a solution to the problem not to do anything about the freedom of speech, but to reduce the sensitivity of sterling to the increasing pressures that it is subject to in international financing?
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "freedom of speech" appears but is used contextually to contrast with economic measures on sterling—the sentence is asking whether not addressing freedom of speech itself is a solution to currency stability, making "freedom of speech" an incidental reference within a discussion of monetary policy rather than a substantive claim about liberty-as-a-value.

records.speaker: Mr. Sandys
records.sentence: Anyone who believes in freedom and fair play must condemn them for their contemptible behaviour.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom as a rhetorical value opposed to contemptible behaviour; a general invocation of liberty as a cause without specification of what is being freed from or to.

records.speaker: The Joint Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministry of Transport
records.sentence: We are not in this debate at liberty to discuss the merits one way or the other of the principle of whether there should be a Channel Tunnel.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "at liberty to discuss" is a parliamentary procedural expression meaning permission to speak on a topic; it does not concern freedom as a substantive value or the removal/expansion of constraints on conduct, speech, or autonomy.

records.sentence: Between the seventeenth century and the early nineteenth century, there were a number of ways in which those restrictions were whittled away until, by 1925 at the latest, there was complete freedom to benefit or to cut off whoever the deceased chose.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom to dispose of one's property as chosen (the power/capacity of testators to make wills without restriction) — an empowering freedom, not merely absence of constraint.

records.speaker: Mr. John P. Mackintosh
records.sentence: I believe that from various sources in varying degrees our Press is in some danger of having its freedom eroded.
records.haiku_rationale: The press's freedom from interference and erosion is being protected as a value against encroachment.

records.speaker: Mr. Foot
records.sentence: He said that we have to choose between the freedom of the Press and the principles of trade unionism.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of the Press is freedom from interference with journalism and publication; the sentence presents it as a value to be weighed against trade union principles.

records.speaker: Mr. Foot
records.sentence: The last time I mentoned proprietors in the House I was told not to drag them into a debate about the freedom of the Press, that it was reprehensible of me to do so, and that it was trying to introduce a note of bias into the discussions.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "freedom of the Press" as a value being protected from the introduction of bias or improper influence—a classical instance of negative liberty (freedom from interference with the press's operations).

records.speaker: Mr. Banks
records.sentence: The Government are seeking powers in this Bill to deprive an individual of his or her cardinal freedom to choose inheritants.
records.haiku_rationale: An individual is being deprived of the freedom to choose inheritors (beneficiaries of their estate); the government seeks power to interfere with this personal capacity to act.

records.speaker: Mr. Stonehouse
records.sentence: I became deeply involved as a result of first-hand experience in Bengal during the struggle for freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "struggle for freedom" in reference to Bengal's independence movement—a rhetorical invocation of liberty as a cause opposed to colonial rule and tyranny, which exemplifies negative liberty (freedom from foreign domination/interference).

records.speaker: Mr. Millan
records.sentence: To say that does not mean that all of us are absolutely happy about the present position concerning editorial content or editorial freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: Editorial content and editorial freedom — freedom from interference with editorial decisions and publication choices — are classic instances of freedom of the press/expression from state or external control.

records.speaker: Unknown
records.sentence: That would be the beginning of a slippery slope which could lead to the destruction of the freedom we have always enjoyed and which I hope we always will enjoy.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "freedom we have always enjoyed" as something that could be destroyed—a rhetorical appeal to liberty as a value to be preserved against erosion (the "slippery slope"). This is a negative liberty claim: freedom as immunity from interference/oppression that the speaker wants to protect from encroachment.

records.speaker: Mr. Rathbone
records.sentence: Whether that is a Magna Carta or a Declaration of Rights or, as in the European Community, a Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms, I am not particularly qualified to comment.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence references foundational liberty documents (Magna Carta, Declaration of Rights, European Convention) but makes no substantive claim about what is being freed or from-to what; the speaker explicitly declines to comment on their substance, merely listing them as historical or legal instruments.

records.speaker: Mr. Robert Hughes
records.sentence:
What happens in Rhodesia is our responsibility, and if we want to see events brought to a speedy conclusion, we should say that we want to guarantee the settlement and that, if it has to come to an arms struggle, we shall supply weapons, if necessary, to the liberation movements to enable them to obtain their


freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker proposes guaranteeing settlement and supplying weapons to liberation movements "to enable them to obtain their freedom" — framing freedom as the empowered capacity of these movements to achieve independence and self-determination through armed struggle.

records.speaker: Mr. Buchan
records.sentence: Would the Lord Advocate agree that there are aspects of this question which bear strongly on the freedom and liberty of the subject?

records.speaker: Mr. Nicholas Ridley
records.sentence: Gentleman was the champion of the rights of the individual and that he believed in the freedom of the Press.

records.speaker: Mr. Henderson
records.sentence: Members, is part of the much wider problem of individual freedom generally.

records.speaker: Mr. Short
records.sentence: The first is between, on the one hand, allowing the maximum local freedom and initiative and, on the other hand, safeguarding the unity of the United Kingdom.

records.speaker: Sir Derek Walker-Smith
records.sentence: I believe that a monopoly control of the personnel of the Press is as great a threat to freedom of expression as monopoly ownership—or even, in contemporary circumstances, a greater threat.

records.speaker: Mr. Oakes
records.sentence: Friend the Minister for Planning and Local Government has said before in the House that, in his view, local authorities should be given as much independence and freedom as possible—and that that independence and freedom should be given a purpose and a means to support that purpose.
records.haiku_rationale: Local authorities are being empowered and granted independence and freedom as agents of governance—freedom to govern and act autonomously with means to do so, exemplifying positive liberty as capacity and empowerment.

records.speaker: Mr. James Prior
records.sentence:
Just over two months later, with unemployment at just over 1 million on unadjusted figures, he told the House:
 In the dole queue there is no freedom;

records.speaker: Mr. Robert Hughes
records.sentence: But it has been demonstrated repeatedly that there is no possible way in which that freedom can be secured peacefully.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence refers to "that freedom" (antecedent unclear in isolation) being "secured peacefully" — it treats freedom as a condition or state to be achieved or protected, suggesting positive liberty (something to be brought about or enabled), though the specific object of freedom is not named in the excerpt.

records.sentence:
Members who have spoken on the subject of freedom, which is the essential issue, acknowledged that they were in favour of the wearing


of seat belts and were convinced of the efficacy of the device.

records.speaker: Mr. Geoffrey Dodsworth
records.sentence: I took the understandable liberty of looking at that answer in April 1975.

records.speaker: Mrs. Castle
records.sentence: The freedom of movement provisions of the EEC apply here.

records.speaker: Mr. Edward Lyons
records.sentence: It is an intrusion on freedom, admittedly, but I am sure that most of us would support it.

records.speaker: Mr. Evans
records.sentence: Freedom for the asset stripper means the denial of freedom of many men to be employed.

records.speaker: Mr. David Weitzman
records.sentence: Gow) in his excellent speech, to which I pay tribute, but I wish to begin by asking what is meant by personal liberty.

records.speaker: Mr. Onslow

records.speaker: Mr. Aitken
records.sentence: Indeed, as the Minister read out her highly selective list of items for praise in her freedom-loving Government's programme, especially when she touched on such measures as the Race Relations Bill and the Sex Discrimination Act, I was reminded of a comment made by Mr.

records.speaker: The Lord Advocate
records.sentence: I have repeated the arrangements regarding the supply of names and addresses of witnesses in criminal proceedings in order to stress that even in summary criminal proceedings, where of course the penalty can include loss of liberty, this matter is regulated by an informal procedure which, to the best of my knowledge, works well and has not given rise to criticism.

records.speaker: Mr. Ross

That is


the proper test of freedom of speech—not that one's views are disagreeable to other people but that they may cause a breach of the peace.

records.sentence: I remember the Labour Party spokesman asking from the Dispatch Box on such an occasion "It it seriously suggested by Conservative Members that someone should be at liberty to say that coloured immigration into this country should be totally stopped?

records.sentence: If under my original definition service to constituents and a wider service to the country were to be the yardstick that justified safeguarding a person and protecting his freedom of speech, there could be no room in that concept for personal gain or personal advantages.

But, as I have indicated before, I am


seeking a new relationship with housing authorities which, within firm capital budgets, would allow them greater freedom to tailor their housing investment programmes to local needs.

records.speaker: Mr. Walker
records.sentence: The House will be interested to learn that this court action has been initiated by an organisation called the National Association for Freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: This sentence mentions "National Association for Freedom" as a proper noun—the name of an organization—but makes no substantive claim about liberty-as-a-value or what freedom entails.

records.speaker: Mr. Armstrong
records.sentence: This is a freedom that most people take for granted.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence provides no specification of what freedom is being referred to (the object is unspecified) or whether it concerns freedom from interference or capacity to act.

records.speaker: Mrs. Winifred Ewing
records.sentence: Lady would have mentioned my point, and as I saw that she was about to sit down, I take the liberty of asking her whether we shall hear a paragraph yet on the subject of devolution.
records.haiku_rationale: Parliamentary procedure: "took the liberty of" is a formulaic expression meaning "ventured to" or "proceeded to," with no substantive claim about freedom-as-a-value at stake.

records.speaker: Mr. Eric S. Heffer
records.sentence: Freedom is a wonderful thing.
records.haiku_rationale: A bare assertion that freedom is valuable, without specifying what is being freed, from what, or to what. The sentence is too general and unspecific to determine whether it references negative liberty (freedom from constraint) or positive liberty (freedom to act).

records.speaker: Mr. Reid
records.sentence: The Swedish Parliament in 1905–6 had the same rather tedious debates as the people of Norway sought to achieve their freedom in economic matters.
records.haiku_rationale: Norway sought freedom in economic matters—the capacity to manage economic affairs autonomously, an empowerment to self-govern in economic domain rather than freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Mr. Douglas Jay
records.sentence: As our freedom is limited by the Community guidelines, will other major exporting nations outside the EEC be similarly affected?
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker refers to the nation's freedom (to act/trade) being limited by Community guidelines—a constraint on capacity to act independently imposed by external rules.

records.speaker: Mr. Kilroy-Silk
records.sentence: It is punishment enough to take away a man's liberty and to remove him from his family and friends, and that he is put in a cell designed for one person but has to share it with two other people in close physical proximity.

records.speaker: Mr. Crouch
records.sentence: Only Parliament can pass a Bill to remove the liberty of the people to come to Parliament.

records.sentence: In contrast, we were putting emphasis on the freedom of conscience and the freedom of worship and thought.

records.speaker: Mr. Fletcher
records.sentence: Freedom is real in Britain today.

We have had such

records.speaker: Norman Buchan
records.sentence: We have a Government who have increased poverty among council tenants and slashed the freedom of local authorities at a stroke on rent and rates.
records.haiku_rationale: Local authorities are being freed from (or rather, prevented from exercising) their capacity to govern rent and rates policy autonomously—a removal of empowerment/self-governance.

records.speaker: Geoffrey Johnson Smith
records.sentence: My emotions and background are firmly in favour of more freedom of information.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of information is freedom from state or institutional interference with access to and dissemination of information.

records.speaker: Geoffrey Johnson Smith
records.sentence: Therefore, with that background I have been firmly in favour of an extension of freedom of information, certain that it should happen.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker advocates for extension of "freedom of information"—a freedom from governmental interference with access to information, a classic negative liberty.

records.speaker: Michael Meacher
records.sentence: One of the most noticeable concomitants of freedom of information abroad has been a galvanising of the bureaucracy, as the spotlight has been turned on its numbers and its methods of operation.
records.haiku_rationale: The freedom being referenced is "freedom of information"—the public's freedom from interference with access to governmental information. The sentence describes the effect of removing this constraint on bureaucratic practices.

records.speaker: Unknown
records.sentence: Michael Colvin presented a Bill to provide the freedom to belong or not to belong to a trade union: And the same was read the First time;
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom to belong or not to belong to a trade union is freedom from coercion regarding union membership—a classic negative liberty claim protecting non-interference with one's choice to join or avoid unions.

records.speaker: Frank Hooley
records.sentence: Since the Prime Minister has often declared support for open government, may I ask the Leader of the House when the Government will bring forward their Freedom of Information Bill?
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of information is a negative liberty—it refers to freedom from governmental secrecy and interference with public access to information, not a capacity being granted to the government.

records.speaker: Ian Mikardo
records.sentence: When the Freedom bookshop was opened one morning, six letters were found.
records.haiku_rationale: No substantive claim about liberty-as-a-value; "Freedom" is a proper noun (the name of a bookshop).

records.speaker: Paul Dean
records.sentence: I welcome the Government's decision to give freedom of choice to mothers.
records.haiku_rationale: Mothers are being freed to choose (presumably regarding childcare, work, or family decisions); the object is capacity/empowerment to make choices about their own lives.

records.speaker: Robert Hughes
records.sentence: I wish to comment briefly on the amendment, for the simple reason that, although I believe in the maximum freedom of choice for parents and children within the State school system, there must be some order in the way in which the scheme is operated.
records.haiku_rationale: Parents and children are to be freed for capacity to choose their school within the state system—an enabling of choice opportunity.

records.speaker: Margaret Thatcher
records.sentence: I totally agree that an exporting country such as ours needs freedom in international trade.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence asserts that an exporting country needs freedom (non-interference) in international trade—freedom from protectionist barriers and trade restrictions.

records.speaker: Patrick Mayhew
records.sentence: There should be a presumption in favour of freedom of expression, and only material of which the production causes or involves harm can justify prohibition;
records.haiku_rationale: The object is freedom of expression, which is freedom FROM governmental or legal interference with one's ability to express oneself; prohibition only justified by demonstrable harm.

records.speaker: Jack Dormand
records.sentence: Members, but there must always be an important element of personal responsibility and freedom of choice in health education.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from interference with individuals' choice in health education decisions; the speaker advocates protection of personal autonomy against constraint.

records.speaker: Ivan Lawrence
records.sentence: As everyone is welcoming the Bill, I take the liberty of offering yet one more word of welcome.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker uses the idiom "take the liberty of" offering welcome; this is parliamentary procedure language indicating the speaker felt permitted to speak, not a substantive claim about freedom as a value.

records.speaker: Neil Macfarlane
records.sentence: Kinnock) talking about compassion and freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence is a bare reference to "freedom" in an unspecified context (Kinnock talking about compassion and freedom), without sufficient detail to determine whether the freedom at issue is freedom from interference or freedom/capacity to act.

records.speaker: Toby Jessel
records.sentence: Some confusion arises from the use of the word "freedom".
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence makes an observation about linguistic confusion around the word "freedom" itself, without specifying what is being freed from or to what.

records.speaker: Barry Sheerman
records.sentence: We are constantly arguing and discussing liberty and freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence makes no substantive claim about what is being freed or from-or-to what; it merely reports that MPs are discussing the concepts of liberty and freedom without specifying any object of freedom or constraint.

records.speaker: Terence Higgins
records.sentence: The fact that people are using their freedom not to wear seat belts imposes a cost upon the Exchequer and thus on the taxpayer.
records.haiku_rationale: People are free from legal requirement to wear seat belts; the speaker frames this negative liberty (freedom from interference with personal choice) as imposing costs on the state.

records.speaker: Barry Sheerman
records.sentence: On both sides of the House we profoundly defend freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: Both sides of the House defend freedom as a general cause against tyranny or oppression—a rhetorical invocation of liberty as a foundational political value.

records.speaker: Geraint Howells
records.sentence:
Article 4 says:
 The freedom of movement appropriate to an animal … shall not be restricted in such a manner as to cause it unnecessary suffering or injury".
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from restriction of the animal's movement is being protected against unnecessary suffering—negative liberty framed as freedom from interference with the animal's physical mobility.

records.speaker: Archibald Hamilton
records.sentence: I am a great believer in freedom, and we should be careful before we censor such establishments, but we should consider whether they have a corrupting influence on a locality.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "freedom" as a general principle against censorship interference, but the substance concerns enabling evaluation of whether to regulate businesses; this mixes negative liberty (freedom from censorship) with a pragmatic capacity-to-evaluate approach that resists clean classification.

records.speaker: Jeremy Bray
records.sentence: Within the technical work being undertaken by the Inland Revenue, we have a fixing of the freedom within which the House can reform the pattern of taxation during the next 10 or 15 years.
records.haiku_rationale: The House (Parliament) is constrained by technical work of the Inland Revenue; "freedom" refers to the scope/capacity within which Parliament can reform taxation policy—an empowerment and opportunity to act within defined bounds.

records.speaker: George Younger
records.sentence: They have complete democratic freedom to put through their policies, strike their rate, and be judged by their electors for doing so.
records.haiku_rationale: Local authorities are empowered/enabled to exercise their own policy choices (putting through policies, striking rates) and be accountable for them—this is freedom to self-govern and act autonomously.

records.speaker: Gerald Kaufman
records.sentence:
The Association of County Councils, which is Conservative controlled, denounces the Bill as
 a further encroachment on local government autonomy… It will diminish the freedom of local authorities.
records.haiku_rationale: Local authorities are being freed from central government control and interference; the Bill diminishes their capacity for independent self-governance.

records.speaker: Hugh Rossi
records.sentence: No basic individual liberty is at risk.
records.haiku_rationale: Individual liberty—understood as freedom from government interference with personal conduct and rights—is not under threat according to this statement.

records.speaker: John Evans
records.sentence: Friend and some of his friends outside the House will give the same freedom to other members of the Labour Party to debate and call into question some of the policy decisions — as he has rightly done today.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom to debate and call into question policy decisions — freedom from interference with engaging in debate and questioning — is negative liberty, a protection against suppression of political speech and contestation.

records.speaker: Sally Oppenheim
records.sentence: The Director General says that he is satisfied that if the building societies follow the association's recommendation, complaints about the freedom of borrowers to choose an insurance company should no longer arise.
records.haiku_rationale: Borrowers freed to choose their insurance company (an enabled capacity to select providers), not merely freedom from interference with that choice.

records.speaker: Christopher Price
records.sentence:
My second point is that Lord Scarman made it absolutely clear in his judgment that the majority judgment contravened article 10 of the European Convention on Human Rights which states that
 Everyone has the right to freedom of expression
 and that that right
 shall include freedom to hold opinions and to receive and impart information and ideas without interference by public authority and regardless of frontiers.
records.haiku_rationale: What is being protected: freedom of expression, holding opinions, and receiving/imparting information. What it protects against: interference by public authority. This is freedom from government interference with expression and the flow of ideas.

records.speaker: Percy Grieve
records.sentence:
I shall not waste time at this late hour by reading the particular passage, but it is contained in articles 38, 39, and so on, of the proposed Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, under the heading
 Procedure for Amending Constitution of Canada".
records.haiku_rationale: This sentence is a procedural reference to sections of a Canadian constitutional document; it does not make a substantive claim about what anyone is freed from or empowered to do.

records.speaker: Bernard Braine
records.sentence:
Specific mention is then made in section 25 of 
 any" — 
 that is the word to watch — 
 rights or freedoms that have been recognised by the Royal Proclamation of October 7 1763;
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence refers to "rights or freedoms" that have been recognised by a historical proclamation, without specifying what those freedoms entail or whether the speaker is discussing freedom from interference or capacity to act. records.speaker: Ronald W. Brown
records.sentence: As a result of that we were able to give freedom to London as a whole for the concessionary fares by using a 2p rate, which brought the matter under general local government powers and not under the 1968 Act.
records.haiku_rationale: London is being empowered (given the capacity/freedom) to set concessionary fares using a 2p rate, enabling autonomous local governance. This is positive liberty—the freedom to act on one's own governance choices.

records.speaker: Dale Campbell-Savours
records.sentence:
Section 52 says that under the Charter of Rights and Freedoms
 the Constitution of Canada is the supreme law of Canada, and any law that is inconsistent with the provisions of the Constitution is … of no force or effect.
records.haiku_rationale: This sentence describes a legal-constitutional framework (Canada's Charter of Rights and Freedoms and supremacy clause) but does not advance a substantive claim about what freedom is or who should be freed from-or-to what. It is a statement of procedure and legal structure.

records.speaker: Ivan Lawrence
records.sentence: I do not do so carelessly or without a great deal of heart-searching, for I appreciate that such action could easily be misconstrued as unfriendliness or even colonialism to a truly great independent nation that forms so vital a part of the Commonwealth and that stood side by side with Britain in defence of freedom, democracy and civilisation itself.

records.speaker: Gerald Kaufman
records.sentence: It is unacceptable in its unprecedented interference with the freedom of local authorities.
records.haiku_rationale: Local authorities are being freed from interference by the state in their ability to govern and make decisions — this is negative liberty, asserting freedom from constraint on their autonomous action.

records.speaker: John Farr
records.sentence: The circumstances may range from a partially successful suicide pact through mercy killing and a violent reaction to an intolerable husband to a cold calculated murder with financial gain or sexual liberty in mind.

records.speaker: John Stokes
records.sentence: After all, those countries owe their freedom to what we did for them in the last war.
records.haiku_rationale: Countries' freedom (independence/sovereignty) from foreign occupation/domination, enabled/granted by military victory in the last war.

records.speaker: Margaret Thatcher
records.sentence: Our objective is to restore freedom and the rule of law to the Falkland Islands and we will not be put off by Argentine procrastination.
records.haiku_rationale: The Falkland Islands are being freed from Argentine occupation/control—the freedom sought is self-determination and sovereignty restored to the islanders, which is a capacity to govern themselves.

records.speaker: Margaret Thatcher
records.sentence: Gentleman, who also makes good use of his freedom, would begrudge the cash necessary, and thereby deny it to those people.
records.haiku_rationale: A person exercises freedom (implicitly freedom to use resources or act as they wish) and the sentence addresses whether denying cash to others restricts their freedom to do so.

records.speaker: Teddy Taylor
records.sentence: So long as the nation States retain their freedom to elect Governments committed to either interventionist Socialist or noninterventionist Conservative Governments, this paragraph is either a meaningless form of words or designed to pave the way towards supranational economic policies.
records.haiku_rationale: Nation-states are being freed to retain their capacity to elect governments of their chosen ideological direction—an empowerment of political self-determination.

records.speaker: Ivor Stanbrook
records.sentence: The very idea is incompatible with freedom and democracy.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence makes a bare rhetorical invocation of "freedom" as a value opposed to a particular idea, but does not specify what is being freed, from what, or to what. records.speaker: Dennis Skinner

records.speaker: Peter Blaker
records.sentence: It will, I believe, have enhanced in Europe the prospects of peace and freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: Enhanced prospects of "freedom" as an abstract value opposed to constraint or domination (in the context of European peace and security); the object of freedom is under-specified, but the invocation treats it as a general political good—typically understood as freedom from external interference or oppression.

records.speaker: Neville Trotter
records.sentence: Member for Kingston upon Hull, East disagrees, he is at liberty to pay a short visit to the Library as I did after his speech.
records.haiku_rationale: Parliamentary procedure: "at liberty to" is a conventional phrase meaning "permitted to" or "welcome to", not a substantive claim about freedom as a value. The speaker is making a procedural point that the other member is permitted to visit the Library if he wishes.

records.speaker: Malcolm Rifkind
records.sentence: Throughout the realm of human rights, the concepts of personal liberty and freedom which all hon.

records.speaker: Jock Bruce-Gardyne
records.sentence: While we in this country cannot hope to insulate ourselves from the impact of interest rate movements elsewhere in the world and especially in the United States, responsible fiscal and monetary policies at home give us some freedom of manoeuvre that would be denied us if our domestic stance was perceived to be one of budgetary laxity such as suggested by Opposition parties.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker claims that "responsible fiscal and monetary policies at home give us some freedom of manoeuvre" — the freedom being discussed is the capacity/ability to manoeuvre (act flexibly) in economic policy, which is enabled by domestic fiscal discipline. records.speaker: Stanley Clinton-Davis
records.sentence: Does the Secretary of State agree that linkage is the latest excuse among many for many years now on the part of South Africa to delay further freedom for Namibia?
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence refers to "freedom for Namibia" in the context of South Africa delaying political independence and self-determination—what is being freed is Namibia's capacity to govern itself, freed from South African control.

records.speaker: Jill Knight
records.sentence: Freedom of speech no longer completely exists because of the fear within the Health Service, and that is also due to the bully boys.

records.sentence: The deprivation of the liberty of someone that young, the curtailment of the freedom of someone that young, is the same to him in its effect whether his freedom is restricted as a result of being in secure accommodation or in a remand centre.
records.haiku_rationale: Curtailment and deprivation of freedom through institutional confinement (secure accommodation or remand centre) restricts the freedom of a young person from normal movement and association.

records.speaker: Edwin Wainwright
records.sentence: That is surely in line with the Secretary of State's view on the freedom of democracies to decide who should govern the country and how it should be governed.
records.haiku_rationale: Democracies are freed (empowered) to make their own decisions about self-governance and leadership, without external interference or constraint.

records.speaker: Gerard Vaughan
records.sentence: one with total freedom in clear visual conditions, free from cloud;
records.haiku_rationale: This is a meteorological description of visibility conditions ("total freedom in clear visual conditions, free from cloud"), not a substantive claim about liberty or freedom as a political or social value.

records.speaker: Norman Buchan
records.sentence: Once we have the freedom to plan and develop a proper support system in accordance with our needs, several things will happen.

records.speaker: Gerry Neale
records.sentence: Its view is that the Bill will unlock many opportunities to expand and that the greater freedom will bring more jobs.

records.sentence: I am in no doubt that there is a great deal more support among BT's staff for freeing BT from Treasury control and giving it commercial freedom than was evident on the so-called day of action by the POEU.

records.speaker: John Grant

records.haiku_rationale: British Telecom is being freed (empowered/enabled) to react to market forces and operate independently from political control—a capacity to act in response to economic conditions rather than freedom from specific interference.

records.speaker: George Thomas
records.sentence: Member for Hackney, South and Shoreditch, whose application I received first, is accordingly at liberty to table a motion for the commencement of public business tomorrow, which the House will decide.
records.haiku_rationale: Parliamentary procedure: "at liberty to table a motion" is procedural permission granted by the Speaker, not a substantive claim about freedom-as-a-value.

records.speaker: Peter Blaker
records.sentence: I entirely agree that they are the guarantee of our liberty and have been ever since they have been here with the consent of Governments of both parties.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence refers to institutions (likely the armed forces) as guarantees of liberty—freedom from external interference and threats to national sovereignty and independence, understood as a condition requiring protective institutional capacity rather than removal of governmental constraints.

records.speaker: Roy Hattersley
records.sentence: Member for Wycombe couched his speech in terms of freedom, but it is not and never has been the view of the Opposition that freedom is simply the absence of restraint.
records.haiku_rationale: This sentence contrasts two conceptions of freedom: freedom-as-non-interference (absence of restraint, negative liberty) versus an unarticulated alternative conception that the Opposition holds (likely positive liberty or a richer conception). records.speaker: Roy Hattersley
records.sentence: I did so because I wanted to pay special and proper respect to the quotation from Tawney on the relationship of the state to freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence references Tawney's view on the relationship between the state and freedom, but does not substantively assert what freedom is or from what it is to be freed or enabled. It is a meta-statement about paying respect to a quotation being discussed, not a claim about liberty itself.

records.speaker: David Mellor
records.sentence: To sum up the Government's view — I apologise if I have taken too much time — the Bill gives freedom to choose on grounds from which we cannot dissent.
records.haiku_rationale: The Government grants freedom to choose (among options regarding grounds for action), enabling agents to select according to their own judgment.

records.speaker: Alan Beith
records.sentence: However, there is no doubt that a change towards extensive Sunday trading would clearly affect the freedom of many people to worship and enjoy peace and quiet on Sundays.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom being affected is the capacity of people to worship and enjoy peace and quiet on Sundays—an enabled condition or power to engage in religious practice and rest, which would be constrained by extensive Sunday trading.

records.speaker: Angus Maude
records.sentence: There is no legal aid in libel cases, they take far too long to get to court, and the sort of complaint which has been made about individual cases here is not met by those legal restraints on the freedom of the press.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of the press is being freed from legal restraints (libel law, court delays); this is freedom from interference with press activity.

records.speaker: Thomas Benyon
records.sentence: That is the body with the real power of freedom of speech in Britain.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of speech is a negative liberty—freedom from interference with one's ability to speak. The sentence identifies a body as wielding the power of this freedom, which is fundamentally about non-interference with expression.

records.speaker: Geraint Morgan
records.sentence: First, citizens of the United Kingdom living in Northern Ireland are entitled to the same standards of liberty and civil rights as British citizens travelling and living anywhere else in the country.
records.haiku_rationale: Citizens are entitled to the same civil rights and liberty (freedom from interference with fundamental rights) as other British citizens, regardless of location—a claim about protection from discrimination in access to negative liberties.

records.speaker: Ivan Lawrence
records.sentence: How can it be against the interest of any British subject to extend the laws, if necessary interfering with some individual liberty, to protect society from terrorist outrages, which are growing and seem increasingly, if those articles are right, to be centred upon Great Britain?
records.haiku_rationale: Individual liberty (negative liberty: freedom from interference) is being interfered with to protect society from terrorism; the speaker presents this as potentially justified, weighing constraint on negative liberty against security.

records.speaker: Roy Jenkins
records.sentence: It is a case not of the good or the wise but of trying to form a judgment about what best strikes the balance between human freedom and proper protection.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "human freedom" as a value to be balanced against "proper protection," without specifying what freedom is being freed, from what interference, or to do what. The abstraction and ambiguity between freedom from constraint versus freedom as empowerment, combined with the balancing framework, prevents a determinate classification.

records.speaker: Norman Buchan
records.sentence: I should like to draw attention to the speed with which the Government have been able to act on a difficulty of this type, which poses questions of freedom, nationality and international obligation.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence raises "freedom" as a value in a policy context (alongside nationality and international obligation) but does not specify what is being freed, from what constraint, or to what capacity. The object and direction of freedom are entirely unspecified.

records.speaker: John Browne
records.sentence: Until the employment cartels are broken and more freedom and enterprise are introduced, Government spending will continue to increase.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker calls for "freedom and enterprise" to be "introduced" into the economy by breaking employment cartels—this is freedom TO innovate, compete, and conduct business (opportunity/empowerment), not freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Anthony Meyer
records.sentence: After the issues of great moment involving human rights and individual freedom that have been raised in what has been one of the most interesting debates that I have listened to for a long time, I confess that the matter that I want to raise is of a perhaps more restricted interest.
records.haiku_rationale: Human rights and individual freedom are invoked as matters of great moment in debate, establishing them as values opposed to constraint—this is a rhetorical invocation of liberty as freedom from infringement, without specifying the particular object or mechanism.

records.speaker: Angela Rumbold
records.sentence: The provisions of the 1980 Act and the voucher scheme have given or could give freedom of choice to parents, as will the retention of church schools.
records.haiku_rationale: Parents are being empowered (given the capacity/opportunity) to choose their children's schools through vouchers and retention of church schools—this is freedom TO act with expanded options, not freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Richard Shepherd
records.sentence: The little niggles that suggested to me that the intentions of the Bill as originally framed were not as generous as the words resided in such pointers as the Government's initial reluctance to accept the non-discrimination principle, which is of the essence of the protection of our freedom and choice in the market place.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom and choice in the market place are being protected by a non-discrimination principle, enabling individuals to act without arbitrary constraint—a capacity to choose freely in economic transactions.

records.speaker: Peggy Fenner
records.sentence: We believe that the new clause would have an adverse effect on the commercial freedom and performance of the plant breeding industry, which would be compelled to release the material that was being developed for the production of new varieties.

records.speaker: Roger Moate
records.sentence: We must assert clearly and without any doubts that it is our purpose and our determination to defend the integrity, the independence and the freedom of the dependent peoples who still look to us.
records.haiku_rationale: The dependent peoples are to be freed from external domination and control—their independence and freedom as a collective is being empowered against interference, though the focus is on assertion of protective purpose rather than individual non-interference.

records.speaker: Thomas King
records.sentence: We can find out what that comprehensive freedom means from an interview which the right hon.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence is incomplete and does not contain a substantive claim about what "comprehensive freedom" entails—it merely signals that a reference (an interview) will provide the definition.
