records.speaker: Eldon Griffiths
records.sentence: The first civil liberty should be the householder's right to live undisturbed in his or her own home, the right of old people to walk the streets without being set upon and the right of women to be safe from sexual assault.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from interference with one's person and property: the householder's freedom from intrusion/disturbance in the home, the elderly's freedom from assault in public spaces, and women's freedom from sexual violence.

records.speaker: Stefan Terlezki
records.sentence: Defending Britain means that what our fathers and grandfathers have fought and died for is worth defending and protecting, so that we, our children and our grandchildren will live in freedom without experiencing slavery, tyranny and oppression, as, regrettably, some of us had to.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from slavery, tyranny, and oppression—what is being freed is future generations from coercive constraints and authoritarian rule.

records.speaker: Nicholas Ridley
records.sentence: The real need is for London Transport to be allowed freedom to manage its affairs with a minimum of political interference and control, but within clearly stated financial and policy objectives.
records.haiku_rationale: London Transport is being freed from political interference and control in order to manage its affairs—this is empowerment to act autonomously, not freedom from a negative constraint, making it positive liberty.

records.speaker: Unknown

records.speaker: Edward Heath
records.sentence: In particular, we have been opposed to the centralisation of power because we have throughout realised the intense dangers to freedom that that holds for everyone.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from the centralisation of power, understood as opposition to concentration of authority that endangers liberty; this is freedom from (concentrated) interference with self-governance.

records.speaker: Robin Maxwell-Hyslop
records.sentence: Would you be good enough to let the House know whether you have selected the amendments in my name, bearing in mind that this is not an affirmative resolution on the statutory instrument and that you are at liberty to select the amendments if you so desire?

 Our aims in the media are to safeguard freedom of expression, encourage diversity and establish greater accountability make sense, but as a student of history he will know that those words are similar to those found in the constitutions of many Eastern European countries.

records.sentence: Going even further, the Government have introduced two major pieces of legislation — the Employment Acts of 1980 and 1982  —  both designed to restrict the freedom to bargain and to impose upon employers decent basic individual rights at the work place.

records.speaker: Richard Ryder
records.sentence: They cannot be expected to underwrite for ever the freedom of distant cousins when appreciation is often grudging, or when cultural contrasts are stressed by leaders of western European opinion.
records.haiku_rationale: The specific object of freedom is distant cousins' ability to govern themselves or maintain sovereignty (understood contextually as the UK's commitment to their independence/self-determination), freed from the burden of perpetual underwriting or military/economic guarantee.

records.speaker: Neil Macfarlane
records.sentence: Friend has expressed a false concern about freedom in sport.

records.sentence: Local authorities must have more freedom to take them back into ownership with full reimbursement by central Government.
records.haiku_rationale: Local authorities are empowered (given capacity) to take assets back into ownership—this is about enabling a positive power or opportunity for governmental action, not removing interference.

records.speaker: Roger Freeman

records.speaker: Terry Lewis
records.sentence: It is another useful step, however, towards freedom of information.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of information is being protected from governmental secrecy or restriction—a freedom from interference with access to information.

records.speaker: Peter Thurnham
records.sentence: Over the years freedoms have been introduced to help people gain more control over their lives.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedoms introduced to help people gain control over their lives represents positive liberty—empowerment enabling people to have increased capacity and agency to direct their own circumstances.

records.speaker: Gerald Howarth
records.sentence: Freedoms are constrained.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedoms (unspecified) are being constrained or restricted—a reduction in freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Jeremy Corbyn
records.sentence: " Speaker after speaker from the Tory Benches proposed freedom for landlords to exploit people to the nth degree.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from interference with landlords' ability to set rents and terms—what is being freed is landlords' power to exploit tenants; the freedom is FROM regulatory constraint or tenant protection.

records.speaker: Tony Banks
records.sentence: Those who wish to go into the polling booths and write something discourteous about the Prime Minister or about the Labour party candidate for Newham, North-West, would still be at liberty to do so.
records.haiku_rationale: Voters are freed from interference in their capacity to write discourteous things about political figures/parties on ballot papers.

records.speaker: Derek Conway
records.sentence: I believe that, although his new-found freedom will ultimately be to the detriment of the Government and of my party, it will be of great benefit in the battles ahead to safeguard the Health Service in Shropshire.
records.haiku_rationale: A government actor (presumably a minister or official) is granted freedom—empowerment or discretion—to act in a certain way (safeguarding the Health Service), which will benefit the speaker's political goals. This is an enablement to act, not a protection from interference.

records.speaker: David Porter
records.sentence: The Government have largely won the arguments on defence, freedom of choice, trade union reforms, wider ownership, and, to some extent, jobs.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of choice is empowerment to select from options—the speaker celebrates the Government having advanced the capacity of people to choose, particularly in contexts like consumption, education, or employment.

records.speaker: George Younger
records.sentence: The power of freedom must be exercised by the social will of the community.
records.haiku_rationale: The community is empowered to exercise freedom through collective social will—a capacity to act and decide, rather than freedom from interference.

records.speaker: George Younger
records.sentence: She wants freedom to control the 300,000 newspapers that are printed each day, but what about the freedom of those 300,000 people who wanted to read that particular newspaper which is now changing hands?
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence presents two competing liberties: (1) freedom to control newspapers (positive liberty—capacity to exercise editorial control), and (2) freedom of readers to access a particular newspaper (negative liberty—freedom from interference with their reading choices). The sentence does not resolve which should take precedence, presenting both enabling and constraining aspects as a genuine tension.

records.speaker: Nick Brown
records.sentence: How will the Government's declared aim of achieving freedom of choice be realised if pupils are debarred from undertaking courses because they cannot afford the cost?
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "freedom of choice" — pupils' ability to choose courses they wish to undertake — and identifies financial barriers (affordability) as preventing this capacity. Being unable to afford courses prevents the realization of choice, a positive liberty framing.

records.speaker: Martin O'Neill
records.sentence: We recognise that we demand a loss of civil liberties from our voluntary forces so that our civil liberties and freedom can be maintained and protected.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker discusses loss of civil liberties (constraining non-interference for military personnel) as a means to maintain and protect civil liberties for the wider population. This is fundamentally about freedom from state interference in civilian life, which is negative liberty.

records.speaker: Tony Blair
records.sentence: I am not prepared to take that liberty.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "take that liberty" is a conventional idiom expressing unwillingness to presume or overstep in parliamentary procedure; it is not a substantive claim about freedom-as-a-value.

records.speaker: The Rev Martin Smyth
records.sentence: Does the Secretary of State accept that those of us who demand a high standard of protection for our people welcome the modernisation of our prisons, both for the morale of the staff and for the care of those who have suffered — quite justifiably in most cases — the deprivation of liberty?
records.haiku_rationale: The object of freedom is literal/legal liberty (freedom from deprivation of liberty itself, i.e., imprisonment), constrained by criminal justice; the speaker accepts this deprivation as justified, and the sentence discusses prison conditions rather than freedom from constraint itself.

records.speaker: Ian Taylor
records.sentence: That gives room for the freedom to make certain national movements within the barriers.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker describes a capacity to make national movements within specified barriers—an empowerment or enabling of action, not a removal of interference.

records.speaker: Kenneth Baker
records.sentence: I would sum up the Bill's 169 pages in three words  —  standards, freedom and choice.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "freedom" as a substantive goal alongside "standards" and "choice"—this is a bare, under-specified invocation of freedom as a value without specifying what is being freed or from/to what.

records.speaker: Angela Rumbold
records.sentence: Is it so hard for Opposition Members to believe that somewhere out there parents, governors and teachers may want to exercise freedom of choice?
records.haiku_rationale: Parents, governors and teachers are freed from interference with their capacity to choose (schools, education arrangements, governance decisions)

records.speaker: Kenneth Clarke
records.sentence: I believe that early privatisation and full commercial freedom will enable the company and its work force to be best placed to go on to further achievements and to secure a firmly based competitive industry with a long-term future.
records.haiku_rationale: Commercial freedom—the company and workforce are empowered to compete, innovate, and achieve future success through privatisation and market opportunity.

records.speaker: Dennis Skinner
records.sentence: 11 and tell the Attorney-General to make a statement about the freedom and liberty of the British people in relation to the gagging and censoring of the BBC by a party whose friends own and control most of the press, and which has a majority of 100 in the House.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes freedom and liberty as values being violated by censoring interference with the BBC's editorial independence, which constrains the British people's freedom from government/political interference with media expression.

records.speaker: Robert N. Wareing
records.sentence: There is no doubt that this clause, introduced by the Government, is contrary to the stated philosophy of the Conservative party, which is always talking about freedom of choice.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence identifies "freedom of choice" as a stated value that is being violated by a government clause, invoking negative liberty as freedom from interference with one's choices.

records.speaker: Tony Benn
records.sentence: We have seen an alliance of former Home Secretaries — who have been involved to some extent and who do not want the degree of freedom of information that, on the whole, the public want, even if they do not write to the hon.
records.haiku_rationale: What is being freed: the public's access to information. From what: government secrecy/official restriction. This is a claim about freedom from interference with access to information—a core negative liberty.

records.speaker: Gavin Strang
records.sentence: Therefore, we submit, as do the Freedom Association and a range of organisations, that the proposal is fundamentally antidemocratic.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "Freedom Association" as a proper noun (organization name), and characterizes a proposal as "antidemocratic" rather than making a substantive claim about liberty-as-a-value.

records.speaker: Graham Allen
records.sentence: " They do so through a few dissident members and through a few people funded by the likes of David Hart and the Freedom Association.
records.haiku_rationale: The Freedom Association is a proper noun (organization name), and the sentence does not make a substantive claim about liberty-as-a-value, only mentions the organization as a funding source.

records.speaker: Bob Clay
records.sentence: It is concerned with the rights of mavericks, and is to be manipulated by Conservative organisations, industry, the Economic League, people such as David Hart, who may get the job — that is the irony of it — and by the Freedom Association to harass trade unions.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence names the "Freedom Association" as an organization engaged in harassment of trade unions, treating freedom as a proper noun (organization name) without making a substantive claim about liberty-as-a-value.

records.speaker: Graham Allen
records.sentence: It is hypocritical because the Tory party and the Government seek to corner the key words, the buzz words of "democracy" and "freedom".
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker uses "freedom" rhetorically as a political value that the Tory party claims to embody, without specifying what aspect of freedom is at stake. The sentence criticizes the government for monopolizing the term "freedom" as propaganda, treating it as a symbol of their political identity rather than analyzing what freedom from or freedom to something means.

records.speaker: Ivan Lawrence
records.sentence: As this is such a sensible and important Bill, protecting the liberty of the individual, it comes as no surprise to me that the Government support it.
records.haiku_rationale: The individual is being freed from interference; "protecting the liberty of the individual" invokes freedom from external constraint as a cause opposed to restriction.

records.speaker: Andrew Welsh
records.sentence: The self-employed require a taxation package to allow them freedom of decision making and maximum help, especially in the first years of any new business.
records.haiku_rationale: Self-employed people are being empowered with a taxation package that enables their capacity to make decisions and conduct business—this is freedom to exercise entrepreneurial agency, not freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Harry Ewing
records.sentence: As people in Scotland continue to elect Labour councils, including in the capital city of Edinburgh, the Government take the huff and pull into the centre the freedom of local authorities to decide their own domestic housing policies.
records.haiku_rationale: Local authorities are being freed from (or would have) the capacity to decide their own domestic housing policies; the government is pulling that empowered authority away from them, removing their autonomy.

records.speaker: Bob Cryer
records.sentence: The report is a demonstration of the crushing weight placed by central Government bureaucracy on local authorities, instead of giving them the freedom of choice — much vaunted by the Conservatives — and allowing them some choice in expenditure so that they can improve services.
records.haiku_rationale: Local authorities are being freed to the capacity to make choices about expenditure and service improvement, rather than being freed from interference — this is empowerment to act.

records.speaker: Allan Stewart
records.sentence: That goes right to the heart of academic freedom and democracy, whatever the views of the people concerned.
records.haiku_rationale: Academic freedom — the freedom from interference with scholarship and intellectual enquiry — is being invoked as a fundamental value at the heart of democracy.

records.speaker: Derek Fatchett
records.sentence: Those who break the law are not exercising the right of freedom of speech;
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes freedom of speech, which is a prototypical negative liberty—freedom from interference with the expression of one's views. The claim is that law-breaking falls outside the scope of this protected freedom.

records.speaker: Terence Higgins
records.sentence: I hope profoundly that, on reflection, those who participated in the incident will realise that democracy is a fragile thing and that it is not easy to defend freedom of speech in this place.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker references "freedom of speech" in Parliament—a classic negative liberty framing about non-interference with expression in this deliberative forum.

records.speaker: Derek Fatchett
records.sentence: Gentleman and the Government is that all parents will be given greater freedom, why does not that freedom extend all the way — why does it not extend, by analogy, to allowing parents to make a choice on the school curriculum and the provision that it will give?
records.haiku_rationale: Parents are being freed to make choices (choice of school curriculum and provision), which is an enabling capacity rather than mere non-interference; this is positive liberty.

records.speaker: Andrew Smith
records.sentence:
He referred to the hypothetical example given by the Under-Secretary of State of a member of a theological college or faculty who had lost his faith and no longer wanted to teach the basic tenets of Christianity, and asked:
 In such a case, if the faculty and vice-chancellor tried to dismiss him, should there be provision in the Bill to allow him to remain in the faculty because his academic freedom would otherwise be inhibited?
records.haiku_rationale: Academic freedom (freedom from inhibition/interference with teaching and intellectual pursuits) is being discussed—the speaker asks whether a member should be protected from dismissal to preserve his academic freedom.

records.speaker: Christopher Hawkins
records.sentence: I should hate this Government to be blamed for destroying what should be an integral part of any civilised society and of the policies of any party that values freedom of speech, freedom of thought and freedom of the written word.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes freedom of speech, freedom of thought, and freedom of the written word as core values of a civilised society—these name freedoms from interference with expression and conscience, not capacities to do something.

records.speaker: Jeremy Ashdown
records.sentence: However, as we recall what happened, we are all aware that there was an attack on the freedom of speech predominantly of Conservative Members and that caused that measure to be introduced.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of speech is a classic negative liberty — it refers to freedom from interference with the ability to speak, here specifically noting an attack on that non-interference by others.

records.speaker: James Wallace
records.sentence: The Tory party tells us that it is the party of freedom and of individual choice.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence reports a claim by the Tory party about themselves but does not specify what is being freed or from-to what. It is a bare invocation of "freedom" and "individual choice" without substantive content about the object of liberty.

records.speaker: Dennis Skinner
records.sentence: That is one of the few freedoms  —  the most important freedom  —  for working men and women.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is asserting a freedom (unspecified in the excerpt, but clearly referring to some fundamental entitlement for workers) from interference or constraint—the mention of "the most important freedom for working men and women" invokes liberty as a value against denial or suppression.

records.speaker: Nicholas Bennett
records.sentence:
I was just going to quote from "On Liberty" to show that John Stuart Mill, the 19th-century Liberal Member of Parliament, set out clearly the principles of his party when he said:
 That the whole or any large part of the education of the people should be in State hands, I go as far as anyone in depreciating.
records.haiku_rationale: The quoted Mill passage expresses skepticism about state control of education—it is concerned with preventing state interference with the domain of education, a constraint on governmental power over a traditional zone of individual and family autonomy.

records.speaker: Robin Corbett
records.sentence: That is not the kind of freedom to which, in a properly free society, any of us can subscribe.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker rejects a particular conception of "freedom" (unspecified in the sentence) as unacceptable to subscribe to in a "properly free society," invoking freedom/liberty as a value but not specifying whether the contested freedom is negative (absence of interference) or positive (empowering capacity).

records.speaker: Christopher Chope
records.sentence: Gentleman wants to allow that council to have freedom to incur more and more debt without any restraint whatever.
records.haiku_rationale: A council being freed to incur debt without restraint—empowerment to act (spend and borrow without constraint).

records.speaker: Mo Mowlam
records.sentence: Without some form of economic freedom, the only freedom that those people have is the freedom to sit in front of an electric fire with one bar on and to decide whether they can afford to watch telly tonight.
records.haiku_rationale: Economic capacity (purchasing power to heat, light, and entertain oneself) is being freed—the speaker argues that without material means, formal freedoms of choice are meaningless; what is being freed is the ability to live with dignity and make basic life decisions.

records.speaker: Robert Maclennan
records.sentence: He supervises the serving of sentences, custodial conditions, permission to work outside prison, the granting of semi-freedom and release on licence.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence describes administrative functions (supervising sentences, custodial conditions, work permission, semi-freedom, release on licence) without making a substantive claim about liberty as a value—it is an enumeration of a supervisor's duties within the prison system.

records.speaker: John Cope
records.sentence: The amendments do not detract from the union's freedom of choice but simply ensure that, where overseas members can vote, they are treated in the same way as their counterparts in Great Britain.
records.haiku_rationale: The union is being freed to maintain its capacity to choose its own procedures (freedom of choice), and the amendments ensure equal treatment of overseas members without constraining that choice—enabling/protecting the union's power to determine voting rules.

records.speaker: Allan Roberts
records.sentence: Because the people running the housing action trusts are not directly elected by the people being governed, we need this freedom of information and access to information legislation even more than we need it for local authorities.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from interference with access to information about unelected housing action trusts—citizens freed from informational barriers imposed by non-democratic governance.

records.speaker: Anthony Favell
records.sentence: The indiscipline that was then introduced into schools when freedom of expression took away the power of teachers properly to punish, as well as the lack of a proper curriculum, is now leading to the indiscipline of those teenagers.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of expression is negative liberty—freedom from interference with expression—and the speaker treats it as a constraint on teachers' power to punish, implying loss of authority rather than gain of capacity.

records.speaker: Jeremy Corbyn
records.sentence: We should commemorate the retribution meted out to the Catholic people of Ireland as a result of William and Mary coming to the throne by remembering that the only way we can ever bring peace and freedom to all the people of Ireland is by the reunification of Ireland and removal of British troops from it.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence presents freedom as self-determination and empowerment: Irish people are freed to govern themselves through reunification and removal of foreign occupation, not merely freedom from interference with a specific activity.

records.speaker: Robert Jackson
records.sentence: Concern for academic freedom is one of those values which constitute the common ground between the Government and the universities, to which my right hon.
records.haiku_rationale: Academic freedom is freedom from interference with scholarly inquiry and research; it names a zone of non-interference from government control.

records.speaker: John McWilliam
records.sentence: We believe that classification should be determined by the courts, or at least by an independent committee, and that there should be a statutory right of access to official information in all Government Departments on the lines of the American Freedom of Information Act.
records.haiku_rationale: Citizens are being freed from government secrecy and obstruction to access official information held by government departments—a negative liberty protecting access against interference and withholding.

records.speaker: Eric Forth
records.sentence: Gentleman should so criticise a move designed to recognise that those closest in their work to the requirements of industry should be given greater freedom and flexibility to work ever more closely with industry, to the mutual benefit of all.
records.haiku_rationale: Educational/work institutions are being freed to design and manage their own practices and partnerships with industry (capacity/empowerment to act), rather than constrained by regulation.

records.speaker: Seamus Mallon
records.sentence:
In 1941, as it was about to enter a world war and face enormous world pressure, Franklin Roosevelt said:
 In the future days which we seek to make secure we look forward to a world founded on four essential human freedoms.
records.haiku_rationale: Roosevelt's "four essential human freedoms" invokes freedom as a foundational value against tyranny and oppression in wartime—a classic rhetorical appeal to negative liberty (freedom from interference with speech, conscience, want, and fear).

records.speaker: Ronald Renton
records.sentence: What we are debating is not a restriction on the freedom of speech.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of speech is being protected from restriction; this invokes freedom from interference with the ability to speak.

records.speaker: Ivor Stanbrook
records.sentence: That is to dismantle the apparatus of Socialism, to promote freedom in economic affairs, to move to remove the burden of oppressive taxation and to force more individuals to take responsibility for their own lives.
records.haiku_rationale: Individuals are freed from oppressive taxation and paternalistic state control (the "apparatus of Socialism") to become capable of taking responsibility for their own economic lives.

records.speaker: David Owen
records.sentence: She is not the only person to have had this difficulty of striking a balance between freedom and security.
records.haiku_rationale: A bare invocation of "freedom" in tension with "security" without specifying what the freedom is (from interference, or to act) or what particular liberty is at stake; the sentence does not clarify whether the speaker means freedom from state interference or freedom as capability/empowerment.

records.speaker: Bernard Weatherill
records.sentence: The Editor sent me a copy of this letter, but since it was not addressed to me I was not at liberty to read its terms to the House as I was asked to do yesterday.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "not at liberty to" is parliamentary procedure language meaning "not permitted/able to" — the Speaker is describing a procedural constraint on what he could do, not invoking liberty-as-a-value.

records.speaker: Jeremy Hanley
records.sentence: They have, if they want, freedom to act within the law, as we all do.
records.haiku_rationale: They are freed/empowered to act (conduct their affairs) within the legal constraints that bind everyone equally—a capacity granted or preserved by law.

records.speaker: Barry Sheerman
records.sentence: They talk of lifting Government restrictions on liberty.
records.haiku_rationale: Liberty is being freed from government restrictions—a classic negative liberty formulation where freedom consists in the absence of state interference.

records.speaker: Greg Knight
records.sentence: He was a member of the previous Labour Government who, in 1978, published a White Paper — it was debated in July of that year — which did not address the question of freedom of information about which he was so concerned today.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of information (access to government information) is a negative liberty claim—freedom from government interference with the right to access and receive information.

records.speaker: David Evennett
records.sentence: To widen freedom of choice for the individual is an obvious way in which to promote equal opportunities.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of choice (negative liberty: absence of interference in deciding one's own path) is presented as a means to promote equality of opportunity (positive capability).

records.speaker: Michael Foot
records.sentence: If we allow that to go through and do not examine in detail what the consequences may be, I believe that the Bill will be even worse than the Bill that we shall be discussing later on the freedom of information.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from Government restriction on access to information—the Bill concerns constraining or preventing governmental interference with public knowledge and transparency.

records.speaker: George Younger
records.sentence: If we are to fight back against the sovereignty of the Executive, both sides of the House must combine to fight for freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom from executive interference or abuse of executive power—parliamentarians are being freed from executive overreach through combined legislative action.

records.speaker: Tony Worthington
records.sentence: It is an attack not on press freedom but on those few proprietors and editors who abuse their power.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "press freedom" as the object being protected from abuse—freedom of the press from interference by proprietors and editors who wield power irresponsibly.

records.speaker: Patrick Ground
records.sentence: There are sound democratic reasons connected with freedom for that decision.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "freedom" as a democratic value supporting a decision, but does not specify what freedom (from interference or to act) is being claimed or what object it concerns. The reference is too abstract and under-specified to determine whether the underlying liberty claim is negative or positive.

records.speaker: John Patten
records.sentence: There is an argument about proper freedom of movement within the Community, but there is also the equally proper argument about the fact that a sea barrier, a land port or an airport is a good place at which to try to operate against illegal immigrants and terrorists.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "freedom of movement" within the EU—a named freedom from interference with the ability to cross borders—contrasted with security concerns at border checkpoints against illegal immigration and terrorism.

records.speaker: George Younger
records.sentence: Clause 6 is a further attack on the freedom of the word in this country.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "freedom of the word" (or "freedom of the press/speech") refers to freedom from interference with expression and public discourse.

records.speaker: Ann Widdecombe
records.sentence: He talked a great deal about choice and the freedom to choose.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker is being freed to choose among options — this describes empowerment and capacity, not merely freedom from interference.

records.speaker: Gwilym Jones
records.sentence: Why should councils in Wales be frightened of that new freedom?
records.haiku_rationale: Councils are being freed from constraints on their decision-making (the "new freedom" refers to empowerment to act without restrictions previously imposed on them).

records.speaker: Hugh Dykes
records.sentence: Incidentally, the local borough council will shortly be offering the freedom of the borough to the Royal Air Force.
records.haiku_rationale: This is ceremonial language; "freedom of the borough" is a traditional honour/title bestowed on institutions, not a claim about liberty-as-a-value or exemption from constraint.

records.speaker: John Fraser
records.sentence: It is important to ensure access to all legal services and freedom of choice for the consumer.
records.haiku_rationale: The consumer is freed from interference with their capacity to choose among legal services; "freedom of choice" names the absence of constraint on choosing.

records.speaker: David Owen
records.sentence: That is rightly seen by general practitioners as limiting their clinical freedom to choose the type of treatment that they think best for the individual patient, so if the Government insist on it they will be starting to challenge a very fundamental aspect of medical practice.
records.haiku_rationale: Doctors are being freed from—or prevented from having—the ability to choose treatment methods for individual patients; the constraint is on their capacity to make clinical decisions according to their judgment.

records.speaker: Teddy Taylor
records.sentence: We all agree that free trade and the extension of freedom to purchase would be good, but there is not much point in putting extra burdens on industry unless we discover that the system works.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker invokes "freedom to purchase" — a capacity to engage in commerce — which is a positive liberty; the sentence frames this as something that would be "good" if extended, an empowerment rather than removal of constraint.

records.speaker: Robin Cook
records.sentence: That is freedom, but it is the freedom to freeze expenditure on prescriptions and to cut expenditure on other services.
records.haiku_rationale: The government is being freed from constraints (to exercise the capacity) to freeze prescription expenditure and cut other service spending—this is empowerment to act, not protection from interference.

records.speaker: John Patten
records.sentence: I certainly do not mind the curtailment of the liberty of a young man to carry a knife in his pocket and the fact that, should he appear in court, the burden of proving why he was carrying that knife now rests with him and not with the prosecution.
records.haiku_rationale: The freedom being constrained is the liberty to carry a knife without legal restriction; the curtailment refers to removing the freedom FROM interference with knife-carrying, making this a discussion of negative liberty being deliberately restricted in the public interest.

records.speaker: John Patten
records.sentence: For some people, of course, liberty has been curtailed.
records.haiku_rationale: People are being freed (or had their freedom restored) from curtailment/restriction of liberty itself—the discussion is about removal of constraints on liberty.

records.speaker: Margaret Thatcher
records.sentence: We have freedom of capital movement and we have abolished exchange controls.
records.haiku_rationale: Capital is freed from exchange controls—a removal of state interference with the movement of money, a classic negative liberty.

records.speaker: Roger Freeman
records.sentence: They will have delegated freedoms in respect of staff numbers, pay, and capital programmes.
records.haiku_rationale: Schools are being empowered (delegated the capacity) to make autonomous decisions regarding their own staffing, pay, and capital allocations, rather than having these centrally controlled.

records.speaker: John MacGregor
records.sentence: Above all, I underlined that it will be a matter of freedom of choice for the consumer, because there will be full and clear labelling of foods that have received this treatment.
records.haiku_rationale: Consumers are freed from interference with their ability to choose food based on complete information about treatment; the object of freedom is "choice" and what enables it is absence of deceptive or incomplete labelling.

records.speaker: Tony Lloyd
records.sentence: There is no going back on the principle of freedom of movement.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of movement names freedom from interference with one's ability to move—a classic negative liberty.

records.speaker: Eric Heffer
records.sentence: But what happened there was that the man who had some sympathy for freedom was removed from the general secretaryship of the Communist party.
records.haiku_rationale: A man sympathetic to freedom was removed from political office, invoked as a rhetorical claim about liberty being suppressed by authoritarian actors—freedom from tyrannical control is the object.

records.speaker: Unknown
records.sentence: There are good, important measures in both of the Bills to increase democratic accountability and freedom.
records.haiku_rationale: The sentence invokes "freedom" as a general value alongside democratic accountability as a desirable outcome of legislative measures, but does not specify what is being freed, from what, or to what.

records.speaker: Bill Cash
records.sentence: They have sought freedom of choice and they will exercise that freedom of choice in their own way.
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of choice is the ability to exercise autonomous decision-making without interference in one's own decisions and actions.

records.speaker: Giles Radice
records.sentence: People of my generation in eastern Europe have never known freedom or tasted the prosperity that for us is routine.
records.haiku_rationale: Eastern European people are being described as having never experienced freedom (implicitly freedom from communist oppression/authoritarian constraint), which opposes their lack of non-interference and autonomy under totalitarian rule.

records.speaker: Jeremy Ashdown
records.sentence: They have stood against any kind of reform in favour of fair votes, against providing a parliament for Scotland and Wales, against any kind of devolution, against a Bill of Rights, against freedom of information — yet they have the brass neck —
records.haiku_rationale: Freedom of information is freedom from government interference with access to public information; it names a freedom from institutional obstruction.

records.speaker: William Ross
records.sentence: They lost freedom of action, and as a result the Secretary of State for Northern Ireland foolishly said that he found it difficult to envisage the military defeat of the IRA.
records.haiku_rationale: The subject "they" (military/security forces) lost freedom of action — capacity to pursue military operations against the IRA — indicating removal of operational empowerment or capability to act.

records.speaker: Bryan Gould
records.sentence: That is extremely welcome, although it has to be said that the only pricing freedom that local authorities will have will be to fix and pay subsidies in relation to prices set by private contractors.
records.haiku_rationale: The speaker identifies "pricing freedom" for local authorities as the capacity to set subsidies within constraints imposed by private contractors' pricing decisions—a narrow slice of actual control or empowerment to set prices.

records.speaker: Dennis Skinner
records.sentence: They are taking a bit of a liberty when they write stuff like that, but there is an element of truth in it.
records.haiku_rationale: The phrase "taking a bit of a liberty" is parliamentary procedure/idiom meaning overstepping propriety or being presumptuous; it does not substantively address freedom-as-a-value (from or to anything).

records.speaker: William Hague
records.sentence: I know that the Government have recently tried to help in this respect and that there is always a danger when local authorities are given financial freedom that that freedom will be abused by a minority of them.
records.haiku_rationale: Local authorities are empowered with financial autonomy (capacity to raise and manage funding), which is being given to them—this is freedom to govern themselves financially, a positive liberty concern about enabling capacity.

records.speaker: Patrick Nicholls
records.sentence: Yet until the Trade Union Act 1984 the law gave unions freedom to call members out on strike without any such democratic process.

records.speaker: John Major
records.sentence: For when people get the chance to choose once again between a party that has principles and a party that has abandoned them, between a party that delivers freedom and a party that inhibits it, between a party that builds prosperity and one that merely seeks to redistribute it, I believe that they will vote for the consistency, courage and conviction with which my right hon.

records.speaker: The Reverend Ian Paisley
records.sentence: I believe in human rights and in civil and religious liberty for all men.
